about.title: InclineYou exercise library — India edition
about.status: DRAFT — generated for review; nothing here has been checked by a qualified trainer yet
about.approach: Written from scratch, one equipment and one muscle at a time. Not derived from the upstream dataset.
about.howToReview: Read each exercise. Correct anything wrong in place and set review.status to 'approved' with reviewedBy and reviewedAt. Use review.notes for disagreements. Entries marked metadata.reviewNote have a specific question for the reviewer.
about.idRule: id is a kebab-case slug and is permanent. When loaded, exercise.source_id = 'inclineyou-' + id, origin = 'inclineyou'.
about.columns: name, bodyPart, target (muscle_group = target), secondaryTargets, equipment, movementPattern, level, logType map to the exercise table; steps are stored joined by blank lines in description; formCues map to form_cues; metadata is a column. aliases (English alternate names) are not a column yet and are not loaded. Indian-language aliases are deliberately left out for now.
about.text: Text only: no images or video.
about.parked: Entries in 'parked' were cut on my recommendation while no professional was available. They are complete and can be moved back into 'exercises' if the reviewer disagrees.
about.decisions: Open review questions were resolved by recommendation: keep the behind-the-neck press and upright row with strong warnings, keep decline bench, keep the barbell pullover under chest and the Yates row under upper back, keep box squat and reverse lunge under quads, keep deadlift under glutes. Revisit with a professional.
about.logTypes: weight_reps = load + reps; reps = bodyweight + reps; time = bodyweight + seconds; distance = bodyweight + metres; weight_time = load + seconds; weight_distance = load + metres. Matches the proposed schema's exercise.log_type CHECK and set_log's load_kind/effort_kind.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar, feet flat on the floor, and your glutes and upper back in contact with the bench.
Pull your shoulder blades together and down and keep a small natural arch in your lower back.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with your wrists stacked over your elbows. Unrack it and hold it over your shoulders with straight arms.
Breathe in and lower the bar under control to your mid-chest, with your elbows about 45–60° away from your body.
Stop just above or lightly touching the chest. Do not bounce the bar.
Press the bar up and slightly back to the start, pushing your feet into the floor, and breathe out as you press.
Re-rack the bar only when the set is finished.
formCues: Shoulder blades pinned back and down
Elbows about 45–60°, not flared out to the sides
Bar over mid-chest, wrists over elbows
Feet planted, drive through the floor

commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
Wrists bent back behind the bar
Letting one side of the bar rise faster than the other
safety: Use a spotter or set the rack safety arms for any heavy set
Always wrap the thumb around the bar
Use collars so plates cannot slide

exercises.name: Barbell incline bench press
steps: Set the bench to 30–45°. Sit back with your feet flat and your head, upper back and glutes on the pad.
Pull your shoulder blades together and down. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack it over your shoulders.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your upper chest, just below the collarbone, with your elbows about 45–60° from your body.
Pause briefly without bouncing, then press the bar up to straight arms over your shoulders.
Re-rack the bar only when the set is finished.
formCues: Bench at 30–45° — steeper turns it into a shoulder press
Bar travels to the upper chest
Press straight up over the shoulders

commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the collarbone
Lifting the hips off the pad
Lowering the bar to the neck
safety: Use a spotter or rack safeties on heavy sets
Wrap the thumb around the bar
Keep the bar path over the shoulders, never over the face

exercises.name: Barbell low incline bench press
steps: Set the bench to a slight incline of about 15–30°. Lie back with your feet flat and your upper back and glutes on the pad.
Pull your shoulder blades together and down, grip the bar slightly wider than shoulders and unrack it over your shoulders.
Lower the bar to the upper-middle chest with your elbows about 45–60° from your body.
Press the bar back up to straight arms, keeping your shoulder blades pinned.
Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Bar lands on the upper-middle chest

commonMistakes: Using the same angle as a full incline
safety: Use a spotter or rack safeties on heavy sets
Wrap the thumb around the bar
metadata.reviewNote: Popular for upper-chest work with less shoulder stress than a full incline; confirm the angle range with the reviewer.

exercises.name: Barbell decline bench press
steps: Set the bench to a decline of about 15–30° and hook your feet securely under the pads.
Lie back, pull your shoulder blades together and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Unrack the bar with a spotter's help and hold it over your lower chest with straight arms.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest with your elbows about 45–60° from your body.
Press the bar back up to straight arms. Re-rack it only when the set is finished.
formCues: Feet locked in before you unrack
Bar lands on the lower chest

commonMistakes: Rushing the unrack without a spotter
safety: Always train with a spotter on this lift
Check the feet are fixed before unracking
Avoid it if you get dizzy or have high blood pressure
metadata.reviewNote: Check whether Indian gyms commonly have a working decline bench; if not, consider dropping this.

exercises.name: Barbell wide-grip bench press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar, feet flat and shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Take a grip about 1.5 times shoulder width, so your forearms are close to vertical at the bottom.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your mid-chest. The range will be shorter than with a standard grip.
Press the bar back up to straight arms. Re-rack it when the set is finished.
formCues: Forearms close to vertical at the bottom

commonMistakes: Going wider than 1.5 times shoulder width
safety: Use a spotter or rack safeties on heavy sets
Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder

exercises.name: Barbell paused bench press
steps: Set up as for a normal flat bench press: eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest and hold it still on the chest for 1–2 seconds. Stay tight; do not relax.
Press the bar up explosively to straight arms.
Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Full stop on the chest, stay tight
Count the pause: one second, two
Drive up as fast as you can

commonMistakes: Relaxing or sinking into the chest during the pause
Cutting the pause short as the set gets hard
safety: Use a spotter or rack safeties — paused reps are slower and harder
Use a lighter load than your normal bench

exercises.name: Barbell floor press
steps: Lie on the floor inside a rack with the bar set at a height you can unrack, knees bent and feet flat.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack it over your chest with straight arms.
Lower the bar until your upper arms rest on the floor. Pause for a moment without relaxing.
Press the bar back up to straight arms. Re-rack it when the set is finished.
formCues: Upper arms stop on the floor
Keep your upper back tight to the floor

commonMistakes: Dropping the arms onto the floor and bouncing
Arching the lower back off the floor
safety: Set the rack so you can unrack and re-rack without reaching
Use rack safeties for heavy loads
metadata.reviewNote: Useful where a bench is busy or a client has shoulder pain; the floor limits the range.

exercises.name: Barbell reverse-grip bench press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat. Pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Grip the bar with palms facing you, hands about shoulder width apart.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your lower-to-mid chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
Press the bar back up to straight arms. Re-rack it when the set is finished.

commonMistakes: Using too much load too soon, which strains the wrists
safety: Use a spotter every set
Start light — this grip stresses the wrists and biceps tendons
Skip it with wrist or elbow pain

exercises.name: Barbell pullover
steps: Lie back on a flat bench with your head near the end and your feet flat on the floor. Hold a light bar over your chest with straight arms and a shoulder-width grip.
Keeping your arms nearly straight with a slight elbow bend, lower the bar in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch across your chest and lats.
Pull the bar back over your chest along the same arc, squeezing your chest.
Hold the bar steady and breathe out as it returns over your chest.
formCues: Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows
Move at the shoulder, not the elbows

commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows like a triceps extension
Arching the back hard to get more range
safety: Use a light load and a spotter on your first sets
Stop if the shoulder pinches at the bottom
metadata.reviewNote: Some coaches file this under lats rather than chest; decide with the reviewer where it should live.

exercises.name: Barbell Spoto press
steps: Set up as for a flat bench press: eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Unrack the bar and lower it under control until it is about 1–2 inches (2–5 cm) above your chest.
Hold the bar still in that spot for about a second without touching the chest.
Press the bar up to straight arms. Re-rack it when the set is finished.
formCues: Stop an inch or two above the chest

commonMistakes: Touching the chest instead of stopping above it
safety: Use a spotter or rack safeties every set
Use a lighter load than your usual bench
metadata.reviewNote: A powerlifting accessory — confirm it is worth carrying for general-population trainers.

exercises.name: Barbell bent-over row
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet. Bend your knees slightly, hinge at the hips and grip the bar just outside your knees with an overhand grip.
Lift the bar so it hangs at arm's length. Set your torso at about 45° to the floor with your back flat, core braced and neck in line with your spine.
Pull the bar towards your lower ribs by driving your elbows back past your torso and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then lower the bar under control to straight arms without letting your back round.
Keep the same torso angle on every rep. Set the bar down on the floor or rack when the set is finished.
formCues: Hinge at the hips with a flat back
Drive the elbows back towards the hips
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top
Hold the same torso angle every rep

commonMistakes: Using momentum by jerking the torso upright
Standing too upright so the bar is just shrugged
Pulling to the chest instead of the lower ribs
Craning the neck up to look in the mirror
safety: Keep your back flat under load — stop the set when it starts to round
Choose a load you can pull without throwing your body
Lift the bar from the floor or rack with a hip hinge, not a rounded back

exercises.name: Barbell wide-grip bent-over row
steps: Set up as for a bent-over row: bar over the middle of your feet, hinge at the hips with a flat back and knees slightly bent.
Take an overhand grip about 1.5 times shoulder width and lift the bar to arm's length, torso at about 45°.
Pull the bar towards your upper abdomen and lower chest, letting your elbows travel out at about 60–75° from your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower the bar under control to straight arms.
Set the bar down when the set is finished.
formCues: Elbows travel out to the sides
Bar to the upper abdomen and lower chest
Shoulder blades squeeze together at the top

commonMistakes: Gripping so wide the range becomes tiny
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
safety: Keep the load moderate — the wide grip loads the rear shoulder
Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder

exercises.name: Barbell Pendlay row
steps: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet. Hinge at the hips until your back is flat and your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip just wider than shoulder width, arms straight, back flat, core braced.
Pull the bar explosively from the floor to your lower chest or upper abdomen, keeping your torso still.
Lower the bar under control until it rests fully on the floor, and reset your back before the next rep.
Every rep starts from a dead stop on the floor.
formCues: Bar returns to the floor every rep

commonMistakes: Letting the torso rise as the weight gets heavy
Bouncing the bar off the floor
Rounding the back at the start
safety: Use bumper or standard plates so the bar sits at the right height
Keep the back flat at the start of every rep
Use a lighter load than your normal bent-over row
metadata.reviewNote: Needs a floor bar height that suits the lifter; check that 20 kg / 25 kg plates are the norm in Indian gyms.

exercises.name: Barbell Yates row
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet. Grip the bar with an underhand or half-underhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart.
Hinge at the hips and lift the bar to arm's length. Set your torso fairly upright, about 30–45° from vertical, with your back flat and core braced.
Pull the bar into your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back and close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a moment, then lower the bar under control.
Set the bar down when the set is finished.
formCues: Torso more upright than a normal row
Elbows stay close to the body

commonMistakes: Leaning back and swinging the bar
Letting the elbows flare out wide
safety: Keep your back flat under load
Keep the weight moderate — the upright torso invites cheating
metadata.reviewNote: Yates rows are often filed under lats. Decide with the reviewer whether this one belongs under upper back or lats.

exercises.name: Barbell T-bar row
steps: Anchor one end of an empty barbell in a landmine attachment or a corner, and load plates on the free end. Straddle the bar and attach a V-handle or grip just behind the plates.
Bend your knees slightly, hinge at the hips with a flat back and lift the bar so your arms hang straight, torso at about 45°.
Pull the handle towards your chest or lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the bar under control to straight arms without rounding your back.
Set the bar down on the floor when the set is finished.
formCues: Chest up, back flat, hips back
Pull the elbows past the body
Do not bounce the plates off the floor

commonMistakes: Using the legs to heave the bar up
Dropping the plates to the floor between reps
safety: Make sure the barbell is firmly anchored before you load it
Use collars or a plate-loaded sleeve that cannot slide
Keep your back flat under load
metadata.reviewNote: This is the barbell/landmine version. The T-bar row machine will live in the leverage-machine batch.

exercises.name: Barbell Meadows row
steps: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or a corner and load plates on the free end. Stand side-on to the bar with a staggered stance.
Hinge forward, rest your free hand on your front thigh or a support, and grip the thick end of the bar with an overhand grip.
Pull your elbow up and back towards your hip, keeping your torso still and your shoulder blade moving.
Pause at the top, then lower the bar under control until your arm is straight.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch sides.
formCues: Pull the elbow to the hip
Let the shoulder blade glide back and forth

commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to heave the weight up
safety: Make sure the bar is firmly anchored
Keep your back flat and brace your core
Use collars

exercises.name: Barbell reverse-grip bent-over row
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet. Bend your knees slightly, hinge at the hips and grip the bar with palms facing forward-up (underhand), hands about shoulder width apart.
Lift the bar to arm's length and set your torso at about 45° to the floor, back flat, core braced and neck in line with your spine.
Pull the bar into your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back and keeping them close to your body, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment, then lower the bar under control to straight arms without rounding your back.
Set the bar down on the floor or rack when the set is finished.
formCues: Elbows stay close and drive to the hips
Bar finishes at the lower abdomen

commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to move the bar
Pulling to the chest instead of the lower abdomen
safety: Keep your back flat under load
Start lighter than your overhand row — the underhand grip loads the biceps more
Stop if you feel pain at the front of the elbow

exercises.name: Barbell standing overhead press
steps: Set the bar at upper-chest height in a rack. Grip it just outside shoulder width with an overhand grip and your elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Unrack the bar and step back. Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, glutes and abs braced, and the bar resting on your front shoulders and upper chest.
Breathe in, tuck your chin back slightly and press the bar straight up, moving your head forward under the bar as it passes your forehead.
Lock out with the bar over the middle of your feet, your arms straight and your shoulders shrugged up slightly.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest, then repeat. Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes and brace the abs
Bar path straight, over mid-foot at lockout
Head moves through under the bar
Ribs down, do not lean back

commonMistakes: Leaning back and turning it into an incline press
Flaring the elbows far behind the bar
Flexing the lower back to cheat the rep
safety: Use rack safeties or step the bar back to the rack, never drop it forward
Keep the load such that your lower back does not arch
Skip it if you have shoulder impingement pain overhead

exercises.name: Barbell seated overhead press
steps: Set an upright bench to 90° (or use a seat with a back pad) inside a rack, and set the bar at about shoulder height.
Sit with your back and glutes against the pad and feet flat on the floor. Grip the bar just outside shoulder width.
Unrack the bar and hold it at your upper chest with your elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Press the bar straight up to lockout over your head, then lower it under control to your upper chest.
Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Elbows under the bar at the bottom

commonMistakes: Arching the back off the pad
Bouncing the bar off the chest
Pressing the bar in front of the face
safety: Use rack safeties
Do not use a bench that wobbles
Skip it if you have shoulder impingement pain overhead

exercises.name: Barbell push press
steps: Set the bar at upper-chest height in a rack. Grip it just outside shoulder width and unrack it so it rests on your front shoulders. Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and hips slightly, about a quarter squat, keeping your torso upright and your heels down.
Drive hard through your legs and hips to explode upwards, and use that momentum to press the bar overhead to lockout.
Lock out with the bar over your mid-foot. Lower it under control to your shoulders, absorbing it with your knees, and reset before the next rep.
formCues: Drive the legs first, then press

commonMistakes: Dipping too deep like a squat
Pressing before the legs finish driving
Dropping the bar onto the chest
safety: Use rack safeties
Keep your torso upright to protect your lower back
Learn the strict press first

exercises.name: Barbell behind-the-neck press
steps: Set an upright bench inside a rack and set the bar at about head height behind you. Sit with your back against the pad.
Grip the bar with a wide overhand grip, about 1.5 times shoulder width, and unrack it behind your neck. Rest it lightly on your upper back, at the base of your neck.
Press the bar straight up until your arms are fully extended, keeping your head neutral.
Lower the bar under control only to ear level — no lower than your ears — and press again.
Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Chin neutral, do not push the head forward

commonMistakes: Lowering the bar all the way to the neck
Pushing the head forward to get the bar past
safety: Skip this lift if you lack good shoulder mobility
Use a very light load and rack safeties
Do not do it if you have any shoulder pain or impingement history
metadata.reviewNote: Common in Indian gyms but widely considered high-risk for the shoulder. The reviewer should decide whether to include it at all, or keep it as a clearly warned expert lift.

exercises.name: Barbell landmine press
steps: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or a corner and load plates on the free end. Stand facing the bar in a split stance or with feet shoulder-width apart.
Lift the free end to your shoulder with one hand, palm facing in, and brace your core.
Press the bar up and forward along its natural arc until your arm is straight, and your shoulder blade slides forward.
Lower the bar under control to your shoulder. Complete all reps on one side, then switch sides.
formCues: Brace the core, do not lean back
Press up and forward along the arc

commonMistakes: Leaning back to push the bar
safety: Make sure the bar is firmly anchored before loading it
Use collars
metadata.reviewNote: Often used instead of an overhead press for clients with limited overhead mobility; the target could be argued as delts or pectorals.

exercises.name: Barbell upright row
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart or slightly wider.
Keeping the bar close to your body, lift it by driving your elbows up and out, leading with your elbows.
Stop when your elbows reach about shoulder height and the bar is near your lower chest.
Lower the bar under control to the start.
formCues: Stop at shoulder height or lower
Keep the bar close to the body

commonMistakes: Pulling the bar up to the chin with the elbows well above the shoulders
Swinging the body to heave it up
safety: Keep the bar below chest height to avoid shoulder pinching
Use a wider grip and lighter load
Skip it if you have shoulder pain
metadata.reviewNote: Often flagged for shoulder impingement. Reviewer to decide whether to keep it, and the safe range to recommend.

exercises.name: Barbell front raise
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a light barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the bar straight in front of you to about shoulder height.
Hold it briefly at the top, then lower it slowly to the start.
Keep your core braced and avoid leaning back.
formCues: Keep a slight bend in the elbows

commonMistakes: Swinging the body to lift the bar
Raising the bar above shoulder height
Using a load that is too heavy
safety: Use a light bar or an EZ bar
Do not lean back to lift

exercises.name: Barbell back squat
steps: Set the bar in a rack at about upper-chest height. Step under it and rest it across your upper back, on the muscle just below your neck, not on the neck itself. Grip the bar just wider than shoulder width.
Brace your core, unrack the bar and step back. Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and toes turned out slightly.
Breathe in and sit down and back, bending your knees and hips together, keeping your chest up and your knees tracking over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as low as you can with a flat back and heels down.
Drive up through your whole foot, keeping your chest up, and breathe out as you pass the hardest point.
Re-rack the bar only when the set is finished.
formCues: Brace the core before every rep
Sit between the hips, drive up through mid-foot

commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Hips shooting up before the chest
Dropping the chest and turning it into a good morning
safety: Set the rack safety arms just below your lowest depth
Use a spotter for heavy sets
Learn the movement with a goblet squat first
Use collars

exercises.name: Barbell front squat
steps: Set the bar in a rack at about shoulder height. Step up to it and rest it across the front of your shoulders, close to your throat, with your elbows pointing forward.
Hold it with a clean grip (fingers under the bar) or cross your arms in front of you. Keep your elbows high.
Unrack the bar, step back and stand with your feet about shoulder width apart.
Bend your knees and hips and sit straight down, keeping your torso very upright and your elbows high.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive up through your whole foot, keeping your elbows up.
Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Drive up with the chest and elbows

commonMistakes: Letting the elbows drop so the bar rolls forward
safety: Use rack safeties
Be ready to drop the bar forward if you fail — never try to bail backward
Use a lighter load than your back squat
Practise the rack position with an empty bar first
metadata.reviewNote: Needs wrist and shoulder mobility for the rack position; the reviewer may want a note on straps or a cross-arm grip for those who lack it.

exercises.name: Barbell pause squat
steps: Set up as for a back squat: bar across your upper back, feet shoulder width apart, core braced.
Sit down and back under control until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Hold the bottom position for 2–3 seconds, keeping your chest up and your core tight. Do not relax or bounce.
Drive up through your whole foot to standing. Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Drive up from a dead stop

commonMistakes: Rounding the back during the pause
safety: Use rack safeties
Use a lighter load than your normal back squat

exercises.name: Barbell box squat
steps: Set a box or bench behind you so that sitting on it puts your thighs about parallel to the floor. Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat.
Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width, unrack the bar and step back so the box is just behind you.
Sit back and down with your hips going first, keeping your shins vertical, until you touch the box.
Pause briefly on the box without relaxing or rocking, keeping your core tight.
Drive up through your feet to standing. Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Touch the box and stay tight
Do not rock or crash onto the box
Drive up from the heels and mid-foot

commonMistakes: Relaxing the core on the box
Using a box that is too low
safety: Use rack safeties
Use a box height that lets you keep a flat back
metadata.reviewNote: A common teaching tool for depth. Target could be argued as glutes.

exercises.name: Barbell Zercher squat
steps: Set the bar in a rack at about hip or low-waist height. Step up to it and hook it in the crook of your elbows, with your forearms crossed or hands clasped in front of you.
Stand up to unrack the bar and step back. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and the bar resting against your upper stomach.
Sit down and back, keeping your torso upright and your elbows close to your thighs.
Lower until your elbows are about at your thighs, then drive back up. Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Brace the abs against the bar

commonMistakes: Using a heavy load that the elbows cannot tolerate
safety: Pad the bar — the elbow crook is sensitive
Use rack safeties
Start with a light load
metadata.reviewNote: Strong-man style lift. Reviewer to decide if this belongs in the library.

exercises.name: Barbell split squat
steps: Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat, unrack it and step back.
Take a long stride so one foot is well in front of the other and stand with your feet hip-width apart in a split stance, your back heel lifted.
Bend both knees and lower your back knee towards the floor, keeping your torso upright and your front shin close to vertical.
Press up through your front foot to the start. Finish all reps on one side, then switch sides.
formCues: Front shin near vertical, front heel down
Drive up through the front foot

commonMistakes: Stance too short or too long
safety: Use rack safeties
Start with an empty bar
Practise the split stance without weight first

exercises.name: Barbell Bulgarian split squat
steps: Stand about two feet in front of a bench. Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat.
Place the top of one foot on the bench behind you. Stand tall with your front foot far enough forward that your front shin can stay vertical.
Bend your front knee and lower your hips straight down until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Press up through your front foot to the start. Finish all reps on one side, then switch sides.
formCues: Drive up through the front heel

commonMistakes: Standing too close to the bench
safety: Use a stable bench
Use rack safeties
Start with bodyweight, then dumbbells, before using a barbell
metadata.reviewNote: Barbell loading is awkward for most lifters; dumbbells are the usual choice. Reviewer to decide whether to keep the barbell version.

exercises.name: Barbell reverse lunge
steps: Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat, unrack it and step back. Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step backward with one foot, landing on the ball of your foot, and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee over your ankle.
Drive through your front foot to stand and bring your back foot forward. Alternate legs.

commonMistakes: Front knee drifting forward over the toes
Losing balance with a heavy load
safety: Use rack safeties
Start with an empty bar
Do it in a rack or with space behind you
metadata.reviewNote: The target could be argued as glutes.

exercises.name: Barbell walking lunge
steps: Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat, unrack it and step back. Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart in a clear space.
Step forward with one foot into a long stride and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°, your back knee just above the floor.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your ankle.
Push through your front foot, bringing your back foot forward to the next stride. Alternate legs.

commonMistakes: Losing balance with a heavy load
safety: Start with an empty bar
Make sure there is a clear walking path
Use collars

exercises.name: Barbell step-up
steps: Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat. Stand facing a stable box or bench with a height around knee level.
Place one foot fully on the box and press through that heel to step up, bringing your other foot beside it.
Stand tall on the box, then step back down with control, leading with the same leg.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch sides.
formCues: Drive through the heel of the top foot
Do not push off the bottom foot

commonMistakes: Using a box that is too high
safety: Use a stable box
Use a height that keeps your knee at or below 90°
Start with an empty bar

exercises.name: Barbell hip thrust
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the long edge of a stable bench, about at the bottom of your shoulder blades. Roll a padded barbell over your legs so it sits across your hip crease.
Plant your feet flat about hip width apart, with your knees bent so your shins are vertical at the top.
Brace your core, tuck your chin slightly and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, ribs down, without arching your lower back.
Lower your hips under control until the plates almost touch the floor, then repeat.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes, do not arch the back

commonMistakes: Overarching the lower back at the top
Feet too close or too far from the hips
Letting the bar roll onto the stomach
safety: Use a thick pad or mat on the bar to protect the hips
Use a bench that cannot slide — brace it against a wall
Use collars

exercises.name: Barbell glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat, hip width apart. Roll a padded barbell over your legs so it sits across your hip crease and hold it in place with both hands.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without arching your lower back.
Lower your hips under control to the floor and repeat.
formCues: Heels close enough that the shins are vertical at the top
Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Use a thick pad on the bar
Use a smaller range than a bench hip thrust
metadata.reviewNote: Shorter range than the hip thrust; useful where no bench is free.

exercises.name: Barbell single-leg hip thrust
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a stable bench and a padded barbell across your hip crease. Plant one foot flat and extend the other leg or hold the knee towards your chest.
Brace your core and drive through the heel of your planted foot to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glute at the top, keeping your hips level and your ribs down.
Lower your hips under control and repeat. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

commonMistakes: Letting the hips rotate or drop on one side
safety: Use a light bar or just a pad before adding weight
Brace the bench against a wall

exercises.name: Barbell deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet. Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the bar just outside your legs.
Keep your chest up, your back flat and your shoulders slightly in front of the bar. Pull the slack out of the bar and brace your core.
Drive through your whole foot as if pushing the floor away, keeping the bar close to your legs, and stand up by extending your hips and knees together.
Finish standing tall with your glutes squeezed, without leaning back.
Lower the bar under control by hinging your hips back first, then bending your knees once it passes them, keeping it close to your legs.
formCues: Bar over mid-foot, close to the shins
Squeeze the glutes at the top

commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the legs
Jerking the bar off the floor
Hips shooting up before the chest
safety: Do not lift with a rounded back
Learn the hinge with a kettlebell or light bar first
Use collars
Do not drop the bar from the top

exercises.name: Barbell sumo deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet wide, about twice shoulder width, with your toes pointing out at about 30–45°, and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the bar between your legs, hands about shoulder width apart.
Keep your chest up and your back flat, pull the slack out of the bar and brace your core.
Drive your knees out over your toes and push the floor apart as you stand up, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Finish standing tall with your glutes squeezed. Lower the bar under control the same way.
formCues: Knees push out over the toes
Bar stays close to the body

commonMistakes: Hips too low so it becomes a squat
Jerking the bar off the floor
safety: Do not lift with a rounded back
Warm up the hips and adductors first
Use collars

exercises.name: Barbell low-bar back squat
steps: Set the bar at about upper-chest height in a rack. Step under it and rest it across your rear shoulders, on the upper back muscles below the bony part of the neck, with your elbows pointing back.
Grip the bar with a wide hold, unrack it and step back. Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width, toes turned out.
Sit your hips back and down, leaning your torso forward a little, until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes, then drive up through your whole foot, hips and chest rising together.
Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Bar on the shelf of the rear shoulders

safety: Use rack safeties
Use a spotter for heavy sets
Wrist and shoulder mobility is needed for the grip — do not force it
metadata.reviewNote: A powerlifting squat variation. Reviewer to decide whether general trainers need it as well as the high-bar back squat.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
steps: Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, hands just outside your legs, feet hip width apart and knees slightly bent.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and your back flat, and push your hips straight back as the bar slides down your thighs.
Lower the bar to about mid-shin, or until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, keeping the bar close to your legs and your knees only slightly bent.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes at the top without leaning back.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

commonMistakes: Bending the knees too much so it becomes a squat
Letting the bar drift away from the legs
safety: Stop lowering when your back starts to round
Use a load you can control
Use collars

exercises.name: Barbell stiff-leg deadlift
steps: Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, feet hip width apart and your legs almost straight.
Keep your back flat and your chest up, and hinge forward at the hips, lowering the bar along your legs.
Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings, usually around mid-shin.
Return to standing by driving your hips forward, squeezing your glutes at the top.
formCues: Stop at the end of the hamstring stretch

commonMistakes: Dropping the bar too far with a rounded back
safety: Use a lighter load than your Romanian deadlift
Stop at the point your back starts to round
Do not do it with lower back pain
metadata.reviewNote: Very close to the Romanian deadlift. The reviewer may prefer to keep only one.

exercises.name: Barbell good morning
steps: Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat, unrack it and step back. Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and push your hips straight back, letting your torso lean forward.
Lower until your torso is about parallel to the floor, or until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
formCues: Hips go back, chest stays proud

commonMistakes: Looking up and straining the neck
safety: Start with an empty bar
Use rack safeties
Stop if your lower back rounds or hurts

exercises.name: Barbell single-leg Romanian deadlift
steps: Hold a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip and stand on one foot with a slight bend in your knee. Rest your other foot lightly behind you.
Brace your core and hinge forward at the hip, sliding the bar down your standing leg while your free leg extends straight back behind you.
Lower until your torso is about parallel to the floor, keeping your hips square to the floor.
Drive through your standing heel to stand tall again. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Free leg and torso move as one lever
Slight bend in the standing knee

commonMistakes: Losing balance with a heavy bar
safety: Start with a light bar or no weight
Stand near a rack or wall for balance

exercises.name: Barbell sumo squat
steps: Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat, unrack it and step back. Stand with your feet about twice shoulder width apart and your toes turned out about 30–45°.
Brace your core and bend your knees and hips, sitting straight down between your feet and pushing your knees out over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and your back flat.
Drive up through your whole foot, pushing your knees out, to stand.
formCues: Knees push out over the toes

safety: Use rack safeties
Warm up the hips and adductors first

exercises.name: Barbell lateral lunge
steps: Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat, unrack it and step back. Stand tall with your feet together.
Step out wide to one side and sit your hips back and down over that leg, keeping the other leg straight and both feet flat and pointing forward.
Lower until your thigh is about parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up.
Push through the bent leg to return to standing. Alternate sides.

commonMistakes: Lifting the heel of the bent leg
safety: Start with an empty bar
Use rack safeties or a clear space
Stop if you feel pain in the groin
metadata.reviewNote: Barbell is awkward for this; a dumbbell or bodyweight version is more common. Reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Barbell standing calf raise
steps: Set the bar on your upper back as for a back squat, unrack it and step back. Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised block or step, heels hanging off.
Stand tall with your knees almost straight and your core braced.
Lower your heels as far as comfortable for a deep stretch in your calves.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can, squeeze your calves at the top, and lower slowly.

commonMistakes: Bending the knees to heave the weight
safety: Use rack safeties
Use a stable step
Start with an empty bar

exercises.name: Barbell seated calf raise
steps: Sit on a bench with the balls of your feet on a raised block or plate, heels hanging off, knees bent at about 90°.
Rest a padded barbell across your thighs just above your knees, holding it in place with both hands.
Lower your heels as far as comfortable for a deep stretch.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can, squeeze your calves at the top, and lower slowly.
formCues: Pause and squeeze at the top

commonMistakes: Letting the bar roll off the knees
safety: Use a thick pad on the bar
Hold the bar firmly in place

exercises.name: Barbell curl
steps: Stand tall holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart, arms hanging straight, elbows close to your sides.
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides and your upper arms still, curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top without letting your elbows drift forward.
Lower the bar slowly to full arm extension.

safety: Use a weight you can curl without swinging
Keep your core braced

exercises.name: Barbell wide-grip curl
steps: Stand tall holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands wider than shoulder width, arms hanging straight.
Keep your elbows by your sides and curl the bar towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.

safety: Use a moderate weight
Stop if your wrists hurt

exercises.name: Barbell close-grip curl
steps: Stand tall holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands about 6–8 inches (15–20 cm) apart, arms hanging straight.
Keep your elbows by your sides and curl the bar towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.

safety: Use a moderate weight

exercises.name: Barbell drag curl
steps: Stand tall holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder width apart, the bar against your thighs.
Curl the bar up by pulling your elbows back, dragging the bar up along your body.
Stop when the bar reaches your lower chest, squeezing your biceps.
Lower the bar slowly, still close to your body.
formCues: Bar stays in contact with the body

commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the body
safety: Use a lighter weight than a standard curl

exercises.name: Barbell preacher curl
steps: Adjust a preacher bench so your armpits rest on the top of the pad. Sit down and grip a barbell with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart.
Start with your arms nearly straight, resting on the pad.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms on the pad.
Squeeze at the top, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are almost straight.
formCues: Upper arms stay on the pad
Stop just short of locking out

commonMistakes: Lifting the shoulders off the pad
Dropping the bar fast and locking the elbows
safety: Do not fully lock the elbows at the bottom
Use a light weight to protect the biceps tendon

exercises.name: Barbell spider curl
steps: Set an incline bench to about 45° and lie face down on it, with your chest against the pad and your arms hanging straight down.
Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart.
Keeping your upper arms still, curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.

safety: Use a light weight
Use a stable bench

exercises.name: Barbell close-grip bench press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat. Pull your shoulder blades together and down.
Grip the bar with your hands about shoulder width apart, slightly narrower than a normal bench press grip.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Press the bar back up to straight arms, keeping your elbows tucked. Re-rack the bar when the set is finished.

commonMistakes: Gripping too narrow, which hurts the wrists
safety: Use a spotter or rack safeties
Do not use a very narrow grip
Wrap the thumb around the bar

exercises.name: Barbell lying triceps extension
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell above your chest with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart, arms straight.
Keeping your upper arms still, bend your elbows to lower the bar towards your forehead or just behind your head.
Stop when your forearms are about parallel to the floor or you feel a stretch in your triceps.
Extend your elbows to return the bar to the start, squeezing your triceps.

commonMistakes: Letting the upper arms drift back
Lowering the bar to the face
safety: Use a spotter on heavy sets
Use a lighter load and control the bar
Stop if your elbows hurt

exercises.name: Barbell seated overhead triceps extension
steps: Sit on an upright bench with back support and hold a light barbell overhead with an overhand grip, hands about 6–8 inches (15–20 cm) apart, arms straight.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head, and lower the bar behind your head by bending your elbows.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your triceps.
Extend your elbows to press the bar back up to straight arms.

safety: Use a light weight
Start with an EZ bar if the straight bar hurts your wrists

exercises.name: Barbell JM press
steps: Lie on a flat bench and unrack a barbell with a grip slightly narrower than shoulder width, holding it over your chest with your arms straight.
Lower the bar by bending your elbows, letting it move towards your chin or upper chest while your elbows travel forward.
Stop when your forearms are close to vertical and your elbows are bent about 90°.
Press the bar back up by extending your elbows.
formCues: Forearms near vertical at the bottom

safety: Use a spotter every set
Start with an empty bar
metadata.reviewNote: A powerlifting triceps exercise; probably more than most trainers need.

exercises.name: Barbell wrist curl
steps: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms up, holding a barbell with an underhand grip and your wrists hanging off your knees.
Let the bar roll down to your fingertips, then curl it back up by flexing your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a light weight
Stop if your wrists hurt

exercises.name: Barbell reverse wrist curl
steps: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms down, holding a barbell with an overhand grip and your wrists hanging off your knees.
Lower the bar by letting your wrists bend down, then lift it by extending your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a light weight
Stop if your wrists hurt

exercises.name: Barbell reverse curl
steps: Stand tall holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart, arms hanging straight.
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full arm extension.

safety: Use a lighter load than your normal curl
metadata.reviewNote: Works forearms and the brachialis; the target could be argued as biceps.

exercises.name: Barbell behind-the-back wrist curl
steps: Stand holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart, arms straight.
Let the bar roll down to your fingertips, then curl it up by flexing your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a light weight

exercises.name: Barbell shrug
steps: Stand tall holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder width, arms straight.
Keeping your arms straight, lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Pause and squeeze at the top, then lower your shoulders slowly.

safety: Use straps for heavy loads so grip is not the limit
Keep your neck neutral

exercises.name: Barbell behind-the-back shrug
steps: Stand tall holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip, hands shoulder width apart, arms straight.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a moderate weight
Keep your neck neutral

exercises.name: Barbell high pull
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with a wide overhand grip.
Bend your knees slightly and push your hips back, lowering the bar to just above your knees.
Explode up through your legs and hips, shrugging your shoulders and pulling the bar up along your body, elbows leading high and outside.
Pull until the bar reaches about chest height, then lower it under control.
formCues: Legs and hips power the bar

safety: Use a light weight and learn the movement with an empty bar
Keep your back flat
metadata.reviewNote: An Olympic-lifting derivative; reviewer to decide whether it belongs.

exercises.name: Barbell rack pull
steps: Set the bar on rack pins or blocks at about knee height. Stand with your feet hip width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Hinge at the hips and grip the bar just outside your legs, chest up and back flat. Pull the slack out and brace your core.
Drive through your feet and extend your hips to stand tall, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Lock out with your shoulders back, then lower the bar under control to the pins.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Do not lift with a rounded back
Use safeties and collars
Use a load you can control

exercises.name: Barbell seated good morning
steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat and a light barbell across your upper back. Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Lean forward from your hips, keeping your back flat, until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your lower back and glutes to return to upright.

safety: Use a very light weight
Stop if your lower back hurts
metadata.reviewNote: Niche; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Barbell rollout
steps: Load a barbell with round plates (about 10 kg or 25 lb each side) and kneel on a mat with your hands on the bar, shoulder width apart.
Brace your core and tuck your hips slightly, then roll the bar forward slowly, extending your body as far as you can without letting your lower back sag.
Pause at the furthest point you can control, then pull the bar back using your abs.
formCues: Roll only as far as you can control

commonMistakes: Using the hips to pull back
safety: Start with a short range
Use round plates so the bar rolls smoothly
Stop if your lower back hurts
metadata.reviewNote: An ab wheel is far more common; reviewer to decide whether to keep the barbell version.

exercises.name: Barbell landmine twist
steps: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or a corner and load plates on the free end. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, holding the free end with both hands at chest height, arms straight.
Keeping your arms straight, rotate your torso to swing the bar in an arc to one side, pivoting on your feet.
Pause, then swing the bar through the middle to the other side, controlling the weight with your core.
formCues: Turn from the torso and hips
Control the bar through the middle

commonMistakes: Using the arms instead of the core
safety: Make sure the bar is firmly anchored
Use a light load

exercises.name: Barbell side bend
steps: Set a light barbell across your upper back as for a back squat and stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Keeping your hips still and your back flat, bend sideways, lowering one side of your torso towards your hip.
Return to upright using your side abs, then bend to the other side.

safety: Use a light weight
Do not do it with lower back pain
metadata.reviewNote: A light assistance move; reviewer to decide whether to keep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
steps: Sit on the end of the bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh. Lie back, using your knees to help kick the dumbbells up to chest level one at a time. Lie with your feet flat, shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Hold the dumbbells over your chest with straight arms and palms facing forward or slightly in.
Lower the dumbbells under control to the sides of your chest, with your elbows about 45–60° from your body, until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly together to straight arms over your chest.
At the end of the set, lower the dumbbells to your thighs and sit up.
formCues: Shoulder blades pinned back and down

commonMistakes: Letting the dumbbells drift out of line with the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
Dropping the dumbbells after the last rep
safety: Kick the dumbbells up and bring them back down to the thighs carefully — do not drop them
Use a spotter for heavy dumbbells
Choose a weight you can control through the full range

exercises.name: Dumbbell incline bench press
steps: Set the bench to 30–45°. Sit on the end of the bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh. Lie back, using your knees to help kick the dumbbells up to chest level one at a time.
Hold the dumbbells over your upper chest with straight arms and palms facing forward or slightly in. Pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Lower the dumbbells under control to the sides of your upper chest, with your elbows about 45–60° from your body.
Press the dumbbells up to straight arms over your upper chest, bringing them slightly together.
At the end of the set, lower the dumbbells to your thighs and sit up.
formCues: Press straight up over the upper chest

safety: Kick the dumbbells up and bring them back carefully — do not drop them
Use a spotter for heavy dumbbells

exercises.name: Dumbbell low incline bench press
steps: Set the bench to a slight incline of about 15–30°. Sit on the end of the bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh. Lie back, using your knees to help kick the dumbbells up to chest level one at a time.
Hold the dumbbells over your upper chest with straight arms and pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your upper chest with your elbows about 45–60° from your body.
Press the dumbbells up to straight arms, bringing them slightly together.

safety: Kick the dumbbells up and bring them back carefully
Use a spotter for heavy dumbbells

exercises.name: Dumbbell decline bench press
steps: Set a decline bench to about 15–30° and hook your feet under the pads. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back, bringing the dumbbells up to your lower chest.
Press the dumbbells up to straight arms over your lower chest, with palms facing forward or slightly in.
Lower them under control to the sides of your lower chest, elbows about 45–60° from your body.
Press back up. At the end of the set, lower the dumbbells carefully to your sides and sit up.

safety: Have a spotter hand you the dumbbells for heavy sets
Do not do it with high blood pressure
metadata.reviewNote: Needs a decline bench, which many Indian gyms lack. Reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell fly
steps: Sit on the end of the bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh. Lie back, using your knees to help kick the dumbbells up to chest level one at a time.
Press the dumbbells up over your chest with your palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Keeping that elbow bend fixed, open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest, with the dumbbells about level with your chest.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back up in the same arc until they almost touch above your chest.
At the end of the set, lower the dumbbells to your thighs and sit up.
formCues: Fixed, slight bend in the elbows
Open in a wide arc like hugging a tree
Stop when the dumbbells reach chest level

commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows like a press
safety: Use a light-to-moderate weight
Stop at chest level to protect the shoulders
Stop if you feel pinching in the front of the shoulder

exercises.name: Dumbbell incline fly
steps: Set the bench to about 30°. Sit on the end of the bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh. Lie back, using your knees to help kick the dumbbells up to chest level one at a time.
Press the dumbbells up over your upper chest with your palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Keeping the elbow bend fixed, open your arms out in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest, with the dumbbells about level with your chest.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back up in the same arc until they almost touch.

safety: Use a light-to-moderate weight
Stop at chest level to protect the shoulders

exercises.name: Dumbbell decline fly
steps: Set a decline bench to about 15–30° and hook your feet under the pads. Lie back with a dumbbell in each hand, held over your lower chest with straight arms and palms facing each other.
Keeping a slight, fixed bend in your elbows, open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together over your lower chest.

safety: Use a light weight
Have a spotter hand you the dumbbells
metadata.reviewNote: Rare in practice; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell squeeze press
steps: Sit on the end of the bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh. Lie back, using your knees to help kick the dumbbells up to chest level one at a time.
Press the dumbbells over your chest and press them firmly together, palms facing each other.
Keep squeezing the dumbbells together and lower them to your chest, keeping your elbows close.
Press them back up to straight arms while still squeezing them together.
formCues: Squeeze the dumbbells together the whole time

safety: Use a moderate weight
Kick the dumbbells up and bring them back carefully

exercises.name: Dumbbell floor press
steps: Lie on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a dumbbell in each hand over your chest.
Lower the dumbbells until your upper arms rest on the floor, keeping your elbows about 45° from your body.
Pause for a moment without relaxing, then press the dumbbells up to straight arms.
formCues: Upper arms stop on the floor

commonMistakes: Bouncing the arms off the floor
safety: Bring the dumbbells to the starting position carefully
Good where there is no bench or the shoulders are sore

exercises.name: Dumbbell pullover
steps: Lie across a flat bench with your upper back on the bench and your feet flat on the floor, or lie lengthwise with your head near the end. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, cupping the top plate, over your chest with your arms nearly straight.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch across your chest and lats.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest along the same arc, squeezing your chest.
Control the dumbbell throughout and breathe normally.

commonMistakes: Bending the elbows like a triceps extension
safety: Hold the dumbbell with both hands, firmly cupping the plate
Use a light weight
Stop if the shoulders pinch
metadata.reviewNote: Some coaches file this under lats; kept under chest for consistency with the barbell pullover.

exercises.name: Dumbbell single-arm bench press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand and your other arm out to the side or across your chest for balance. Plant your feet firmly.
Brace your core and press the dumbbell up to straight arms over your chest, resisting any tendency to twist.
Lower the dumbbell under control to the side of your chest.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Brace the core to resist rotation

safety: Start with a lighter weight than your two-arm press
Use a spotter for heavy weights

exercises.name: Dumbbell bent-over row
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips until your torso is at about 45° to the floor, back flat, arms hanging straight, palms facing each other.
Brace your core, then pull the dumbbells up towards your lower ribs, driving your elbows back past your torso and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower the dumbbells under control to straight arms.
Keep the same torso angle on every rep.
formCues: Hinge at the hips, back flat

commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to move the weight
Pulling to the chest instead of the lower ribs
safety: Keep your back flat under load
Do not use weights so heavy that you have to jerk them up

exercises.name: Dumbbell chest-supported incline row
steps: Set an incline bench to about 30–45°. Lie face down on it with your chest against the pad and your feet on the floor or against the base, a dumbbell in each hand hanging straight down, palms facing each other.
Pull the dumbbells up towards your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly to full arm extension.
Keep your chest on the pad throughout.

commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad
safety: Use a stable bench
Pick up the dumbbells carefully before you lie down

exercises.name: Dumbbell renegade row
steps: Place two hex dumbbells on the floor shoulder width apart and get into a push-up position, gripping the handles, with your feet wider than shoulder width for balance.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line.
Row one dumbbell up towards your ribs while keeping your hips square to the floor, then lower it under control.
Alternate sides, keeping your hips from rotating.
formCues: Row the elbow to the hip

safety: Use hex dumbbells that cannot roll
Start with light weights or without the row
Do not do it with wrist or shoulder pain
metadata.reviewNote: Equal parts core and back exercise; the target could be argued as abs.

exercises.name: Dumbbell one-arm row
steps: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench, with your other foot on the floor and your back flat and roughly parallel to the floor. Hold a dumbbell in the free hand, arm hanging straight, palm facing the bench.
Brace your core and pull the dumbbell up towards your hip, driving your elbow back and close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blade towards your spine at the top, then lower the dumbbell slowly to full extension.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Pull the elbow to the hip

commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to heave the weight
Pulling to the shoulder instead of the hip
safety: Use a stable bench
Keep your back flat
Do not go so heavy that you have to twist

exercises.name: Dumbbell Kroc row
steps: Stand beside a bench or rack and rest one hand on it for support, with your feet staggered and your back flat. Hold a heavy dumbbell in the other hand with a straps-free or strapped grip.
Pull the dumbbell explosively towards your hip with a controlled body english, keeping your back flat.
Lower the dumbbell slowly to a full stretch and repeat for high reps.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Pull the elbow to the hip

safety: Use straps if grip limits you
Do not do it with lower-back problems
Start with a moderate weight
metadata.reviewNote: An advanced bodybuilding variant. Reviewer to decide whether it belongs.

exercises.name: Dumbbell underhand bent-over row
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward-up. Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips until your torso is at about 45° to the floor, back flat.
Pull the dumbbells up towards your lower abdomen, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower the dumbbells under control.

safety: Start lighter than your overhand row
Keep your back flat

exercises.name: Dumbbell shrug
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, arms straight, palms facing your body.
Keeping your arms straight, lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Pause and squeeze at the top, then lower your shoulders slowly.

safety: Use straps for heavy dumbbells
Keep your neck neutral

exercises.name: Dumbbell incline prone shrug
steps: Set an incline bench to about 30–45° and lie face down with your chest on the pad, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging straight.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and up, lifting your shoulders towards your ears without bending your elbows.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
formCues: Squeeze the shoulder blades back and up

commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad
safety: Use light weights
Use a stable bench

exercises.name: Dumbbell back extension
steps: Set a back extension bench so your hips are just off the pad and your heels are locked under the roller. Hold one dumbbell against your chest with both hands.
Keep your back neutral and lower your torso until it is about 90° to your legs.
Squeeze your glutes and lower back to raise your torso until your body is in a straight line. Do not arch past a straight line.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Start without weight
Do not do it with lower back pain

exercises.name: Dumbbell good morning
steps: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands. Stand with your feet hip width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Brace your core and push your hips straight back, letting your torso lean forward with a flat back.
Lower until your torso is about parallel to the floor, or until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
formCues: Hold the dumbbell close to the chest
Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Start with a light dumbbell
Stop if your lower back rounds

exercises.name: Dumbbell seated shoulder press
steps: Set an upright bench to 90° (or use a seat with a back pad). Sit with your back and glutes against the pad and feet flat, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Hold the dumbbells with your palms facing forward and your elbows slightly in front of your body.
Press the dumbbells up in a slight arc until your arms are straight above your shoulders, without clanking them together.
Lower the dumbbells under control to shoulder height.

commonMistakes: Using too much weight and bouncing
safety: Kick the dumbbells up to your shoulders using your knees
Do not drop them
Skip it if you have shoulder pain overhead

exercises.name: Dumbbell standing shoulder press
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward, glutes and abs braced.
Press the dumbbells straight up to a full lockout over your head, moving your head slightly forward as they pass.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to shoulder height.

commonMistakes: Using leg drive when you do not mean to
safety: Use a weight you can control without leaning back
Skip it with shoulder pain overhead

exercises.name: Dumbbell Arnold press
steps: Sit on an upright bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest height with your palms facing you and your elbows pointing down.
As you press the dumbbells up, rotate your wrists so your palms face forward by the time you reach the top.
Lock out overhead, then lower the dumbbells while rotating your palms back towards you.
Finish with the dumbbells at chest height, palms facing you.

safety: Use lighter weights than your normal press
Skip it if the rotation hurts your shoulders

exercises.name: Dumbbell single-arm shoulder press
steps: Stand or sit holding a dumbbell at shoulder height in one hand, with your other hand on your hip or a support.
Brace your core and press the dumbbell straight up to a full lockout over your shoulder.
Lower it under control back to your shoulder.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a weight you can control
Skip it with shoulder pain overhead

exercises.name: Dumbbell push press
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing in.
Bend your knees slightly in a short dip, keeping your torso upright.
Drive explosively through your legs and press the dumbbells overhead to full lockout.
Lower the dumbbells to your shoulders, absorbing the weight with your knees.
formCues: Absorb the weight on the way down

safety: Learn the strict press first
Do not drop the dumbbells onto the shoulders

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in, with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides, leading with your elbows, until they are about level with your shoulders.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly.

commonMistakes: Raising the dumbbells above shoulder height
safety: Use light weights
Control the lowering

exercises.name: Dumbbell seated lateral raise
steps: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, with your back straight and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides, leading with your elbows, until they are about level with your shoulders.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use light weights

exercises.name: Dumbbell front raise
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing your body, with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise one arm straight in front of you to about shoulder height, then lower it slowly.
Alternate arms, or raise both together.

safety: Use light weights

exercises.name: Dumbbell bent-over rear delt raise
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand. Hinge at the hips until your torso is close to parallel to the floor, with your back flat and your arms hanging straight down.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your torso, leading with your elbows.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly.
formCues: Back flat, hinge at the hips

safety: Use light weights
Keep your back flat

exercises.name: Dumbbell chest-supported rear delt raise
steps: Set an incline bench to about 30–45° and lie face down on it, with your chest on the pad and a dumbbell in each hand hanging straight down.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides until they are in line with your torso.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly.

commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad
safety: Use light weights
Use a stable bench

exercises.name: Dumbbell Y raise
steps: Set an incline bench to about 45° and lie face down, holding light dumbbells with your arms hanging straight and your thumbs pointing up.
Raise your arms diagonally up and forward, forming a Y shape with your body, until they are in line with your torso.
Pause, then lower slowly.

safety: Use very light weights
Stop if your shoulders pinch
metadata.reviewNote: A shoulder-health movement rather than a strength lift.

exercises.name: Dumbbell upright row
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, palms facing your body.
Lift the dumbbells up along your body, leading with your elbows, until your elbows are about shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.

commonMistakes: Pulling the elbows above the shoulders
safety: Keep the dumbbells below chest height
Skip it if you have shoulder pain
metadata.reviewNote: Often flagged for shoulder impingement; same warning as the barbell version.

exercises.name: Dumbbell goblet squat
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width and toes turned out a little. Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands cupping the top end.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and sit down and back, bending your knees and hips together.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, with your elbows inside your knees and your heels down.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.
formCues: Chest up, dumbbell close to the chest

commonMistakes: Dropping the dumbbell away from the chest
safety: Start light and master the pattern
Hold the dumbbell firmly with both hands

exercises.name: Dumbbell squat
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, arms straight, palms facing your body.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and sit down and back, bending your knees and hips together.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping the dumbbells at your sides.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.
formCues: Arms hang loose, dumbbells at the sides

safety: Use dumbbells you can hold comfortably
Master the bodyweight squat first

exercises.name: Dumbbell front squat
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with the heads resting on your front shoulders, elbows pointing forward and your palms facing in.
Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, chest up and core braced.
Sit down and back, keeping your torso upright and your elbows high.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive up through your whole foot.

safety: Start light
Do not drop the dumbbells from the shoulders

exercises.name: Dumbbell split squat
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, with one foot a long stride in front of the other and your back heel lifted.
Bend both knees and lower your back knee straight down towards the floor, keeping your torso upright and your front shin near vertical.
Press up through your front foot to the start.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Drive up through the front heel

safety: Use a stable surface and start with light weights

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian split squat
steps: Stand about two feet in front of a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Bend your front knee and lower your hips straight down until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor, keeping your torso upright.
Press up through your front foot to the start.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

commonMistakes: Standing too close to the bench
safety: Use a stable bench
Start with bodyweight, then light dumbbells

exercises.name: Dumbbell walking lunge
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, in a clear space.
Step forward into a long stride and lower until both knees are bent at about 90° and your back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee over your ankle.
Push through your front foot, bringing your back foot forward to the next stride. Alternate legs.

safety: Make sure there is a clear walking path
Start with light dumbbells

exercises.name: Dumbbell reverse lunge
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet hip width apart.
Step back with one foot, landing on the ball of your foot, and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee over your ankle.
Drive through your front foot to stand and bring your back foot forward. Alternate legs.

safety: Start with light dumbbells
Make sure there is space behind you

exercises.name: Dumbbell forward lunge
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet hip width apart.
Step forward into a long stride and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Push back through your front foot to return to the start.
Alternate legs.

safety: Start with light dumbbells

exercises.name: Dumbbell step-up
steps: Stand facing a stable box or bench at about knee height, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place one foot fully on the box and press through that heel to step up, bringing your other foot beside it.
Stand tall, then step back down with control, leading with the same leg.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Do not push off the bottom foot

commonMistakes: Using a box that is too high
safety: Use a stable box
Keep the knee at or below 90°

exercises.name: Dumbbell thruster
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing in, with your feet shoulder width apart.
Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and elbows in front.
Drive up explosively and use that momentum to press the dumbbells overhead to full lockout.
Lower the dumbbells to your shoulders as you go straight into the next squat.
formCues: Drive up and press in one movement
Lower to the shoulders under control

commonMistakes: Pressing before the legs finish driving
Dropping the dumbbells onto the shoulders
safety: Use light-to-moderate dumbbells
Learn the squat and the press separately first
metadata.reviewNote: A conditioning move; could also live under cardio. Reviewer to decide.

exercises.name: Dumbbell hip thrust
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the long edge of a stable bench, about at the bottom of your shoulder blades. Rest a dumbbell on your hip crease, holding it with both hands.
Plant your feet flat about hip width apart, knees bent so your shins are vertical at the top.
Brace your core, tuck your chin and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, ribs down, then lower under control.

commonMistakes: Feet too far or too close
safety: Pad the dumbbell
Brace the bench against a wall

exercises.name: Dumbbell glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, hip width apart. Hold a dumbbell across your hip crease with both hands.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.

safety: Pad the dumbbell

exercises.name: Dumbbell single-leg hip thrust
aliases: One leg glute bridge with dumbbell
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a stable bench and a dumbbell across your hip crease. Plant one foot flat and extend the other leg or hold the knee towards your chest.
Brace your core and drive through the heel of your planted foot to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
