Squeeze your glute at the top, keeping your hips level, then lower under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Start with bodyweight
Brace the bench against a wall

exercises.name: Dumbbell deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart with a dumbbell on the floor on each side of your feet, or hold them in front of your thighs.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the dumbbells, keeping your chest up and your back flat.
Drive through your whole foot and extend your hips and knees to stand tall, keeping the dumbbells close to your legs.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower the dumbbells under control along your legs.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Do not lift with a rounded back
Start light and learn the hinge

exercises.name: Dumbbell sumo deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet wide, about twice shoulder width, toes turned out. Hold one dumbbell hanging between your legs with both hands.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and push your hips back and bend your knees to lower the dumbbell towards the floor.
Drive your knees out and push the floor apart as you stand up.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.

safety: Start light

exercises.name: Dumbbell curtsy lunge
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet hip width apart.
Step one foot back and across behind your other leg, as if curtsying, and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Keep your torso upright and your hips square to the front.
Drive through your front foot to return to the start. Alternate legs.

safety: Start with bodyweight
Use a clear space

exercises.name: Dumbbell swing
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width holding one dumbbell vertically with both hands, hanging in front of you.
Hinge at the hips and swing the dumbbell back between your legs, keeping your back flat.
Snap your hips forward and stand tall, letting the dumbbell float up to about chest height, arms straight.
Let it swing back down, hinging your hips back again, and repeat.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

commonMistakes: Letting the dumbbell pull you forward
safety: Hold the dumbbell firmly with both hands
Learn the hinge with a deadlift first
A kettlebell is easier to swing
metadata.reviewNote: A kettlebell is the normal tool for this; will also appear in the kettlebell batch.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, feet hip width apart and knees slightly bent.
Brace your core, keep your back flat and push your hips straight back, letting the dumbbells slide down your legs.
Lower to about mid-shin or until you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Stop when your back starts to round
Use dumbbells you can control

exercises.name: Dumbbell single-leg Romanian deadlift
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand (or one in the opposite hand to your standing leg) and stand on one foot with a slight bend in the knee.
Brace your core and hinge forward at the hip, sliding the dumbbells down your leg while your free leg extends straight back.
Lower until your torso is about parallel to the floor, keeping your hips square.
Drive through your standing heel to stand tall. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Free leg and torso move as one

safety: Start with a light dumbbell
Use a wall or rack for balance

exercises.name: Dumbbell stiff-leg deadlift
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, feet hip width apart, legs almost straight.
Keep your back flat and hinge forward at the hips, lowering the dumbbells along your legs.
Lower until you feel a deep hamstring stretch, then return to standing by driving your hips forward.

safety: Use lighter weights than your RDL
Stop at the end of the hamstring stretch
metadata.reviewNote: Very close to the dumbbell Romanian deadlift; keep only one if the reviewer prefers.

exercises.name: Dumbbell staggered-stance Romanian deadlift
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with your feet hip width apart, then move one foot back so only the ball of that foot is on the floor, like a kickstand.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back, lowering the dumbbells along your front leg. Most of your weight stays on your front leg.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

commonMistakes: Putting weight on the back foot
safety: Start light

exercises.name: Dumbbell lying leg curl
steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with your knees just off the end. Have a partner place a dumbbell between your feet, or hold it between your feet by gripping it with your heels.
Curl your heels up towards your glutes by bending your knees, keeping your hips pressed to the bench.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a light dumbbell and have a partner help
Stop if the dumbbell slips
metadata.reviewNote: Awkward and rarely used; a leg curl machine is the norm. Reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell sumo squat
steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder width apart, toes turned out about 30–45°. Hold one dumbbell vertically in front of you with both hands, hanging between your legs.
Brace your core and bend your knees and hips, sitting straight down and pushing your knees out over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, chest up.
Drive up through your whole foot, pushing your knees out, to stand.
formCues: Knees push out over the toes

safety: Warm up the hips and adductors first

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral lunge
steps: Stand holding one dumbbell at your chest with both hands (goblet position), feet together.
Step out wide to one side and sit your hips back and down over that leg, keeping the other leg straight and both feet flat and pointing forward.
Lower until your thigh is about parallel to the floor, chest up.
Push through the bent leg to return to standing. Alternate sides.

commonMistakes: Lifting the heel of the bent leg
safety: Start with bodyweight
Stop if you feel groin pain

exercises.name: Dumbbell Cossack squat
steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder width apart, holding one dumbbell at your chest with both hands.
Shift your weight to one side and sit down over that leg, keeping the other leg straight with its toes pointing up.
Lower as far as you comfortably can, then push through the bent leg to return to the centre.
Repeat on the other side, moving smoothly side to side.
formCues: Straight leg stays straight, toes up

commonMistakes: Heel lifting on the bent leg
Going too deep with poor mobility
safety: Move within your range
Start with bodyweight

exercises.name: Dumbbell standing calf raise
steps: Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised block or step, heels hanging off, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Lower your heels as far as comfortable for a deep stretch.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can, squeeze your calves at the top, and lower slowly.

safety: Hold on to a support for balance
Use a stable step

exercises.name: Dumbbell single-leg calf raise
aliases: One leg calf raise with dumbbell
steps: Stand on one foot with the ball of that foot on a step, holding a dumbbell in the same-side hand, and holding a wall or rail with your other hand.
Lower your heel as far as comfortable for a deep stretch.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can, squeeze at the top, and lower slowly.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Hold a support for balance

exercises.name: Dumbbell seated calf raise
steps: Sit on a bench with the balls of your feet on a raised block or plate, knees bent at about 90°.
Rest a dumbbell on each thigh just above your knees, holding them in place with your hands.
Lower your heels for a deep stretch, then rise up onto your toes as high as you can.
Squeeze your calves at the top and lower slowly.

safety: Hold the dumbbells firmly

exercises.name: Dumbbell curl
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward, elbows close to your body.
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl one dumbbell up towards your shoulder, rotating your palm to face you as it rises.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Alternate arms, or curl both together.

safety: Use a weight you can curl without swinging

exercises.name: Dumbbell seated curl
steps: Sit on a bench with your back supported and a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight at your sides, palms facing forward.
Keeping your elbows by your sides, curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a weight you can control

exercises.name: Dumbbell hammer curl
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your body (neutral grip).
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders without rotating your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a weight you can control
metadata.reviewNote: Works the brachialis and forearms as much as the biceps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell cross-body hammer curl
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your body.
Curl one dumbbell up and across your body towards the opposite shoulder, keeping your elbow by your side.
Lower slowly and repeat with the other arm.

safety: Use a weight you can control

exercises.name: Dumbbell incline curl
steps: Set an incline bench to about 45–60° and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down behind your torso, palms facing forward.
Keeping your upper arms still, curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.

safety: Use light weights
Pick up the dumbbells carefully before leaning back

exercises.name: Dumbbell concentration curl
steps: Sit on a bench with your feet wide and hold a dumbbell in one hand, resting the back of that upper arm against your inner thigh, arm hanging straight.
Curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm still against your thigh.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Upper arm braced on the thigh

commonMistakes: Lifting the elbow off the thigh
safety: Use a weight you can control

exercises.name: Dumbbell preacher curl
steps: Adjust a preacher bench so your armpit rests on the top of the pad. Sit down and hold a dumbbell in one hand with your arm resting on the pad, nearly straight.
Curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm on the pad.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arm is almost straight.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Upper arm stays on the pad
Stop just short of locking out

commonMistakes: Dropping the weight fast and locking the elbow
safety: Do not fully lock the elbow at the bottom
Use a light weight

exercises.name: Dumbbell Zottman curl
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward, elbows by your sides.
Curl the dumbbells up to your shoulders with an underhand grip.
At the top, rotate your wrists so your palms face down.
Lower the dumbbells slowly with the overhand grip, then rotate your palms back up at the bottom.
formCues: Rotate at the top and bottom

safety: Use light weights
Stop if your wrists hurt

exercises.name: Dumbbell spider curl
steps: Set an incline bench to about 45° and lie face down on it, chest against the pad, a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging straight down.
Keeping your upper arms still, curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.

safety: Use light weights

exercises.name: Dumbbell overhead triceps extension
steps: Sit or stand holding one dumbbell vertically with both hands, cupping the top end, and press it overhead to straight arms.
Keeping your elbows pointing forward and close to your head, bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your triceps.
Extend your elbows to press the dumbbell back up to straight arms.

safety: Hold the dumbbell firmly with both hands
Use a light weight

exercises.name: Dumbbell single-arm overhead triceps extension
steps: Sit or stand holding a dumbbell in one hand, pressed overhead with your arm straight and your other hand supporting your upper arm.
Keeping your upper arm still and your elbow pointing up, bend your elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Extend your elbow to return to the top.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Elbow points up and stays still

safety: Use a light weight
Keep a firm grip

exercises.name: Dumbbell lying triceps extension
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand above your chest with straight arms and your palms facing each other.
Keeping your upper arms still, bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells towards the sides of your head.
Extend your elbows to return the dumbbells to the start, squeezing your triceps.

safety: Use a light weight
Do not lower the dumbbells onto your head
Use a spotter for heavy sets

exercises.name: Dumbbell triceps kickback
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart and hinge forward at the hips with your back flat, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your upper arm tucked in line with your torso.
Keeping your upper arm still, extend your elbow to straighten your arm behind you.
Squeeze your triceps at the top, then lower slowly.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Upper arm stays in line with the torso

safety: Use a light weight
Support yourself with your free hand on a bench

exercises.name: Dumbbell close-grip press
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand over your chest with your palms facing each other and the dumbbells touching.
Lower the dumbbells to your chest with your elbows tucked close to your body.
Press them back up to straight arms, keeping the dumbbells touching.

safety: Use a moderate weight
Bring the dumbbells to position carefully

exercises.name: Dumbbell Tate press
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand over your chest with straight arms and your palms facing your feet.
Bend your elbows out to the sides to lower the dumbbells until the heads touch your chest, forearms pointing up and elbows flared.
Press the dumbbells back up by extending your elbows, keeping the heads close together.

commonMistakes: Bouncing the dumbbells off the chest
safety: Use light weights
Use a spotter
metadata.reviewNote: A bodybuilding triceps isolation; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell wrist curl
steps: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms up, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your wrists hanging off your knees.
Let the dumbbells roll down to your fingertips, then curl them back up by flexing your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use light weights

exercises.name: Dumbbell reverse wrist curl
steps: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms down, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your wrists hanging off your knees.
Lower the dumbbells by letting your wrists bend down, then lift them by extending your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use light weights

exercises.name: Dumbbell reverse curl
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing down, arms hanging straight.
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use lighter weights than your normal curl

exercises.name: Dumbbell farmer's walk
steps: Stand between two heavy dumbbells and hinge down to pick them up, keeping your back flat. Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Brace your core, pull your shoulders back and walk with controlled steps for the set distance or time.
Keep your posture tall and do not lean or sway.
Lower the dumbbells under control to the floor.

safety: Pick up and set down the dumbbells with a flat back
Make sure the path is clear
metadata.reviewNote: Counted by distance; logged as weight_distance (load and metres). Reviewer to confirm a time option is also wanted.

exercises.name: Dumbbell side bend
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, with your other hand behind your head or on your hip.
Keeping your hips still and your back flat, bend sideways, lowering the dumbbell towards your knee.
Return to upright using your side abs.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a light weight

exercises.name: Dumbbell Russian twist
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels on or just off the floor, leaning back slightly with a straight back. Hold one dumbbell with both hands at your chest.
Brace your core and rotate your torso to one side, moving the dumbbell towards the floor beside you.
Rotate to the other side. Each side counts as one rep.

safety: Start without lifting the feet
Use a light weight

exercises.name: Dumbbell weighted sit-up
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat or hooked under a support. Hold one dumbbell against your chest with both hands.
Brace your core and curl your torso up until you are sitting upright.
Lower yourself slowly back to the floor.
formCues: Curl up, do not yank with the neck

safety: Use a light weight
Skip it with lower back pain

exercises.name: Dumbbell wood chop
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, holding one dumbbell with both hands near one hip.
Brace your core and rotate your torso as you lift the dumbbell diagonally across your body to above the opposite shoulder, pivoting on your feet.
Return under control to the start.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Turn from the torso and hips

commonMistakes: Twisting the lower back without moving the hips
safety: Use a light weight

exercises.name: Dumbbell windmill
steps: Hold a dumbbell overhead in one hand with a locked arm and stand with your feet wider than shoulder width, toes of the back foot turned out a little.
Keeping your eyes on the dumbbell, push your hips out to the side of the overhead arm and lean sideways, sliding your free hand down your leg.
Lower as far as you comfortably can while keeping your back flat and the dumbbell arm locked.
Return to standing by squeezing your glutes and side abs.
formCues: Hips push out to the side

safety: Start with an empty hand or a very light weight
Do not do it with shoulder mobility problems
metadata.reviewNote: A mobility and strength drill that needs coaching; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell suitcase carry
steps: Pick up a heavy dumbbell in one hand with a flat back and stand tall with your other arm at your side.
Brace your core and walk for the set distance or time, keeping your torso upright and not leaning towards the weight.
Set the dumbbell down under control and repeat with the other hand.

safety: Pick up and set down with a flat back

exercises.name: Dumbbell snatch
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width and a dumbbell on the floor between your feet. Hinge down and grip it with one hand, back flat.
Drive through your legs and hips explosively and pull the dumbbell up close to your body, then punch your hand under it and catch it overhead with a locked arm.
Stand tall with the dumbbell overhead, then lower it back to the floor under control.
Alternate arms.
formCues: Keep it close to the body

commonMistakes: Catching it with a bent arm
safety: Learn with a light dumbbell
Make sure there is clear space overhead
Do not do it with shoulder problems
metadata.reviewNote: A power movement; reviewer to decide whether general trainers use it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell man maker
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand, feet shoulder width apart. Place the dumbbells on the floor and step or jump your feet back into a push-up position.
Perform a push-up, then row one dumbbell to your ribs and lower it, then row the other.
Step or jump your feet back in, stand up while pulling the dumbbells to your shoulders, and press them overhead.
Lower the dumbbells to the floor and repeat.
formCues: Brace the core in the plank
Finish with a full overhead press

commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag in the plank
safety: Use hex dumbbells
Start with light weights
Learn each part first
metadata.reviewNote: A conditioning complex; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Kettlebell swing
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width with a kettlebell on the floor about a foot in front of you. Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip the handle with both hands.
Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, like a football snap, keeping your back flat and your forearms against your thighs.
Snap your hips forward and stand tall, letting the kettlebell float up to about chest height with straight arms.
Let the kettlebell fall back, guiding it between your legs by hinging your hips back, and repeat. Set it down by placing it on the floor when the set is finished.
formCues: Hips snap the bell up, arms are hooks
Squeeze the glutes at the top, stand tall

commonMistakes: Rounding the back at the bottom
Letting the bell pull you forward
safety: Learn the hip hinge with a deadlift first
Use a clear space and a bell that is not too heavy
Do not swing above chest height until you are comfortable

exercises.name: Kettlebell single-arm swing
steps: Set up as for a two-hand swing, with the kettlebell on the floor in front of you. Hinge down and grip the handle with one hand.
Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward to swing it up to about chest height with a straight arm.
Brace your core to resist twisting, let the bell fall and hinge your hips back as it returns between your legs.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Free arm stays out for balance
Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Master the two-hand swing first
Use a clear space and never let the kettlebell swing out of control

exercises.name: Kettlebell deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart with a kettlebell on the floor between or just in front of your feet, handle in line with your ankles.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the handle with both hands, back flat and chest up.
Drive through your whole foot to stand tall, squeezing your glutes at the top, keeping the kettlebell close to your legs.
Lower the kettlebell back to the floor by hinging your hips back first.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top
Bell stays close to the legs

safety: A good first step before swings
Keep your back flat

exercises.name: Kettlebell sumo deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder width apart, toes turned out, with a kettlebell on the floor between your feet.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the handle with both hands, chest up and back flat.
Drive your knees out and push the floor apart as you stand up, keeping the bell close.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower the kettlebell under control.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Keep your back flat

exercises.name: Kettlebell hip thrust
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the long edge of a stable bench and a kettlebell resting on your hip crease, held with both hands.
Plant your feet flat, hip width apart, knees bent so your shins are vertical at the top.
Brace your core, tuck your chin and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.

safety: Pad the kettlebell
Brace the bench against a wall

exercises.name: Kettlebell goblet squat
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width and toes turned out a little. Hold a kettlebell by the horns (the sides of the handle) against your chest, elbows pointing down.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and sit down and back, bending your knees and hips together.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, with your elbows inside your knees and your heels down.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.
formCues: Chest up, bell close to the chest

commonMistakes: Letting the bell drift away from the chest
safety: Start with a light bell
Hold the bell firmly

exercises.name: Kettlebell double front squat
steps: Clean two kettlebells to the rack position, one in each hand, elbows tucked against your ribs and the bells resting on your forearms and chest.
Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, chest up and core braced.
Sit down and back, keeping your torso upright and the bells in place.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive up through your whole foot.

commonMistakes: Letting the bells pull you forward
safety: Learn the clean and rack position with a light pair
Be ready to set the bells down safely

exercises.name: Kettlebell single-rack squat
steps: Clean the kettlebell to the rack position: the handle in your hand, the bell resting on the back of your forearm and against your chest or shoulder, your elbow tucked in against your ribs.
Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, chest up and core braced, with your free arm out for balance.
Sit down and back, keeping your torso upright and resisting the lean towards the bell.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive up. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Start with a light bell

exercises.name: Kettlebell goblet reverse lunge
steps: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by the horns against your chest, feet hip width apart.
Step back with one foot, landing on the ball of the foot, and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee over your ankle.
Drive through your front foot to stand and bring your back foot forward. Alternate legs.

safety: Start with a light bell
Make sure there is space behind you

exercises.name: Kettlebell goblet walking lunge
steps: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by the horns against your chest, feet hip width apart, in a clear space.
Step forward into a long stride and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee over your ankle.
Push through your front foot and bring your back foot forward to the next stride. Alternate legs.

safety: Make sure there is a clear path

exercises.name: Kettlebell goblet Bulgarian split squat
aliases: Goblet split squat, rear foot elevated
steps: Stand about two feet in front of a bench, holding a kettlebell by the horns against your chest. Place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Bend your front knee and lower your hips straight down until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor, torso upright.
Press up through your front foot to the start.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

commonMistakes: Standing too close to the bench
safety: Use a stable bench
Start with bodyweight

exercises.name: Kettlebell step-up
steps: Stand facing a stable box or bench at about knee height, holding a kettlebell by the horns against your chest.
Place one foot fully on the box and press through that heel to step up, bringing your other foot beside it.
Stand tall, then step back down with control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

commonMistakes: Using a box that is too high
safety: Use a stable box

exercises.name: Kettlebell thruster
steps: Hold a kettlebell by the horns at your chest, or a kettlebell in each hand in the rack position, feet shoulder width apart.
Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, chest up.
Drive up explosively and use that momentum to press the kettlebell(s) overhead to lockout.
Lower to the rack position as you go straight into the next squat.
formCues: Drive up and press in one movement

commonMistakes: Pressing before the legs finish driving
safety: Use a light bell
Learn the squat and press separately first
metadata.reviewNote: A conditioning move; could also live under cardio.

exercises.name: Kettlebell sumo squat
steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder width apart, toes turned out 30–45°, holding a kettlebell by the handle with both hands, hanging between your legs.
Brace your core and bend your knees and hips, sitting straight down and pushing your knees out over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, chest up.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.

safety: Warm up the hips and adductors first

exercises.name: Kettlebell goblet Cossack squat
steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder width apart, holding a kettlebell by the horns at your chest.
Shift your weight to one side and sit down over that leg, keeping the other leg straight with its toes pointing up.
Lower as far as you comfortably can, then push through the bent leg to return to the centre.
Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Straight leg stays straight, toes up

safety: Move within your range

exercises.name: Kettlebell lateral lunge
steps: Stand holding a kettlebell by the horns at your chest, feet together.
Step out wide to one side and sit your hips back and down over that leg, keeping the other leg straight and both feet flat and pointing forward.
Lower until your thigh is about parallel to the floor, chest up.
Push through the bent leg to return to standing. Alternate sides.

safety: Start with bodyweight

exercises.name: Kettlebell Romanian deadlift
steps: Stand holding a kettlebell in front of your thighs with both hands, or a bell in each hand, feet hip width apart and knees slightly bent.
Brace your core, keep your back flat and push your hips straight back, letting the bell(s) slide down your legs.
Lower to about mid-shin or until you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes.

safety: Stop when your back starts to round

exercises.name: Kettlebell single-leg deadlift
steps: Hold a kettlebell in one hand (the hand opposite your standing leg, or the same side if you prefer) and stand on one foot with a slight bend in the knee.
Brace your core and hinge forward at the hip, lowering the bell towards the floor while your free leg extends straight back.
Lower until your torso is about parallel to the floor, hips square.
Drive through your standing heel to stand tall. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Free leg and torso move as one

safety: Use a light bell
Use a wall or rack for balance

exercises.name: Kettlebell shoulder press
steps: Clean the kettlebell to the rack position: the handle in your hand, the bell resting on the back of your forearm and against your chest or shoulder, your elbow tucked in against your ribs. Stand with your feet hip width apart, glutes and abs braced.
Press the kettlebell straight up, rotating your palm to face forward, until your arm is fully locked out over your shoulder.
Lower the kettlebell under control back to the rack position.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

commonMistakes: Letting the bell crash into the forearm on the way down
safety: Learn the rack position first
Skip it with shoulder pain overhead

exercises.name: Kettlebell push press
steps: Clean the kettlebell to the rack position: the handle in your hand, the bell resting on the back of your forearm and against your chest or shoulder, your elbow tucked in against your ribs. Stand with your feet hip width apart.
Bend your knees slightly in a short dip, keeping your torso upright.
Drive explosively through your legs and press the kettlebell overhead to full lockout.
Lower it to the rack position, absorbing the weight with your knees. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Learn the strict press first

exercises.name: Kettlebell half-kneeling press
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front of you, so your knees and hips are at about 90°, and keep your torso upright and glutes tight. Hold the kettlebell on the same side as your kneeling knee in the rack position.
Press the kettlebell straight up to a full lockout over your shoulder.
Lower it under control to the rack position.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Glute on the kneeling side squeezed

safety: Use a mat under the knee

exercises.name: Kettlebell bottoms-up press
steps: Hold a kettlebell by the handle with the bell upside down (bottom facing up) in the rack position, gripping tightly with your elbow tucked.
Squeeze the handle hard and press the kettlebell straight up to full lockout, keeping the bell balanced and steady.
Lower it under control back to the rack position.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a light bell and a clear space
Keep your head away from the bell
metadata.reviewNote: A grip-and-stability drill; reviewer to decide whether general trainers need it.

exercises.name: Kettlebell halo
steps: Stand tall holding a kettlebell upside down by the horns at chest height, close to your chin.
Keeping the kettlebell close to your head and your torso still, circle it around your head slowly, passing it behind your neck and back to the front.
Complete the reps in one direction, then reverse direction.
formCues: Keep the bell close to the head

safety: Use a light bell and keep your head still
Move slowly

exercises.name: Kettlebell floor press
steps: Lie on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a kettlebell by the handle in one hand with your forearm vertical and the bell resting against your forearm and upper arm.
Lower your arm until your upper arm rests on the floor, keeping your elbow about 45° from your body.
Press the kettlebell up to straight arm.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Start with a light bell
Do not let the bell fall onto your face

exercises.name: Kettlebell pullover
steps: Lie across a flat bench with your upper back on the bench and your feet flat, or lie lengthwise with your head near the end. Hold a kettlebell by the horns with both hands over your chest, arms nearly straight.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, lower the kettlebell in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch across your chest and lats.
Pull the kettlebell back over your chest along the same arc.

safety: Hold the bell firmly with both hands
Use a light bell

exercises.name: Kettlebell one-arm row
steps: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench with your back flat, or stand in a staggered stance and hinge forward with your free hand on a support. Hold a kettlebell by the handle in the free hand with your arm hanging straight.
Brace your core and pull the kettlebell up towards your hip, driving your elbow back and close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blade towards your spine, then lower slowly to full extension.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Pull the elbow to the hip

safety: Keep your back flat

exercises.name: Kettlebell gorilla row
steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width, with a kettlebell on the floor between your feet and a second kettlebell on the floor outside one foot. Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip a kettlebell in each hand.
Row one kettlebell up towards your hip while the other stays on the floor, keeping your hips square.
Lower it to the floor and row the other side, alternating.

safety: Use a light bell until you have the pattern
Keep your back flat

exercises.name: Kettlebell renegade row
steps: Place two kettlebells on the floor shoulder width apart and get into a push-up position, gripping the handles, with your feet wider than shoulder width for balance.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line.
Row one kettlebell up towards your ribs, keeping your hips square to the floor, then lower it under control.
Alternate sides without letting your hips rotate.
formCues: Row the elbow to the hip

safety: Use bells with a flat base
Start with light bells or without the row

exercises.name: Kettlebell high pull
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width with a kettlebell on the floor in front of you. Hinge down and grip it with one hand.
Drive through your legs and hips explosively and pull the kettlebell up close to your body, leading with your elbow high and out to the side.
Pull until your hand is at about chest height, then lower it under control.
Alternate or complete all reps on one side.
formCues: Legs and hips power the pull

safety: Learn the swing first
Use a clear space

exercises.name: Kettlebell good morning
steps: Hold a kettlebell by the horns against your chest. Stand with your feet hip width apart and knees slightly bent.
Brace your core and push your hips straight back, letting your torso lean forward with a flat back.
Lower until your torso is about parallel to the floor, then drive your hips forward to stand tall.

safety: Start light

exercises.name: Kettlebell biceps curl
steps: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by the handle in one hand, arm hanging straight, elbow close to your side.
Keeping your elbow pinned, curl the kettlebell up towards your shoulder.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a light bell

exercises.name: Kettlebell hammer curl
steps: Stand tall holding a kettlebell upside down by the horns with both hands, arms hanging straight in front of your thighs.
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl the kettlebell up towards your chest.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.

safety: Use a light bell

exercises.name: Kettlebell overhead triceps extension
steps: Sit or stand holding a kettlebell upside down by the horns with both hands, and press it overhead to straight arms.
Keeping your elbows pointing forward, bend your elbows to lower the kettlebell behind your head.
Extend your elbows to press the kettlebell back up to straight arms.

safety: Hold the bell firmly with both hands
Use a light bell

exercises.name: Kettlebell skull crusher
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands over your chest, arms straight.
Keeping your upper arms still, bend your elbows to lower the kettlebell towards your forehead or just behind your head.
Extend your elbows to return the bell to the start.

safety: Use a light bell
Do not lower it onto your face

exercises.name: Kettlebell farmer's walk
steps: Stand between two kettlebells on the floor and hinge down to pick them up by the handles, keeping your back flat. Stand tall with a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
Brace your core, pull your shoulders back and walk with controlled steps for the set distance or time.
Keep your posture tall and do not lean or sway.
Set the kettlebells down under control.

safety: Pick up and set down with a flat back
Make sure the path is clear

exercises.name: Kettlebell bottoms-up carry
steps: Clean a kettlebell to the rack position upside down, the bell facing up, gripping the handle tightly with your elbow tucked.
Brace your core and walk slowly for the set distance or time, keeping the bell balanced and upright.
Set it down under control, then repeat with the other hand.

safety: Use a very light bell
Keep your head away from the bell
metadata.reviewNote: A grip and shoulder-stability drill; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Russian twist
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels on or just off the floor, leaning back slightly with a straight back. Hold a kettlebell by the horns at your chest.
Brace your core and rotate your torso to one side, moving the kettlebell towards the floor beside you.
Rotate to the other side. Each side counts as one rep.

safety: Start without lifting the feet
Use a light bell

exercises.name: Kettlebell windmill
steps: Hold a kettlebell overhead in one hand with a locked arm and stand with your feet wider than shoulder width, toes of the back foot turned out a little.
Keeping your eyes on the bell, push your hips out to the side of the overhead arm and lean sideways, sliding your free hand down your leg.
Lower as far as you comfortably can while keeping your back flat and the overhead arm locked.
Return to standing by squeezing your glutes and side abs.
formCues: Hips push out to the side

safety: Start with an empty hand
Do not do it with shoulder mobility problems
metadata.reviewNote: Needs coaching; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Kettlebell side bend
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at your side.
Keeping your hips still and your back flat, bend sideways, lowering the bell towards your knee.
Return to upright using your side abs. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a light bell

exercises.name: Kettlebell suitcase carry
steps: Pick up a heavy kettlebell in one hand with a flat back and stand tall with your other arm at your side.
Brace your core and walk for the set distance or time, keeping your torso upright and not leaning towards the weight.
Set the bell down under control and repeat with the other hand.

safety: Pick up and set down with a flat back

exercises.name: Kettlebell Turkish get-up
steps: Lie on your back with a kettlebell pressed over your shoulder in one hand, arm straight. Bend the knee on that side with your foot flat, and rest your other arm and leg out at about 45° from your body.
Keeping your eyes on the bell, roll up onto your elbow, then your hand, pressing the bell straight up.
Lift your hips, sweep your free leg back and under you into a kneeling lunge, then stand up tall.
Reverse each step, slowly, to lie back down. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Practise without weight, then with a shoe on the fist, then a light bell
Learn it with a coach

exercises.name: Kettlebell goblet sit-up
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat or hooked under a support, holding a kettlebell by the horns against your chest.
Brace your core and curl your torso up until you are sitting upright.
Lower yourself slowly back to the floor.
formCues: Curl up, do not yank with the neck

safety: Use a light bell
Skip it with lower back pain

exercises.name: Kettlebell clean
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width and a kettlebell on the floor in front of you. Hinge down and grip the handle with one hand.
Hike the bell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward and pull the handle up close to your body.
As the bell rises, rotate your hand around it so it lands softly in the rack position, resting on your forearm and chest.
Lower the bell back between your legs under control. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Zip the elbow tight to the ribs

commonMistakes: Letting the bell crash onto the forearm
safety: Learn the swing first
Use a light bell and a clear space

exercises.name: Kettlebell snatch
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width and a kettlebell on the floor in front of you. Hinge down and grip the handle with one hand.
Hike the bell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward and pull the bell up close to your body.
As the bell rises past your chest, punch your hand through and catch it overhead with a locked arm.
Lower it back down in the same path, hinging your hips back as it falls between your legs. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep it close to the body

commonMistakes: Letting the bell flip onto the forearm
Catching it with a bent arm

Use a light bell and a clear space

exercises.name: Kettlebell clean and press
steps: Clean the kettlebell to the rack position from the floor or from a hike between your legs.
Brace your core and press the kettlebell straight overhead to a full lockout.
Lower it under control back to the rack position, then to the floor or between your legs.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Learn the clean and press separately first
Use a light bell

exercises.name: Cable high-to-low crossover
steps: Set both pulleys at the top of the stack with a single handle on each. Grab a handle in each hand and step forward into a split stance, leaning slightly forward with your arms out to the sides.
Keeping a slight, fixed bend in your elbows, bring your hands down and together in a wide arc until they meet in front of your lower chest or hips.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly in the same arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Keep your torso still throughout.
formCues: Fixed slight bend in the elbows

commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows like a press
safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Start light and stop at the end of your comfortable stretch

exercises.name: Cable low-to-high crossover
steps: Set both pulleys at the bottom of the stack with a single handle on each. Grab a handle in each hand and step forward into a split stance, leaning slightly forward.
Keeping a slight, fixed bend in your elbows, sweep your hands up and together in a wide arc until they meet in front of your upper chest.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly in the same arc until you feel a stretch.
formCues: Hands meet at upper chest height

commonMistakes: Bending the elbows into a press
safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a moderate weight

exercises.name: Cable standing fly
steps: Set both pulleys at about chest height with a single handle on each. Grab a handle in each hand and step forward into a split stance, with your arms out to the sides.
Keeping a slight, fixed bend in your elbows, bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide arc.
Squeeze your chest for a moment, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable flat bench fly
steps: Set both pulleys at the bottom of the stack with a single handle on each, and place a flat bench between them. Lie back with a handle in each hand, arms out to the sides.
Pull the handles up and together over your chest in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Squeeze your chest at the top, then lower slowly until you feel a stretch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a stable bench

exercises.name: Cable incline bench fly
steps: Set both pulleys at the bottom of the stack and place an incline bench (about 30°) between them. Lie back with a handle in each hand, arms out to the sides.
Pull the handles up and together over your upper chest in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Squeeze your chest at the top, then lower slowly until you feel a stretch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a stable bench

exercises.name: Cable standing chest press
steps: Set both pulleys at chest height with a single handle on each. Grab a handle in each hand and step forward into a split stance, with your elbows bent and handles at the sides of your chest.

Squeeze your chest, then return slowly to the start.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable single-arm chest press
steps: Set one pulley at chest height with a single handle. Stand sideways to the stack in a split stance, holding the handle at the side of your chest.

Return slowly to the start. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable wide-grip lat pulldown
steps: Sit at a lat pulldown station with your thighs secured under the pads. Grip the bar with an overhand grip, wider than shoulder width.
Lean back slightly, lift your chest and pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back and squeezing your shoulder blades.

Keep your wrists straight
Adjust the thigh pads so you stay seated

exercises.name: Cable close-grip lat pulldown
steps: Sit at a lat pulldown station with your thighs secured. Attach a close-grip or V-bar handle and grip it with your palms facing each other.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest. Pull the handle down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your lats, then let the handle rise slowly until your arms are straight.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable neutral-grip lat pulldown
steps: Sit at a lat pulldown station with your thighs secured. Use a parallel-grip handle so your palms face each other, hands shoulder width apart or slightly narrower.
Lean back slightly, lift your chest and pull the handle to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your lats, then let the handle rise slowly until your arms are straight.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable underhand lat pulldown
steps: Sit at a lat pulldown station with your thighs secured. Grip the bar with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest. Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your lats, then let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.

Use a lighter weight than your overhand pulldown

exercises.name: Cable single-arm lat pulldown
steps: Set a single handle on a high pulley and sit or kneel facing the stack. Grab the handle with one hand.
Brace your core and pull the handle down towards your shoulder, driving your elbow down and back, without twisting your torso.
Squeeze your lat, then let the handle rise slowly until your arm is straight.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

exercises.name: Cable straight-arm pulldown
steps: Set a straight bar or rope on a high pulley. Stand facing the stack with your feet hip width apart, hinge forward slightly and hold the attachment with straight arms.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, pull the attachment down in an arc to your thighs, squeezing your lats.
Return slowly in the same arc until you feel a stretch.

commonMistakes: Bending the elbows into a pushdown
safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable underhand seated row
steps: Sit at a low cable row station with your feet on the platform and your knees slightly bent. Grip a straight bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder width apart.
Sit tall, chest up and back flat, with your arms straight.
Pull the bar into your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back and close to your body, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until your arms are straight, without rounding forward.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Keep your back flat

exercises.name: Cable seated row
steps: Sit at a low cable row station with your feet on the platform and your knees slightly bent. Grip a V-handle or parallel-grip handle with arms straight.
Sit tall with your chest up and your back flat.
Pull the handle to your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back past your torso and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until your arms are straight, without rounding forward.

safety: Keep your back flat
Do not lean back with a heavy stack

exercises.name: Cable wide-grip seated row
steps: Sit at a low cable row station with your feet on the platform and your knees slightly bent. Grip a long bar with an overhand grip, wider than shoulder width.
Sit tall with your chest up and arms straight.
Pull the bar to your lower chest or upper abdomen, with your elbows flaring out about 60–75°, and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.

safety: Keep your back flat

exercises.name: Cable single-arm seated row
steps: Sit at a low cable row station with your feet on the platform and a single handle attached. Grip the handle with one hand and sit tall.
Pull the handle to your side, driving your elbow back and keeping your torso square.
Squeeze your shoulder blade towards your spine, then return slowly.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable rope row
steps: Sit at a low cable row station with a rope attachment, feet on the platform, knees slightly bent, and grip the rope ends with a neutral grip.
Sit tall with your arms straight.
Pull the rope towards your chest, splitting the ends apart as you pull, and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
formCues: Split the rope as you pull

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable shrug
steps: Set a low pulley with a straight bar or two single handles. Stand tall holding the bar or handles at your thighs with straight arms.
Keeping your arms straight, lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable lateral raise
steps: Set a single handle on a low pulley. Stand side-on to the stack and grip the handle with the far hand, arm across your body, with a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise your arm out to the side, leading with your elbow, until it is about level with your shoulder.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a light weight

exercises.name: Cable front raise
steps: Set a low pulley with a straight bar or rope. Stand facing away from the stack with the cable between your legs, holding the attachment at your thighs.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms straight in front of you to about shoulder height.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable rear delt fly
steps: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height with single handles, crossed over: your right hand takes the left handle and your left hand takes the right handle.
Stand tall in the middle with your arms crossed in front of you, a slight bend in your elbows.
Pull your arms out and back in a wide arc until they are in line with your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly under control.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable face pull
steps: Set a rope attachment on a pulley at about face height. Grip the rope ends with your palms facing each other and step back so your arms are straight and the weight is lifted.
Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your core braced.
Pull the rope towards your face, splitting the ends apart, with your elbows high and your hands finishing beside your ears.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a light weight and good form

exercises.name: Cable upright row
steps: Set a low pulley with a straight bar or rope. Stand facing the stack holding the attachment in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Lift the attachment up along your body, leading with your elbows, until your elbows are about shoulder height.
Lower under control to the start.

safety: Keep the bar below chest height
Skip it if you have shoulder pain

exercises.name: Cable single-arm overhead press
steps: Set a single handle on a low pulley. Stand side-on to the stack in a split stance, holding the handle at shoulder height with your elbow bent.
Brace your core and press the handle straight up to a full lockout.
Lower it under control back to your shoulder.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Skip it with shoulder pain overhead

exercises.name: Cable Y raise
steps: Set both pulleys at the bottom of the stack with single handles. Stand in the middle holding a handle in each hand, arms crossed in front of you at your thighs, thumbs pointing up.
Raise your arms diagonally up and out, forming a Y shape with your body, until they are in line with your torso.
Pause, then lower slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use very light weights

exercises.name: Cable external rotation
steps: Set a single handle on a pulley at about elbow height. Stand side-on to the stack with the working arm farthest from it, elbow bent 90° and tucked against your side (use a rolled towel under the elbow).
Hold the handle with your forearm pointing across your body.

exercises.name: Cable curl

exercises.name: Cable EZ-bar curl

Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable rope hammer curl
steps: Set a rope attachment on a low pulley. Stand facing the stack holding the rope ends with a neutral grip, palms facing each other, arms straight.

Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable single-arm curl
steps: Set a single handle on a low pulley. Stand facing the stack holding the handle in one hand with an underhand grip, elbow by your side.
Curl the handle up towards your shoulder, keeping your elbow pinned.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable high double-biceps curl
steps: Set both pulleys at about head height with a single handle on each. Stand in the middle holding a handle in each hand with your arms out to the sides, palms facing up.
Keeping your upper arms still and level with your shoulders, curl the handles towards your ears.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then extend slowly.
formCues: Upper arms stay level and still

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a light weight

exercises.name: Cable Bayesian curl
steps: Set a single handle on a low pulley. Stand facing away from the stack, holding the handle in one hand with your arm behind your body, and step forward so your arm is slightly behind your torso.
Keeping your upper arm back and your elbow pinned, curl the handle up towards your shoulder.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch behind your body.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable preacher curl
steps: Set a low pulley and place a preacher bench in front of it. Sit with your armpits on the top of the pad and grip a straight or EZ bar with an underhand grip.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms on the pad.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.

Stop just short of locking out

Do not fully lock the elbows at the bottom

exercises.name: Cable lying curl
steps: Set a low pulley and lie on the floor or a flat bench with your head near the stack. Hold a straight bar with an underhand grip, arms straight.
Keeping your upper arms still, curl the bar towards your forehead.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable rope pushdown
steps: Set a rope attachment on a high pulley. Stand facing the stack with your feet hip width apart, gripping the rope ends with a neutral grip and your elbows pinned to your sides.
Press the rope down until your arms are fully straight, splitting the ends apart at the bottom.
Squeeze your triceps, then return slowly until your forearms are just past parallel to the floor.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable straight-bar pushdown

Press the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze your triceps, then return slowly until your forearms are just past parallel to the floor.

exercises.name: Cable V-bar pushdown

Press the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze your triceps, then return slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable reverse-grip pushdown
steps: Set a straight bar on a high pulley. Stand facing the stack, gripping the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder width apart, elbows pinned to your sides.
Press the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze your triceps, then return slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a lighter weight than your overhand pushdown

exercises.name: Cable single-arm pushdown
steps: Set a single handle on a high pulley. Stand facing the stack holding the handle in one hand, elbow pinned to your side.
Press the handle down until your arm is fully straight.
Squeeze your triceps, then return slowly.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable overhead rope triceps extension
steps: Set a rope attachment on a high or mid pulley. Stand facing away from the stack in a split stance, holding the rope ends behind your head with your elbows pointing forward.

Squeeze your triceps, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable single-arm overhead triceps extension
steps: Set a single handle on a low or mid pulley. Stand facing away from the stack in a split stance, holding the handle behind your head with your elbow pointing up.
Extend your elbow to press the handle up until your arm is straight, keeping your upper arm still.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Elbow points up and stays still

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable triceps kickback
steps: Set a single handle on a low pulley. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, holding the handle with your upper arm tucked in line with your torso.
Keeping your upper arm still, extend your elbow to straighten your arm behind you.
Squeeze your triceps, then return slowly.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Upper arm stays in line with the torso

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable wrist curl
steps: Set a low pulley with a straight bar. Sit on a bench facing the stack with your forearms resting on your thighs, palms up, holding the bar with an underhand grip and your wrists hanging off your knees.
Let the bar roll down to your fingertips, then curl it up by flexing your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a light weight

exercises.name: Cable reverse wrist curl
steps: Set a low pulley with a straight bar. Sit on a bench facing the stack with your forearms resting on your thighs, palms down, holding the bar with an overhand grip and your wrists hanging off your knees.
Lower the bar by letting your wrists bend down, then lift it by extending your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a light weight

exercises.name: Cable reverse curl
steps: Set a straight bar on a low pulley. Stand facing the stack holding the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder width apart, arms straight.
Keeping your elbows pinned, curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable kneeling crunch
steps: Set a rope attachment on a high pulley. Kneel facing the stack and hold the rope ends beside your head, with your hips above your knees.

exercises.name: Cable high-to-low wood chop
steps: Set a single handle on a high pulley. Stand side-on to the stack with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the handle with both hands above your near shoulder.
Brace your core and rotate your torso as you pull the handle diagonally down across your body to the opposite hip, pivoting on your feet.
Return slowly under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Turn from the torso and hips

commonMistakes: Twisting the lower back without moving the hips

exercises.name: Cable low-to-high wood chop
steps: Set a single handle on a low pulley. Stand side-on to the stack with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the handle with both hands near your near hip.
Brace your core and rotate your torso as you pull the handle diagonally up across your body to above the opposite shoulder, pivoting on your feet.

commonMistakes: Twisting the lower back without moving the hips
safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable Pallof press

Brace your core and step out until the cable is taut, resisting the pull to rotate.
Press the handle straight out in front of you until your arms are straight, without letting your torso turn.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable side bend
steps: Set a single handle on a low pulley. Stand side-on to the stack, holding the handle in your near hand at your side.
Keeping your hips still and your back flat, bend sideways away from the stack, lowering your torso towards the opposite hip.
Return to upright using your side abs. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely
Use a light weight

exercises.name: Cable standing twist
steps: Set a single handle on a pulley at chest height. Stand side-on to the stack with your feet shoulder width apart, holding the handle with both hands in front of your chest.
Keeping your arms straight in front of you, rotate your torso away from the stack, pivoting on your feet.
Return slowly under control. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable Romanian deadlift
steps: Set a low pulley with a straight bar or rope. Stand facing the stack holding the attachment at your thighs, feet hip width apart, knees slightly bent.
Brace your core, keep your back flat and push your hips straight back, letting the attachment slide down your legs.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable standing leg curl
steps: Set a low pulley and attach an ankle strap. Strap it to one ankle and stand facing the stack, holding a support for balance.

exercises.name: Cable glute kickback

exercises.name: Cable pull-through

exercises.name: Cable hip abduction

exercises.name: Cable hip adduction

Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.

exercises.name: Cable goblet squat
steps: Set a handle or rope on a low pulley. Stand facing the stack, holding the attachment at your chest with both hands, elbows pointing down, and step back so the cable is taut.

Sit down and back, bending your knees and hips, keeping the cable close to your chest.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive up through your whole foot.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Cable leg extension
steps: Set a low pulley and attach an ankle strap. Sit on a bench facing away from the stack, with the strap on one ankle and your knee bent, holding the bench.
Extend your knee to straighten your leg in front of you, squeezing your quad at the top.

safety: Check the attachment is clipped on securely

exercises.name: Smith machine incline bench press
steps: Set an incline bench (30–45°) in the middle of the smith machine so the bar lines up with your upper chest. Set the safety stops just below your chest.
Lie back with your feet flat and shoulder blades pulled back and down. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and twist it to unhook it.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest.
Press the bar up to straight arms, then rehook it when the set is finished.

safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Smith machine close-grip bench press
steps: Place a flat bench in the middle of the smith machine. Lie back with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat. Grip the bar with your hands about shoulder width apart, and unhook it.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Press the bar back up to straight arms, keeping your elbows tucked, then rehook it when the set is finished.

safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Smith machine shoulder press
steps: Place an upright bench (90°) in the middle of the smith machine so the bar is in front of your face when you sit. Set the safety stops at about chin height.
Sit with your back against the pad and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width. Twist it to unhook it.
Press the bar straight up to a full lockout, then lower it under control to your chin or upper chest.
Rehook the bar when the set is finished.

commonMistakes: Lowering the bar behind the neck
safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Smith machine squat
steps: Set the bar at about upper-chest height and step under it so it rests across your upper back. Place your feet a little in front of the bar, shoulder width apart, toes slightly out.
Twist the bar to unhook it, brace your core and sit down, bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive up through your whole foot.
Rehook the bar when the set is finished.
formCues: Feet slightly in front of the bar

commonMistakes: Feet directly under the bar, which pushes the knees too far forward
safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Smith machine front squat
steps: Set the bar at about shoulder height. Step under it so it rests across the front of your shoulders, with your elbows pointing forward or your arms crossed. Place your feet slightly in front of the bar.
Unhook the bar, brace your core and sit down, keeping your torso upright.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive up.
Rehook the bar when the set is finished.

safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Smith machine split squat
steps: Set the bar at about upper-chest height and step under it, with the bar across your upper back. Take a long stride, one foot in front of the bar and one behind, back heel lifted.
Unhook the bar and lower your back knee straight down towards the floor, keeping your torso upright.
Press up through your front foot to the start. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Rehook the bar when the set is finished.

safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Smith machine hack squat
steps: Set the bar at about hip height. Stand with your back to the bar, your feet slightly in front of you, and hold the bar behind your thighs.
Unhook the bar and sit down, keeping your back upright and the bar against the back of your legs.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, then drive up.
Rehook the bar when the set is finished.

safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish
metadata.reviewNote: Rare; the hack squat machine is the normal tool. Reviewer to decide whether to keep this.

exercises.name: Smith machine calf raise
steps: Place a block or step under the bar with the balls of your feet on it, heels hanging off. Step under the bar so it rests across your upper back.
Unhook the bar and stand tall with your knees almost straight.
Lower your heels as far as comfortable, then rise onto your toes as high as you can, squeezing your calves at the top.
Rehook the bar when the set is finished.

safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Smith machine shrug
steps: Set the bar at about thigh height. Stand facing it and grip it with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, arms straight. Unhook it.
Keeping your arms straight, lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly. Rehook the bar when the set is finished.

safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Smith machine bent-over row
steps: Set the bar at about knee height. Stand facing it with your feet hip width apart, hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip the bar with an overhand grip just outside your knees. Unhook it.
Pull the bar up towards your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control to straight arms. Rehook the bar when the set is finished.

safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Smith machine hip thrust
steps: Set the bar low, at about the height of your hips when you sit on the floor. Sit with your upper back against a bench and roll the padded bar over your legs to your hip crease. Unhook it.
Plant your feet flat, hip width apart, knees bent so your shins are vertical at the top.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor, squeezing your glutes.
Lower under control, and rehook the bar when the set is finished.

commonMistakes: Feet too far or too close
safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish
Pad the bar

exercises.name: Smith machine Romanian deadlift
steps: Set the bar at about thigh height. Stand facing it, feet hip width apart, grip it with an overhand grip and unhook it. Keep your knees slightly bent.
Brace your core, keep your back flat and push your hips straight back, sliding the bar down your legs.
Lower until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand tall.
Rehook the bar when the set is finished.

safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before the set
Twist the bar to hook it back on the rungs when you finish

exercises.name: Leg press
steps: Adjust the seat so your knees are bent at about 90° when your feet are on the platform. Place your feet about shoulder width apart in the middle of the platform, toes slightly out, and sit with your back and hips firmly against the pad.
Release the safety handles and lower the platform under control until your knees are about 90°, keeping your lower back on the pad.
Press through your whole foot to extend your legs without locking your knees.
Re-engage the safety handles when the set is finished.
formCues: Lower back stays on the pad
Do not lock out the knees

commonMistakes: Lowering so far that the hips lift off the pad
Locking the knees at the top
Using too much weight with a short range
Placing hands on the knees to push
safety: Never lock your knees hard at the top
Always release and re-engage the safety handles
Stop before your lower back leaves the pad
metadata.reviewNote: Applies to both the 45° and horizontal seated leg press.

exercises.name: Leg press narrow stance
steps: Adjust the seat and sit with your back and hips firmly against the pad. Place your feet close together, about hip width apart, low on the platform.
Release the safety handles and lower the platform under control until your knees are about 90°.
Press through your whole foot to extend your legs without locking your knees.
Re-engage the safety handles when the set is finished.

safety: Never lock your knees hard
Use the safety handles

exercises.name: Leg press wide stance
steps: Adjust the seat and sit with your back and hips firmly against the pad. Place your feet wide, well past shoulder width, high on the platform, with your toes turned out.
Release the safety handles and lower the platform under control until your knees are about 90° and pointing over your toes.
Press through your whole foot, pushing your knees out, without locking them.
Re-engage the safety handles when the set is finished.

safety: Never lock your knees hard
Use the safety handles

exercises.name: Leg press high foot
steps: Adjust the seat and sit with your back and hips firmly against the pad. Place your feet high on the platform, about shoulder width apart.
Release the safety handles and lower the platform under control until your knees are bent at about 90°, or as far as you can without your hips lifting.
Press through your heels to extend your legs without locking your knees, squeezing your glutes.
formCues: Feet high, press through the heels

commonMistakes: Feet so high that the lower back rounds
safety: Stop before your lower back leaves the pad
Use the safety handles

exercises.name: Single-leg press
steps: Adjust the seat and sit with your back and hips firmly against the pad. Place one foot in the middle of the platform and keep the other foot off.
Release the safety handles and lower the platform under control until your knee is about 90°.
Press through your whole foot to extend your leg without locking the knee.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch. Re-engage the safety handles when finished.
formCues: Hips stay square and on the pad

safety: Use a lighter weight than your two-leg press
Use the safety handles

exercises.name: Leg press calf raise
steps: Sit in the leg press with your back and hips against the pad. Place the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform, with your heels hanging off.
Release the safety handles and press the platform up until your legs are straight but your knees are not locked.
Let your heels sink down to feel a deep calf stretch, then push through the balls of your feet to rise as high as you can.
Re-engage the safety handles when the set is finished.

commonMistakes: Bending the knees to heave the weight
safety: Never lock your knees hard
Make sure your feet cannot slip off the platform

exercises.name: Hack squat machine
steps: Step onto the platform and place your back and shoulders firmly against the pad, with your feet shoulder width apart a little in front of you on the platform. Position your shoulders under the shoulder pads.
Release the safety handles and lower under control by bending your knees until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Press through your whole foot to stand, without locking your knees.
Re-engage the safety handles when the set is finished.

commonMistakes: Locking the knees at the top
safety: Never lock your knees hard
Use the safety handles

exercises.name: Hack squat machine narrow stance
steps: Step onto the platform with your back against the pad and your feet close together, a little forward.
Release the safety handles and lower under control until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Press through your whole foot to stand without locking your knees.
Re-engage the safety handles when the set is finished.

safety: Never lock your knees hard

exercises.name: Hack squat machine high foot
steps: Step onto the platform with your back against the pad and your feet placed high on the platform, shoulder width apart.
Release the safety handles and lower under control until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Press through your heels to stand without locking your knees, squeezing your glutes.
formCues: Feet high, press through the heels

safety: Use the safety handles

exercises.name: Leg extension
steps: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot and the pad rests on the front of your lower shins, just above your ankles. Hold the handles.
Extend your legs to straighten your knees, squeezing your quads at the top.
