Pause briefly, then lower slowly until your knees are bent at about 90°.
formCues: Squeeze the quads at the top

safety: Do not use a very heavy weight with a jerky motion
Stop if your knees hurt

exercises.name: Single-leg extension
steps: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot and the pad rests on one shin, just above the ankle. Hold the handles.
Extend that leg to straighten the knee, squeezing your quad at the top.
Lower slowly. Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.
formCues: Squeeze the quad at the top

safety: Use a lighter weight than for two legs

exercises.name: Lying leg curl
steps: Lie face down on the machine with the pad resting on the back of your lower legs, just above your heels. Your knees should be just off the end of the bench. Hold the handles.
Curl your heels up towards your glutes by bending your knees, keeping your hips pressed to the bench.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a weight you can control
Stop if you feel cramping or pain behind the knee

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
steps: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and the pad on the back of your lower legs, just above your heels. Lower the thigh pad over your thighs.
Curl your heels down and back by bending your knees, squeezing your hamstrings.
Pause, then return slowly until your legs are almost straight.

commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the seat
safety: Adjust the thigh pad so it holds your legs firmly

exercises.name: Single-leg lying curl
steps: Lie face down on the machine with the pad on the back of one lower leg, just above the heel. Hold the handles.
Curl your heel up towards your glute by bending your knee, keeping your hips pressed to the bench.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly. Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.

safety: Use a lighter weight than for two legs

exercises.name: Seated hip abduction
steps: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and the outer pads against the outside of your knees. Set the range so you start with your legs together or slightly apart.
Press your legs apart, pushing your knees out against the pads as far as is comfortable.
Pause, then return slowly under control.

safety: Use a weight you can control
Set the range to your comfort

exercises.name: Seated hip abduction with a forward lean
steps: Sit on the abductor machine with the pads against the outside of your knees. Lean your torso forward slightly and hold the handles.
Press your legs apart against the pads, squeezing your glutes.
Pause, then return slowly.

safety: Set the range to your comfort

exercises.name: Seated hip adduction
steps: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and the pads on the inside of your knees. Set the range so you start with your legs apart at a comfortable width.
Squeeze your legs together, bringing your knees towards each other.
Pause, then return slowly under control.

commonMistakes: Starting with the legs too wide
safety: Set the range to your comfort — do not force a wide starting position

exercises.name: Machine standing calf raise
steps: Position your shoulders under the pads of the machine, with the balls of your feet on the platform edge and your heels hanging off. Stand tall with your knees almost straight.
Lower your heels as far as comfortable for a deep calf stretch.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can, squeeze your calves at the top, and lower slowly.

safety: Use a weight you can control

exercises.name: Machine seated calf raise
steps: Sit on the machine with the balls of your feet on the platform and your knees under the pad, bent at about 90°. Release the safety handle.
Lower your heels as far as comfortable for a deep stretch.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can, squeeze your calves at the top, and lower slowly.

safety: Make sure the pad is secure on your thighs

exercises.name: Machine single-leg calf raise
steps: Set up on the standing calf raise machine with one foot on the platform edge, keeping the other foot off the platform, and hold the handles for balance.
Lower your heel for a deep stretch.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can, squeeze at the top, and lower slowly. Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.

safety: Use a lighter weight than for two legs

exercises.name: Machine chest press
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are level with your mid-chest. Sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet flat on the floor, and grip the handles.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down, brace your core and press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Squeeze your chest at the end, then return slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
formCues: Back and head on the pad

commonMistakes: Seat too high or too low
Lifting the hips or back off the pad
safety: Use a weight you can control
Adjust the seat to your height before starting
metadata.reviewNote: Covers both selectorised and plate-loaded chest press machines.

exercises.name: Machine incline chest press
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are level with your upper chest. Sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet flat on the floor, and grip the handles.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down and press the handles up and forward until your arms are almost straight.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly.

safety: Adjust the seat before starting

exercises.name: Machine decline chest press
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are level with your lower chest. Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles.
Pull your shoulder blades back and press the handles forward and slightly down until your arms are almost straight.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly.

safety: Adjust the seat before starting
metadata.reviewNote: Not found in many Indian gyms; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Machine single-arm chest press
steps: On a machine with independent arms, sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet flat. Grip one handle and keep the other arm resting.
Press the handle forward until your arm is almost straight, without letting your torso twist.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Adjust the seat before starting

exercises.name: Pec deck fly
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at about chest height and your upper arms are roughly level with the pads. Sit with your back flat against the pad and grip the handles or rest your forearms on the pads.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down, and bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly until you feel a stretch, without letting the weights touch down.
formCues: Squeeze the chest at the centre

safety: Do not let your arms go back too far behind your shoulders
Use a weight you can control

exercises.name: Pec deck rear delt fly
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at about shoulder height. Sit facing the pad with your chest against it and grip the handles with your arms out in front of you.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, pull the handles out and back in a wide arc until your arms are in line with your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause, then return slowly.

safety: Use a light weight
Do not force your arms back past your shoulders

exercises.name: Pec deck single-arm fly
steps: Set up on a pec deck with your back flat against the pad. Grip one handle and keep the other arm resting.
Bring the handle across in a wide arc in front of your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a lighter weight than for two arms

exercises.name: Machine shoulder press
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at about shoulder height when you sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet flat on the floor. Grip the handles.
Brace your core and press the handles straight up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly under control until the handles are back at shoulder height.

commonMistakes: Seat set too low or too high
safety: Adjust the seat before starting
Skip it if you have shoulder pain overhead

exercises.name: Machine single-arm shoulder press
steps: On a machine with independent arms, sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet flat. Grip one handle at shoulder height and keep the other arm resting.
Press the handle straight up until your arm is almost straight, without leaning to the side.
Lower slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Adjust the seat before starting

exercises.name: Machine lateral raise
steps: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot. Sit with your back against the pad and place your forearms or the backs of your elbows against the pads.
Raise your arms out to the sides by pushing your elbows up, until they are about level with your shoulders.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a light weight

exercises.name: Machine seated row
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at about chest height and the chest pad is against your upper chest or stomach. Sit tall with your arms straight and grip the handles.
Pull the handles back towards your torso, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause, then return slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your chest on the pad.

commonMistakes: Rounding the shoulders forward at the end
safety: Adjust the chest pad before starting
metadata.reviewNote: Covers selectorised and plate-loaded chest-supported row machines.

exercises.name: Machine low row
steps: Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet on the platform. Grip the lower handles with your arms straight.
Pull the handles towards your hips, driving your elbows back and close to your body.
Squeeze your lats, then return slowly until your arms are straight.

safety: Adjust the seat and chest pad before starting

exercises.name: Machine high row
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are above your head when your arms are extended. Sit with your chest against the pad and grip the handles.
Pull the handles down and back towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your lats, then return slowly until your arms are straight above you.

safety: Adjust the seat before starting

exercises.name: Machine T-bar row
steps: Stand on the platform of a T-bar row machine and lean your chest against the pad, or stand over a plate-loaded T-bar with a flat back. Grip the handles with your arms straight.
Pull the handles towards your chest or lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control to straight arms.
formCues: Chest on the pad or back flat

safety: Keep your back flat
metadata.reviewNote: The barbell/landmine T-bar row already exists in the barbell batch.

exercises.name: Machine single-arm row
steps: On a row machine with independent arms, sit with your chest against the pad and grip one handle with your arm straight.
Pull the handle back, driving your elbow past your torso, without twisting.
Squeeze your lat, then return slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Adjust the seat before starting

exercises.name: Machine lat pulldown
steps: Adjust the seat and thigh pad so you are held firmly. Grip the handles with a wide overhand or neutral grip, arms straight above you.
Lean back slightly, lift your chest and pull the handles down towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your lats, then return slowly until your arms are straight.

safety: Adjust the thigh pad before starting
metadata.reviewNote: A separate machine from the cable lat pulldown station; many Indian gyms only have the cable version, in the cable batch.

exercises.name: Pullover machine
steps: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot. Sit with your back against the pad, place your elbows on the pads and grip the bar or handles.
Push your elbows down and forward in an arc, bringing the bar towards your hips and squeezing your lats.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch.

safety: Adjust the seat before starting
metadata.reviewNote: Less common in Indian gyms.

exercises.name: Assisted pull-up
steps: Choose an assist weight (more weight means more help). Kneel or stand on the platform, and grip the handles with an overhand grip, wider than shoulder width.
Hang with straight arms, then pull your chest up towards the bar, driving your elbows down and back.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms.

commonMistakes: Using too much assistance and never progressing
safety: Reduce the assist weight over time
Do not drop quickly at the bottom

exercises.name: Assisted chin-up
steps: Choose an assist weight. Kneel or stand on the platform, and grip the handles with an underhand grip, shoulder width apart.
Hang with straight arms, then pull your chin up over the handles, driving your elbows down.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms.

safety: Reduce the assist weight over time

exercises.name: Assisted dip
steps: Choose an assist weight. Kneel on the platform and grip the dip handles with straight arms, leaning slightly forward.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
formCues: Lower until the upper arms are parallel

safety: Do not go lower than comfortable
Reduce the assist weight over time

exercises.name: Machine seated dip
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at about waist height. Sit with your back against the pad, and grip the handles with your elbows close to your body.
Press the handles down until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly under control.

safety: Adjust the seat before starting

exercises.name: Machine triceps extension
steps: Adjust the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot. Sit with your back against the pad and place your upper arms on the pads, gripping the handles.
Extend your elbows to push the handles down or forward until your arms are almost straight.
Squeeze your triceps, then return slowly.
formCues: Upper arms stay on the pad

safety: Adjust the seat before starting

exercises.name: Machine biceps curl
steps: Adjust the seat so your armpits rest on top of the pad and your elbows line up with the machine's pivot. Grip the handles with an underhand grip, arms nearly straight.
Curl the handles up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms on the pad.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.
formCues: Upper arms stay on the pad

safety: Adjust the seat before starting

exercises.name: Machine ab crunch
steps: Adjust the seat so the pads or handles sit at about chest height and the pivot lines up with your lower ribs. Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles or rest your arms on the pads.
Brace your core and curl your torso forward by contracting your abs, bringing your ribs towards your pelvis.
Squeeze at the bottom, then return slowly under control.
formCues: Curl the ribs towards the pelvis
Do not pull with the arms

commonMistakes: Pulling with the arms or hip flexors
safety: Adjust the seat before starting
Skip it with lower back pain

exercises.name: Machine torso rotation
steps: Sit on the machine with your hips and thighs secured by the pads and your chest against the chest pad. Set the machine to a comfortable starting angle.
Brace your core and rotate your torso to one side as far as is comfortable, keeping your hips still.
Return slowly through the middle to the other side, or complete all reps on one side then switch.

safety: Use a light weight
Set the starting angle to your comfort
metadata.reviewNote: Controversial for lower-back loading; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Machine back extension
steps: Adjust the pad so it sits just below your hips and your heels are locked under the roller. Cross your arms over your chest or hold them behind your head.
Keeping your back neutral, lower your torso until it is about 90° to your legs.
Squeeze your glutes and lower back to raise your torso until your body is in a straight line. Do not arch beyond a straight line.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Do not arch past a straight line
Do not do it with lower back pain
metadata.reviewNote: Covers both the 45° bench and the 90° Roman chair.

exercises.name: Reverse hyperextension
steps: Lie face down on the machine with your hips at the edge of the pad and your legs hanging down. Grip the handles.
Keeping your legs straight, squeeze your glutes to swing your legs up until they are in line with your torso.
Pause, then lower slowly under control.
formCues: Lift to the torso line, no higher

safety: Use a light weight
Skip it with lower back pain
metadata.reviewNote: Less common in Indian gyms.

exercises.name: Machine glute kickback
steps: Stand facing the machine with your chest against the pad and the pad against the back of one lower leg or heel. Hold the handles.
Press your leg back and slightly up by squeezing your glute, keeping your hips square.
Squeeze at the top without arching your lower back, then return slowly.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.
formCues: Do not arch the lower back

safety: Use a weight you can control

exercises.name: Machine hip thrust
steps: Sit on the machine with your upper back against the pad and the belt or pad across your hips. Plant your feet flat on the platform, hip width apart.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Adjust the pad and belt before starting

exercises.name: Treadmill walk
steps: Stand on the side rails, start the belt at a slow speed, then step onto it with your feet shoulder width apart.
Walk with your head up, shoulders back and arms swinging naturally, without holding the handrails.
Increase the speed to a brisk but comfortable pace and keep it steady for the planned time.
Slow the belt gradually at the end for a cool-down before stepping off.

commonMistakes: Starting at too high a speed
safety: Clip the safety key to your clothing
Straddle the belt when starting
Do not step off a moving belt

exercises.name: Treadmill incline walk
steps: Start the treadmill at a slow walk. Set the incline to a moderate level, about 5–12%.
Walk with your torso upright, your head up and your arms swinging naturally, without holding the handrails.
Keep a steady pace and increase the incline gradually as you feel comfortable.
Lower the incline and slow the belt for a cool-down before stepping off.

commonMistakes: Holding the rails and leaning back
safety: Clip the safety key to your clothing
Build up the incline gradually

exercises.name: Treadmill run
steps: Start with a 5-minute walk to warm up. Gradually increase the speed to a comfortable jog.
Run with your torso upright, your head up, relaxed shoulders and your arms swinging at 90°, landing with your feet under your hips.
Keep a steady pace, or alternate faster and slower intervals as planned.
Slow to a walk for a cool-down at the end before stepping off.

safety: Clip the safety key to your clothing
Warm up first
Do not step off a moving belt

exercises.name: Elliptical trainer
steps: Step onto the pedals, holding the handles, with your feet flat and your torso upright.
Start moving in a smooth, circular stride, pushing and pulling the handles in rhythm with your legs.
Keep your posture tall, your core braced and your shoulders relaxed, at a steady resistance and pace.
Slow down for a cool-down before stepping off.
formCues: Do not lean on the handles

commonMistakes: Setting the resistance too light so the legs just spin
safety: Hold the handles when stepping on and off

exercises.name: Upright stationary bike
steps: Adjust the seat so your knee is slightly bent when the pedal is at its lowest point. Sit tall and hold the handlebars lightly.
Start pedalling at an easy pace to warm up, with your feet flat on the pedals.
Increase the resistance and speed to a steady pace, keeping your back straight and your core braced.
Slow down and lower the resistance for a cool-down at the end.

commonMistakes: Seat too low or too high
safety: Adjust the seat before starting
Do not stand up on a fast spinning flywheel

exercises.name: Recumbent stationary bike
steps: Adjust the seat so your knee is slightly bent when the pedal is at its furthest point. Sit back with your back against the pad.
Start pedalling at an easy pace, with your feet secured in the straps.
Increase the resistance and speed to a steady pace, keeping your back against the pad.
Slow down and lower the resistance for a cool-down.

commonMistakes: Seat too close or too far
safety: Adjust the seat before starting

exercises.name: Spin bike intervals
steps: Adjust the seat and handlebars so you are comfortable with a slight bend in your knees at the bottom of the pedal stroke. Clip or strap your feet in.
Warm up for 5 minutes at an easy pace and light resistance.
Alternate harder efforts (heavier resistance or faster cadence) with recovery periods at an easy pace, as planned.
Cool down for 5 minutes at an easy pace before stopping.

safety: Set up the bike before starting
Stop if you feel dizzy

exercises.name: Rowing machine
steps: Sit on the seat with your feet strapped in, your knees bent and your arms straight, holding the handle. Your shins should be vertical and your back tall.
Drive with your legs first, then lean back slightly and pull the handle to your lower ribs, with your elbows going back.
Return in the reverse order: straighten your arms, lean your torso forward, then bend your knees to slide forward.
Keep a steady rhythm — legs, body, arms on the way out; arms, body, legs on the way back.
formCues: Legs first, then back, then arms

safety: Keep your back flat
Learn the sequence at a light pace first

exercises.name: Stair climber
steps: Step onto the stair climber, holding the side rails lightly, with your feet flat on the steps and your torso upright.
Start at a slow speed and step steadily, pushing through your heels.
Keep your posture tall, your core braced and your weight on your legs, not on your arms.
Slow down for a cool-down before stepping off.
formCues: Weight on the legs, light touch on the rails

safety: Hold the rails when stepping on and off
Start slowly

exercises.name: Air bike
steps: Adjust the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke. Sit tall and grip the moving handles.
Start pedalling at an easy pace, pushing and pulling the handles in rhythm with your legs.
Increase the effort for the planned intervals — the harder you push, the more resistance the fan gives.
Slow down gradually for a cool-down at the end.
formCues: Push and pull with the arms in rhythm

safety: Warm up first
Stop if you feel dizzy
Use intervals, not endless maximum effort

exercises.name: Push-up
steps: Start in a plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width, directly under or just outside your shoulders, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them about 45° from your body.
Stop when your chest is just above the floor, then press the floor away to return to straight arms.
Keep your body in one straight line throughout.
formCues: Chest to the floor, full range

safety: Stop if you feel wrist or shoulder pain
Drop to your knees if you cannot keep a straight body

exercises.name: Knee push-up
steps: Kneel on a mat with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width and your body in a straight line from head to knees.
Brace your core. Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows about 45° from your body.
Press back up to straight arms, keeping the line from head to knees.
formCues: Straight line from head to knees

safety: Progress to full push-ups as you get stronger
metadata.reviewNote: Common beginner regression; keep the label neutral rather than 'girl push-up' in the UI.

exercises.name: Incline push-up
steps: Place your hands on a stable bench, step or counter, slightly wider than shoulder width, with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and lower your chest to the edge of the surface, keeping your elbows about 45° from your body.
Press back up to straight arms.
formCues: Straight line from head to heels

safety: Use a stable surface that will not slide

exercises.name: Decline push-up
steps: Place your feet on a stable bench or step and your hands on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder width, with your body in a straight line.
Brace your core and lower your chest towards the floor, elbows about 45° from your body.
Press back up to straight arms.

safety: Use a stable bench

exercises.name: Wide push-up
steps: Start in a plank with your hands about 1.5 times shoulder width apart and your body in a straight line.
Brace your core and lower your chest towards the floor, letting your elbows flare out a little more than a standard push-up.
Press back up to straight arms.

safety: Stop if you feel shoulder pinching

exercises.name: Archer push-up
steps: Start in a wide push-up position with your hands about twice shoulder width apart.
Shift your weight to one side, bending that elbow and lowering your chest towards that hand while the other arm stays straight.
Press back up to the centre, then repeat on the other side.

safety: Build up with wide push-ups first

exercises.name: Clap push-up
steps: Start in a standard push-up position with your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest towards the floor, then push up explosively so your hands leave the floor.
Clap quickly and land with soft, slightly bent elbows, then go straight into the next rep.

safety: Master the push-up first
Land with soft elbows to protect your wrists

exercises.name: Hindu push-up (dand)
steps: Start in a pike position with your hands shoulder width apart, hips high, legs straight and feet about shoulder width apart, forming an inverted V.
Bend your elbows and swoop your chest down and forward, close to the floor, in a smooth arc between your hands.
Continue the arc up into an upward-facing dog position, with your arms straight, hips low and chest up.
Reverse the movement by pushing your hips back and up to return to the starting pike. That is one rep.

commonMistakes: Overarching the lower back at the top
safety: Warm up the shoulders and wrists
Keep the arch gentle if your lower back is sensitive
metadata.reviewNote: A traditional Indian wrestling exercise. Reviewer to decide the target (chest, shoulders or full upper body).

exercises.name: Dive-bomber push-up
steps: Start in a pike position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width and your hips high.
Swoop your head and chest down towards the floor between your hands, then forward and up into a cobra position, with your hips low and arms straight.
Reverse the path by pushing your hips back and up to the pike position.

safety: Learn the Hindu push-up first
metadata.reviewNote: A harder variation of the Hindu push-up.

exercises.name: Scapular push-up
steps: Start in a high plank with your arms straight and your hands shoulder width apart.
Keeping your arms straight, let your chest sink between your shoulder blades by squeezing them together.
Push the floor away and round your upper back slightly, spreading your shoulder blades wide apart, to return to the top.
formCues: Shoulder blades move, not the elbows

safety: Keep the movement small and controlled

exercises.name: Chest dip
steps: Hold a pair of parallel bars with straight arms, lean your torso forward about 30° and cross your ankles behind you.
Bend your elbows to lower your body, letting your elbows flare slightly, until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up to straight arms, keeping the forward lean.
formCues: Lower until the upper arms are parallel

safety: Do not drop below parallel
Skip it if your shoulders hurt

exercises.name: Pike push-up
steps: Start in a downward-facing dog position with your hands shoulder width apart, hips high and legs straight.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head towards the floor between your hands.
Press the floor away to return to straight arms, keeping your hips high.

commonMistakes: Hips dropping so it becomes a push-up
safety: Stop if you feel wrist or neck strain

exercises.name: Feet-elevated pike push-up
steps: Place your feet on a stable bench or box and your hands on the floor, hips high, in a pike position.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head towards the floor between your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.

safety: Master the pike push-up first

exercises.name: Wall handstand push-up
steps: Kick up into a handstand facing the wall with your hands shoulder width apart and your heels against the wall, or place your feet on the wall in a pike.
Bend your elbows to lower your head to the floor, keeping your core braced.
Press back up to straight arms.

safety: Use a mat under your head
Only attempt it after mastering pike push-ups
Have a spotter when learning
metadata.reviewNote: Advanced; reviewer to decide whether it belongs in a general library.

exercises.name: Prone Y raise
steps: Lie face down on a mat with your arms extended overhead in a Y shape and your thumbs pointing up.
Lift your arms and chest slightly off the floor by squeezing your upper back and shoulders.
Hold for a moment, then lower slowly.

safety: Keep the lift small
Skip it if your lower back hurts

exercises.name: Prone T raise
steps: Lie face down on a mat with your arms straight out to the sides in a T shape and your thumbs pointing up.
Lift your arms off the floor by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold for a moment, then lower slowly.

safety: Keep the movement small

exercises.name: Diamond push-up
steps: Start in a plank with your hands together under your chest, forming a diamond with your thumbs and index fingers, and your body in a straight line.
Brace your core and lower your chest to your hands, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Press back up to straight arms.

safety: Stop if your wrists hurt — place your hands slightly wider

exercises.name: Bench dip
steps: Sit on the edge of a stable bench and place your hands on the edge beside your hips, fingers pointing forward. Slide your hips off the bench with your legs out in front of you.
Bend your elbows to lower your body, keeping your back close to the bench, until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
formCues: Lower until the upper arms are parallel

commonMistakes: Hips drifting far from the bench
safety: Do not go lower than parallel
Use a stable bench
Skip it with shoulder pain

exercises.name: Feet-elevated bench dip
steps: Place your hands on the edge of a stable bench behind you and your heels on another bench or a box in front of you, legs straight.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
formCues: Lower until the upper arms are parallel

safety: Do not go lower than parallel
Use stable supports

exercises.name: Parallel bar dip
steps: Hold a pair of parallel bars with straight arms, keep your torso upright and cross your ankles behind you.
Bend your elbows to lower your body, keeping your elbows close to your body, until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
formCues: Lower until the upper arms are parallel

safety: Do not drop below parallel
Skip it if your shoulders hurt

exercises.name: Bodyweight triceps extension
steps: Place your hands on a bar or a sturdy table edge at about waist height and walk your feet back until your body is at an angle, with your arms straight.
Bend your elbows to lower your forehead towards the bar, keeping your upper arms still.
Extend your elbows to press back up.

safety: Use a stable bar or table

exercises.name: Pull-up
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, arms straight and shoulders engaged.
Pull your chest towards the bar by driving your elbows down and back, until your chin is over the bar.
Pause at the top, then lower under control to straight arms.
formCues: Start from a full hang with the shoulders engaged

safety: Use an assisted version or negatives if you cannot do one yet
Stop if your shoulders hurt

exercises.name: Chin-up
steps: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip about shoulder width apart, arms straight.
Pull your chin over the bar by driving your elbows down and into your sides.
Pause at the top, then lower under control to straight arms.
formCues: Full hang to chin over the bar

safety: Use an assisted version or negatives if needed

exercises.name: Neutral-grip pull-up
steps: Hang from parallel handles with your palms facing each other and your arms straight.
Pull your chest towards the handles by driving your elbows down and back.
Pause at the top, then lower under control.

safety: Use an assisted version if needed

exercises.name: Negative pull-up
steps: Step or jump up so your chin is over a pull-up bar, holding it with an overhand grip.
Lower yourself as slowly as you can, taking 3–5 seconds, until your arms are straight.
Step back up and repeat.

safety: Use a box or step for the start position
metadata.reviewNote: A progression for people who cannot yet do a full pull-up.

exercises.name: Archer pull-up
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with a very wide overhand grip.
Pull your chest up towards one hand, keeping the other arm straight out to the side.
Lower under control, then repeat to the other side.

safety: Build up with standard pull-ups first

exercises.name: Muscle-up
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Pull explosively, driving your chest up past the bar and leaning your torso forward over it.
Transition your wrists over the bar and press up to straight arms, with the bar at your waist.
Lower under control by reversing the movement.

safety: Master strict pull-ups and dips first
Use a bar that is high enough
metadata.reviewNote: Advanced calisthenics; reviewer to decide whether it belongs.

exercises.name: Inverted row
steps: Set a bar at about waist height in a rack or smith machine, or use a sturdy table. Lie underneath it and grip it with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder width, arms straight, with your heels on the floor and your body in a straight line.
Pull your chest up to the bar by driving your elbows back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control to straight arms, keeping your body in a straight line.

safety: Use a stable bar or table
Bend your knees to make it easier
metadata.equipmentNeeded: bar at waist height, or sturdy table

exercises.name: Feet-elevated inverted row
steps: Set a bar at about waist height and place your feet on a bench. Lie under the bar and grip it with an overhand grip, with your body in a straight line.
Pull your chest up to the bar by driving your elbows back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control to straight arms.

safety: Use a stable bar and bench
metadata.equipmentNeeded: bar at waist height and a bench

exercises.name: Scapular pull-up
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, arms straight and shoulders relaxed up by your ears.
Keeping your arms straight, pull your shoulder blades down and together, lifting your body slightly.
Pause, then relax back to a full hang.

safety: Keep the movement small and controlled

exercises.name: Superman
steps: Lie face down on a mat with your arms stretched out in front of you and your legs straight.
Lift your arms, chest and legs slightly off the floor by squeezing your lower back and glutes.
Hold for a moment, then lower slowly.
formCues: Lift with the glutes and back

safety: Keep the lift small
Skip it if your lower back hurts

exercises.name: Bird dog
steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, back flat.
Brace your core and extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back, keeping your hips and shoulders level.
Hold for a moment, then return and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Reach long, do not lift high

safety: Keep the back flat
Use a mat under your knees

exercises.name: Bodyweight good morning
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart and your hands behind your head or across your chest, knees slightly bent.
Push your hips straight back and lean your torso forward with a flat back until it is about parallel to the floor.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Stop if your lower back rounds

exercises.name: Dead hang
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart, arms straight.
Let your body hang with your shoulders relaxed, or gently engaged if instructed.
Hold for the planned time, then step down.

safety: Step down carefully
Skip it with shoulder pain

exercises.name: Bodyweight squat
steps: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and your toes turned out slightly, arms out in front of you for balance.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and sit down and back, bending your knees and hips together.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, with your heels down and your knees over your toes.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.

safety: Stop if your knees hurt
Reduce the depth if your heels lift

exercises.name: Hindu squat (baithak)
steps: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Swing your arms back as you rise onto your toes and sit down, bending your knees and keeping your heels off the floor, until your hamstrings touch your calves or you reach your comfortable depth.
Swing your arms forward and stand up, driving through the balls of your feet, to the starting position.
Move in a smooth rhythm, with your torso upright.

commonMistakes: Going deeper than your knees can handle
safety: Warm up the ankles and knees
Skip it or reduce the depth if you have knee pain
metadata.reviewNote: A traditional Indian wrestling exercise, done in high reps. Reviewer to confirm the form and heel position.

exercises.name: Wall sit
steps: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet about two feet in front of you, shoulder width apart.
Slide down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor and your knees are bent at about 90°.
Hold the position with your back flat against the wall and your weight on your heels, for the planned time.

safety: Stop if your knees hurt

exercises.name: Jump squat
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. Sit into a squat with your chest up.
Explode upwards, jumping as high as you can, with your arms swinging up for momentum.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, bending your knees to absorb the impact, and go straight into the next squat.

safety: Land softly
Skip it with knee, ankle or lower-back problems

exercises.name: Box jump
steps: Stand in front of a sturdy box, with your feet shoulder width apart.
Swing your arms back, dip into a quarter squat, then explode up, swinging your arms forward and jumping onto the box.
Land softly with both feet fully on the box, knees bent, then stand tall.
Step back down, rather than jumping down, and reset.

commonMistakes: Using a box that is too high
safety: Use a stable box
Choose a height you can land on comfortably
Step down rather than jump down

exercises.name: Bodyweight split squat
steps: Stand with one foot a long stride in front of the other and your back heel lifted, hands on your hips.
Bend both knees and lower your back knee straight down towards the floor, keeping your torso upright.
Press up through your front foot to the start.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Hold a wall or rail for balance if needed

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
steps: Stand about two feet in front of a bench and place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Bend your front knee and lower your hips straight down until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor, torso upright.
Press up through your front foot to the start.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

commonMistakes: Standing too close to the bench
safety: Use a stable bench

exercises.name: Forward lunge
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your hands on your hips.
Step forward into a long stride and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Push back through your front foot to return to the start.
Alternate legs.

safety: Hold a wall for balance if needed

exercises.name: Reverse lunge
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your hands on your hips.
Step back with one foot, landing on the ball of the foot, and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Drive through your front foot to stand and bring your back foot forward.
Alternate legs.

safety: Make sure there is space behind you

exercises.name: Walking lunge
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart, hands on your hips, in a clear space.
Step forward into a long stride and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Push through your front foot and bring your back foot forward to the next stride.
Alternate legs.

safety: Make sure there is a clear path

exercises.name: Bodyweight step-up
steps: Stand facing a stable box or bench at about knee height.
Place one foot fully on the box and press through that heel to step up, bringing your other foot beside it.
Stand tall, then step back down with control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

commonMistakes: Using a box that is too high
safety: Use a stable box

exercises.name: Sissy squat
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart, holding a support with one hand for balance.
Rise onto your toes and lean your torso back as you bend your knees forward and down, keeping your hips extended and a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Lower as far as is comfortable, then drive your knees back and return to standing.
formCues: Straight line from knees to shoulders

safety: Hold a support
Skip it if you have knee problems
metadata.reviewNote: High knee stress; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Pistol squat
steps: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended in front of you and your arms out in front for balance.
Sit down on your standing leg, keeping your heel flat and your chest up, lowering as far as you can.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.

safety: Hold a support or sit onto a box until you build strength
Skip it if you have knee pain

exercises.name: Glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, hip width apart, arms by your sides.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Skip the high lift if your lower back hurts

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and one foot flat, with the other leg extended or held towards your chest.
Brace your core and drive through the heel of your planted foot to lift your hips until your body is in a straight line.
Squeeze your glute at the top, keeping your hips level, then lower under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop or rotate
safety: Start with two-leg bridges

exercises.name: Bodyweight hip thrust
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the long edge of a stable bench and your knees bent, feet flat.
Brace your core, tuck your chin and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.

commonMistakes: Feet too far or too close
safety: Use a stable bench

exercises.name: Single-leg hip thrust
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a stable bench, one foot flat and the other leg extended or held towards your chest.
Brace your core and drive through the heel of your planted foot to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glute at the top, keeping your hips level, then lower under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a stable bench

exercises.name: Donkey kick
steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, back flat.
Brace your core and kick one leg back and up with your knee bent at 90°, squeezing your glute, until your thigh is in line with your back.
Lower under control and repeat. Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.
formCues: Squeeze the glute at the top
Do not arch the lower back

safety: Use a mat under your knees

exercises.name: Curtsy lunge
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your hands on your hips.
Step one foot back and across behind your other leg, as if curtsying, and lower until both knees are bent at about 90°.
Keep your torso upright and your hips square to the front.
Drive through your front foot to return to the start. Alternate legs.

safety: Hold a wall for balance if needed

exercises.name: Bodyweight single-leg Romanian deadlift
steps: Stand on one foot with a slight bend in the knee, hands in front of you or on your hips.
Brace your core and hinge forward at the hip while your free leg extends straight back behind you.
Lower until your torso is about parallel to the floor, keeping your hips square.
Drive through your standing heel to stand tall. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Free leg and torso move as one

safety: Hold a wall or rail for balance if needed

exercises.name: Nordic hamstring curl
steps: Kneel on a mat with your ankles anchored under a sturdy support or held by a partner, with your body in a straight line from knees to head.
Keeping your hips extended, lower your torso towards the floor as slowly as you can, controlling the descent with your hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the start.
formCues: Use hands to push back up

safety: Use a mat
Build up with short ranges first
metadata.equipmentNeeded: mat and a secure anchor or partner

exercises.name: Slider hamstring curl
steps: Lie on your back with your heels on sliders, towels on a smooth floor or a stable bench, knees bent, and your hips lifted in a bridge.
Keeping your hips lifted, slide your heels away from you until your legs are almost straight.
Pull your heels back in by bending your knees, keeping your hips up.

safety: Use a smooth floor and a mat for grip under your shoulders

exercises.name: Cossack squat
steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder width apart, arms out in front of you.
Shift your weight to one side and sit down over that leg, keeping the other leg straight with its toes pointing up.
Lower as far as you comfortably can, then push through the bent leg to return to the centre.
Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Straight leg stays straight, toes up

safety: Move within your range

exercises.name: Lateral lunge
steps: Stand tall with your feet together and your hands in front of your chest.
Step out wide to one side and sit your hips back and down over that leg, keeping the other leg straight and both feet flat and pointing forward.
Lower until your thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Push through the bent leg to return. Alternate sides.

safety: Stop if you feel groin pain

exercises.name: Sumo squat
steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder width apart, toes turned out 30–45°, hands clasped in front of your chest.
Bend your knees and hips, sitting straight down and pushing your knees out over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, chest up.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.

safety: Warm up the hips and adductors first

exercises.name: Side-lying hip adduction
steps: Lie on your side with your bottom leg straight and your top leg crossed over, with the foot of the top leg flat on the floor in front of the bottom knee.
Lift your bottom leg straight up as high as is comfortable, squeezing your inner thigh.
Lower slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a mat

exercises.name: Fire hydrant
steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, back flat.
Keeping your knee bent at 90°, lift one knee out to the side, as high as you comfortably can, without rotating your torso.
Lower slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a mat under your knees

exercises.name: Side-lying leg raise
steps: Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked, supporting your head with your lower arm.
Keeping your toes pointing forward, lift your top leg up towards the ceiling, leading with your heel, without rolling your hips back.
Lower slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a mat

exercises.name: Clamshell
steps: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent at about 45° and your feet together, supporting your head.
Keeping your feet together, open your top knee up like a clamshell without rolling your hips back.
Lower slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a mat

exercises.name: Bodyweight calf raise
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart, the balls of your feet on the floor or on the edge of a step, holding a wall for balance.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can and squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower slowly until your heels are below the step or touch the floor.

safety: Hold a support for balance

exercises.name: Single-leg calf raise
steps: Stand on one foot with the ball of your foot on the edge of a step, holding a wall for balance.
Lower your heel below the step for a deep stretch.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can and squeeze your calf at the top, then lower slowly.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.

safety: Hold a support for balance

exercises.name: Crunch
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, hands lightly behind your head or across your chest.
Brace your core and curl your upper back off the floor by bringing your ribs towards your pelvis.
Squeeze your abs at the top, then lower slowly.
formCues: Curl the ribs towards the pelvis
Lower back stays on the floor
Do not pull on the neck

safety: Keep your neck relaxed
Skip it with neck pain

exercises.name: Bicycle crunch
steps: Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head and your legs lifted, knees bent at 90°.
Brace your core and bring one elbow towards the opposite knee while extending the other leg straight.
Switch sides in a smooth pedalling motion, keeping your lower back on the floor.
formCues: Rotate the shoulder, not just the elbow

safety: Keep your neck relaxed

exercises.name: Reverse crunch
steps: Lie on your back with your hands by your sides and your knees bent at 90°, lifted over your hips.
Brace your core and curl your hips up off the floor, bringing your knees towards your chest.
Lower slowly until your tailbone touches the floor.

safety: Skip it with lower back pain

exercises.name: Sit-up
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat or anchored, arms crossed over your chest.
Brace your core and curl your torso up until you are sitting upright.
Lower slowly back to the floor.
formCues: Curl up, do not yank with the neck

safety: Skip it with lower back pain

exercises.name: V-up
steps: Lie on your back with your arms stretched overhead and your legs straight.
Brace your core and lift your arms and legs together, reaching your hands towards your toes in a V shape.
Lower slowly with control.

safety: Skip it with lower back pain

exercises.name: Lying leg raise
steps: Lie on your back with your hands under your hips and your legs straight.
Brace your core, keep your lower back pressed to the floor and lift your legs up until they are vertical.
Lower slowly, stopping just above the floor.
formCues: Lower back stays on the floor

safety: Bend your knees if your back arches
Skip it with lower back pain

exercises.name: Hanging knee raise
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar, or support yourself on a captain's chair with your forearms on the pads, with your legs straight down.
Brace your core and curl your knees up towards your chest, tilting your pelvis up.
Lower slowly without swinging.

safety: Keep a firm grip

exercises.name: Hanging leg raise
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your legs straight down.
Brace your core and raise your straight legs up until they are about parallel to the floor or higher.
Lower slowly without swinging.

safety: Start with knee raises

exercises.name: Plank
steps: Place your forearms on the floor with your elbows under your shoulders and your legs straight behind you, on your toes.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing steadily.
formCues: Straight line from head to heels

safety: Stop if your lower back hurts

exercises.name: Side plank
steps: Lie on your side with your forearm on the floor, elbow under your shoulder, and your legs stacked.
Brace your core and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Hold for the planned time, then switch sides.

safety: Bend your knees to make it easier

exercises.name: Plank shoulder tap
steps: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your feet wider than shoulder width.
Brace your core and tap your left shoulder with your right hand, keeping your hips still.
Return and tap the other shoulder, alternating.

safety: Use a wider stance to make it easier

exercises.name: Dead bug
steps: Lie on your back with your arms pointing to the ceiling and your knees bent at 90° over your hips.
Brace your core and press your lower back into the floor. Lower your right arm overhead and extend your left leg, keeping your back flat.
Return to the start and repeat on the other side.

safety: Reduce the range if your back arches

exercises.name: Flutter kick
steps: Lie on your back with your hands under your hips and your legs straight, lifted a few inches off the floor.
Brace your core, keep your lower back pressed down and kick your legs up and down in small, quick alternating movements.
Continue for the planned reps or time.

safety: Bend your knees if your back arches

exercises.name: Russian twist
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels on or just off the floor, leaning back slightly with a straight back and your hands clasped in front of your chest.
Brace your core and rotate your torso to one side, moving your hands towards the floor beside your hip.
Rotate to the other side. Each side counts as one rep.

safety: Keep your heels on the floor to make it easier

exercises.name: Hollow body hold
steps: Lie on your back with your arms stretched overhead and your legs straight.
Brace your core, press your lower back into the floor and lift your shoulders and legs off the floor in a shallow banana shape.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing steadily.

safety: Bend your knees or raise your legs to make it easier

exercises.name: Heel touch
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, arms by your sides, and lift your shoulders slightly off the floor.
Reach your right hand towards your right heel by bending sideways, then your left hand towards your left heel.
Keep alternating in a smooth, controlled movement.

safety: Keep your neck relaxed

exercises.name: L-sit
steps: Sit on the floor or between two parallel bars or sturdy supports, with your hands by your hips and your legs straight out in front of you.
Press down through your hands to lift your body off the floor, keeping your legs straight and parallel to the floor.
Hold for the planned time.

safety: Start with tucked knees
Use parallettes or stable supports
metadata.reviewNote: Advanced calisthenics skill; reviewer to decide whether it belongs.

exercises.name: Neck isometric hold
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed. Place your palm against the side, front or back of your head.
Gently press your head into your hand while your hand resists, so your head does not move.
Hold for 5–10 seconds, then relax. Repeat in each direction.

safety: Use gentle pressure only
Stop if you feel dizziness, tingling or pain
Do not do it with neck injuries
metadata.reviewNote: Neck work should be gentle; reviewer to decide whether to include it at all.

exercises.name: Burpee
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. Squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Jump or step your feet back into a plank, and lower your chest to the floor (optional).
Push up, jump or step your feet back towards your hands, then explode up into a jump with your arms overhead.
Land softly and go straight into the next rep.
formCues: Brace the core in the plank

safety: Step rather than jump if you are new
Skip the push-up if needed
Stop if you feel dizzy

exercises.name: Jumping jack
steps: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides.
Jump your feet out wide while swinging your arms up overhead.
Jump your feet back together and lower your arms. Repeat at a steady rhythm.

safety: Land softly on the balls of your feet
Step side to side instead of jumping if your knees hurt

exercises.name: High knees
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Run in place, driving your knees up to about hip height, with your arms pumping in rhythm.
Stay on the balls of your feet and keep your torso upright.

safety: Land softly
Lower the height if your knees hurt

exercises.name: Butt kicks
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Jog in place, kicking your heels up towards your glutes with each step.
Keep your torso upright and your arms pumping in rhythm.

safety: Land softly

exercises.name: Mountain climber
steps: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Brace your core and drive one knee towards your chest, then quickly switch legs in a running motion.
Keep your hips low and your shoulders over your hands.

safety: Slow down to make it easier

exercises.name: Squat thrust
steps: Stand tall, then squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Jump or step your feet back into a plank.
Jump or step your feet back towards your hands and stand up.
formCues: Brace the core in the plank

safety: Step rather than jump if you are new

exercises.name: Skater jump
steps: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Leap sideways to the other leg, landing softly on the opposite foot with your knee bent and your other leg swinging behind you.
Immediately leap back the other way, alternating.

safety: Land softly
Skip it with knee or ankle problems

exercises.name: Bear crawl
steps: Start on your hands and feet with your knees bent and hovering just off the floor, back flat and hands under your shoulders.
Crawl forward by moving opposite hand and foot together, keeping your knees low and your back flat.
Keep your hips level and move for the planned distance, then reverse or turn around.
formCues: Knees hover close to the floor
Opposite hand and foot move together

safety: Use a clear space

exercises.name: Shadow boxing
steps: Stand in a staggered stance with your knees slightly bent, hands up near your chin and your elbows in.
Throw straight punches (jab and cross) in the air, rotating your hips and shoulders, and return your hands to your chin each time.
Move around lightly on the balls of your feet, throwing combinations for the planned time.
formCues: Rotate the hips into the punch

safety: Do not lock the elbows when punching
Clear the space around you

exercises.name: Surya namaskar (sun salutation)
steps: Stand tall at the front of your mat with your feet together and your palms pressed together at your chest (pranamasana).
Inhale, raise your arms overhead and arch back gently. Exhale, fold forward at the hips and place your hands beside your feet.

Inhale, step or lunge your right leg back and lift your chest; exhale and step your other foot back into a plank. Lower your body down with your chest and knees, or move through a plank to a cobra with your hips low.
Exhale into downward dog with your hips high. Then step or jump your feet forward, rise to a forward fold, then stand up with arms overhead, and return to the start.
Repeat the sequence, leading with the other leg, for the planned rounds.
formCues: Breathe in rhythm with the movement
Move smoothly from one pose to the next
Keep the core braced in the plank

commonMistakes: Collapsing the hips in the plank
Locking the knees in the forward fold
safety: Warm up first
Bend your knees in the forward fold if your hamstrings are tight
Skip the deep backbend if you have lower back pain
metadata.reviewNote: A traditional Indian sequence of 12 poses. The reviewer should confirm the exact order and breathing cues.

exercises.name: Broad jump
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. Swing your arms back and dip into a quarter squat.
Explode forward, jumping as far as you can with your arms swinging forward.
Land softly with both feet and bend your knees to absorb the impact, then reset.

safety: Land softly
Skip it with knee, ankle or lower-back problems

exercises.name: Neck side-tilt stretch
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed down.
Tilt your head to one side, bringing your ear towards your shoulder, without lifting the shoulder. Rest a hand lightly on your head for a gentle extra pull, if needed.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not pull hard on your head
Stop if you feel tingling or dizziness
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Neck rotation
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly turn your head to look over one shoulder as far as is comfortable, keeping your chin level.
Return to the centre and turn to the other side. Repeat slowly.

safety: Do not force the turn
Stop if you feel dizziness or pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Chin tuck
steps: Sit or stand tall with your eyes level.
Draw your chin straight back, as if making a double chin, keeping your eyes level and not tilting your head down.
Hold for a few seconds, then release. Repeat.
formCues: Do not tilt the head down

safety: Do not force it
Stop if you feel pain or tingling
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce
metadata.reviewNote: Often used for forward-head posture; reviewer to confirm the hold time.

exercises.name: Levator scapulae stretch
steps: Sit tall and turn your head about 45° to one side, then look down towards your armpit.
Rest a hand on the back of your head and apply a gentle pull, until you feel a stretch along the back of your neck and the top of the shoulder blade.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Pull gently
Stop if you feel tingling or pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Upper trap stretch
steps: Sit tall with one arm behind your back or holding the edge of your seat to keep the shoulder down.
Tilt your head to the opposite side, ear towards the shoulder, until you feel a stretch along the side of your neck and top of your shoulder.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not pull hard on your head
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Doorway chest stretch
steps: Stand in a doorway or beside a wall and place your forearm or palm on the frame or wall, with your elbow bent at about 90° and level with your shoulder.
Step forward with the same-side foot, or turn your body away gently, until you feel a stretch across the front of your chest and shoulder.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not push into pain
Keep your shoulder blade relaxed
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Standing chest opener
steps: Stand tall and clasp your hands together behind your back, or hold a towel.
Straighten your arms and lift your hands slightly away from your back, opening your chest, with your shoulder blades drawn back and down.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release.

safety: Do not lean the torso forward
Do not force the arms up
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
steps: Stand or sit tall and bring one arm straight across your chest at shoulder height.
Use your other hand to hold the arm just above the elbow and gently pull it closer to your chest.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Arm stays straight, at shoulder height

safety: Pull on the elbow, not the wrist
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Arm circles
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Make small circles with your arms, gradually making them bigger, for 10–15 reps.
Reverse the direction and repeat.

safety: Stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Wall slide
steps: Stand with your back, head and hips against a wall and your feet a little forward. Bend your elbows to 90° with your arms and the backs of your hands against the wall.
Slide your arms up the wall as far as you can keep them in contact, then slowly slide them back down.
Keep your ribs down and your lower back neutral throughout.
formCues: Arms and head stay on the wall

commonMistakes: Letting the arms leave the wall
safety: Do not force the arms up if they lift off the wall
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Sleeper stretch
steps: Lie on your side with your bottom arm in front of you and your elbow bent at 90°, upper arm at right angles to your torso.
Use your top hand to gently press the forearm of your bottom arm towards the floor, until you feel a stretch at the back of the shoulder.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not push into pain
Skip it if you have shoulder pain or impingement
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce
metadata.reviewNote: A rehab-style stretch; reviewer to decide whether to keep it for general trainers.

exercises.name: Shoulder CARs (controlled articular rotations)
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and one arm by your side, with your fist closed.
Slowly lift your arm forward and up, then rotate it overhead and back behind you in the largest circle you can make, keeping your body still.
Reverse the direction, then switch arms.

commonMistakes: Moving the torso to cheat the range
safety: Stop if you feel pinching
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Overhead triceps stretch
steps: Stand or sit tall and raise one arm overhead, then bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your head.
Use your other hand to gently press the elbow back and down, until you feel a stretch along the back of your upper arm.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not pull on your neck
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Wall biceps stretch
steps: Stand next to a wall and place your palm flat on it at shoulder height, with your fingers pointing backwards and your arm straight.
Slowly turn your body away from the wall until you feel a stretch in the front of your upper arm.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Stop if you feel tingling in the arm
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Wrist flexor stretch
steps: Extend one arm in front of you with your palm facing up and your elbow straight.
Use your other hand to gently pull your fingers down and back, until you feel a stretch in the underside of your forearm.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not force the wrist
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Wrist extensor stretch
steps: Extend one arm in front of you with your palm facing down and your elbow straight.
Use your other hand to gently pull your hand down and in towards you, until you feel a stretch on the top of your forearm.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not force the wrist
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Wrist circles
steps: Hold your arms out in front of you with your hands relaxed and your fingers loosely together or in a loose fist.
Make slow circles with your wrists, in one direction for 10 reps.
Reverse the direction and repeat.

safety: Stop if you feel wrist pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Kneeling lat stretch
steps: Kneel in front of a bench or sturdy chair and place your forearms or hands on it with your arms straight in front of you.
Sit your hips back towards your heels and let your chest sink towards the floor, until you feel a stretch along the sides of your back and under your arms.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release.

safety: Do not force the shoulders
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Side-bend lat stretch
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and reach one arm overhead, holding your wrist with your other hand.
Gently bend sideways away from the reaching arm, until you feel a stretch along the side of your torso and under your arm.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not lean forward or twist
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Hanging lat stretch
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart, with your feet on the floor or knees bent.
Let your body weight stretch your lats and shoulders, relaxing your shoulders up.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release.

safety: Do not drop suddenly
Skip it with shoulder pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Cat-cow
steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, back flat.
Inhale and let your belly sink as you lift your chest and tailbone (cow).
Exhale and round your spine up towards the ceiling, tucking your chin and tailbone (cat).
Move smoothly between the two positions in time with your breathing.

safety: Do not force the end ranges
Skip it if it causes wrist pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Child's pose
steps: Kneel on a mat with your big toes together and your knees about hip width apart or wider.
Sit your hips back towards your heels and walk your hands forward, lowering your chest towards the floor with your forehead on the mat.
Relax and breathe slowly, holding for the planned time.

safety: Place a cushion under your knees or hips if needed
Skip it if you have knee pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Supine spinal twist
steps: Lie on your back with your arms out to the sides in a T shape. Bend one knee and bring it across your body towards the floor on the opposite side.
Keep your shoulders on the floor and turn your head the other way if comfortable.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Skip it or support the knee with a cushion if your lower back hurts
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Seated spinal twist
steps: Sit tall on the floor with your legs straight. Bend one knee and place that foot flat on the outside of the opposite knee.
Hold the bent knee with your opposite arm and place your other hand behind you, then twist your torso towards the bent knee, lengthening your spine.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not force the twist
Skip it if your lower back hurts
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Thread the needle
steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Slide one arm under your body, palm up, lowering your shoulder and the side of your head to the floor, until you feel a stretch across your upper back and shoulder.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not force the shoulder
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Open book rotation
steps: Lie on your side with your knees bent at 90° in front of you and your arms stretched out in front, palms together.
Keeping your knees together and down, lift your top arm and open it up and back, following it with your eyes, until your chest faces the ceiling.
Return to the start slowly. Repeat for the planned reps, then switch sides.
formCues: Follow the hand with your eyes

safety: Do not force the arm to the floor
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Standing back extension
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart and place your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down.
Gently lean back, extending your upper and lower back, as far as is comfortable, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Return to upright. Repeat for a few reps.

safety: Do not lean back too far
Skip it with lower back pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Cobra stretch
steps: Lie face down on a mat with your hands under your shoulders and your legs straight, tops of the feet on the floor.
Press gently through your hands to lift your chest off the floor, keeping your hips on the floor, until you feel a stretch along your abs.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Lower slowly.
formCues: Lift from the back, press gently with hands

safety: Skip it if it causes lower back pain
Do not push up too far
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Standing side stretch
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your arms overhead, hands clasped or one holding the other wrist.
Bend sideways from your waist, keeping both hips square, until you feel a stretch along the side of your torso.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not twist or lean forward
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Standing quad stretch
steps: Stand tall, holding a wall or support for balance with one hand.
Bend one knee and bring your heel towards your glute, holding your ankle with the same-side hand.
Keep your knees together and your hips tucked slightly, until you feel a stretch along the front of your thigh. Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

commonMistakes: Letting the knee drift forward or out
safety: Do not pull on the foot if your knee hurts
Hold a support for balance
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
steps: Kneel on one knee on a mat, with the other foot flat in front of you, knee over your ankle.
Tuck your pelvis under and squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg, then shift your hips gently forward until you feel a stretch in the front of the hip.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Tuck the pelvis, squeeze the glute

safety: Use a cushion under the kneeling knee
Do not arch the lower back
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce
metadata.reviewNote: Hip flexors are not in our muscle list, so this is filed under quads (the part that crosses the hip).

exercises.name: Couch stretch
steps: Kneel with your back to a wall or couch and place one foot up against it, with your knee on the floor and your shin against the wall.
Step the other foot forward into a lunge and lift your torso upright, tucking your pelvis under and squeezing your glute.
Hold until you feel a deep stretch in the front of your thigh and hip. Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Use a cushion under the knee
Skip it with knee pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce
metadata.equipmentNeeded: wall or couch and a mat

exercises.name: Lying quad stretch
steps: Lie face down on a mat and bend one knee, bringing your heel towards your glute.
Hold your ankle with the same-side hand, or use a towel around the ankle, and gently pull your heel closer.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Use a towel if you cannot reach your ankle
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Standing hamstring stretch
steps: Stand tall and place one heel on a low step or the floor in front of you, with your leg straight and your toes pointing up.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, reaching towards your toes, until you feel a stretch along the back of your thigh.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Hinge from the hips, back flat
Toes up, leg straight but not locked

safety: Do not round your back to reach further
Keep the knee soft
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Seated forward fold
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you and your feet flexed.
Hinge forward from your hips with a long spine, reaching your hands towards your feet, until you feel a stretch along the back of your legs.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release.

commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach the toes
safety: Bend your knees slightly or sit on a cushion if your hamstrings are tight
Do not round hard to reach your toes
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Supine hamstring stretch
steps: Lie on your back with both legs straight, and loop a towel or strap around the ball of one foot.
Lift that leg towards the ceiling with your knee straight, using the towel to gently pull, until you feel a stretch along the back of your thigh.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Lower back stays on the floor

safety: Bend the knee slightly if it is too intense
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Inchworm
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart. Hinge forward and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet, bending your knees if needed.
Walk your hands forward until you are in a high plank, keeping your core braced.
Walk your hands back towards your feet, keeping your legs as straight as you can, then stand up.
formCues: Keep the core braced in the plank

commonMistakes: Sagging the hips in the plank
safety: Bend the knees if your hamstrings are tight
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Forward leg swing
