steps: Stand tall next to a wall or rail for support, with your weight on one leg.
Swing your other leg forward and back in a smooth pendulum, keeping your torso upright and gradually increasing the range.
Complete the reps on one leg, then switch.

safety: Hold a support
Do not swing wildly
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Figure-four stretch
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee, making a figure four.
Lift the bottom foot off the floor, and gently pull the thigh of the bottom leg towards your chest, until you feel a stretch in the glute of the crossed leg.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not force the knee outward
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Pigeon pose
steps: Start on your hands and knees. Bring one knee forward behind that wrist, with your shin angled across your body, and extend the other leg straight behind you.
Square your hips to the floor, and walk your hands forward to lower your chest and fold over the front shin, until you feel a deep stretch in your glute.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Place a cushion under your hip if it does not reach the floor
Skip it with knee pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Knee-to-chest stretch
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight. Bring one knee towards your chest and hold it with both hands.
Gently pull the knee closer to your chest, keeping the other leg flat on the floor, until you feel a stretch in your glute and lower back.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Skip it if it causes hip pinching
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: 90/90 hip switch
aliases: Hip internal and external rotation drill
steps: Sit on the floor with your front knee bent at 90° in front of you and your back knee bent at 90° to the side, with both legs flat on the floor.
Sit tall, then lift your knees and rotate them over to the other side so your legs swap positions, controlling the movement.
Continue smoothly from side to side for the planned reps.

safety: Use your hands for support if you need
Skip it if you have knee pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Hip circles
steps: Stand on one leg, holding a wall for balance, and lift the other knee in front of you to about hip height.
Slowly rotate the knee out to the side and around behind you in the largest circle you can make, keeping your torso still.
Reverse the direction, then switch legs.

commonMistakes: Moving the torso to cheat the range
safety: Hold a support
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: World's greatest stretch
steps: Step into a long lunge with your right foot forward and your left knee lifted, and place both hands on the floor inside your front foot.
Place your right elbow towards the floor inside your foot, then rotate your torso and reach your right arm up to the ceiling, following it with your eyes.
Return the hand down, straighten your front leg to stretch the hamstring, then step back and repeat on the other side.

safety: Move within your range
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce
metadata.reviewNote: A full-body mobility drill (hips, hamstrings and upper back); filed under glutes.

exercises.name: Butterfly stretch
steps: Sit on the floor with your back tall, bring the soles of your feet together and let your knees drop out to the sides.
Hold your feet or ankles and gently lean forward from your hips, keeping your spine long, until you feel a stretch in your inner thighs.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release.

commonMistakes: Pushing the knees down with force
safety: Sit on a cushion if your knees are high or your back rounds
Do not press on your knees
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Frog stretch
steps: Start on your hands and knees and widen your knees out to the sides as far as is comfortable, keeping your ankles in line with your knees and your feet turned out.
Lower down onto your forearms, and rock your hips gently back towards your heels, until you feel a stretch in your inner thighs.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release.
formCues: Knees in line with the ankles

safety: Use a cushion under your knees
Skip it with knee or groin pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Wide-leg seated forward fold
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs open wide in a V, knees and toes pointing up.
Sit tall, then walk your hands forward and hinge from your hips with a long spine, until you feel a stretch in your inner thighs and hamstrings.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release.

safety: Sit on a cushion if your back rounds
Do not force the legs wider
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Deep squat hold
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width and toes turned out.
Sit down as low as you can, with your heels flat if possible, your knees pushing out over your toes and your hands pressed together in front of your chest.
Hold the bottom position with a tall chest, pressing your elbows against your knees gently, for the planned time.

safety: Hold a support or put a rolled towel under your heels if they lift
Skip it with knee pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce
metadata.reviewNote: A common resting position in India; useful for hip and ankle mobility. Reviewer to confirm.

exercises.name: Standing IT band stretch
steps: Stand tall and cross one leg behind the other, with your feet close together.
Reach the arm on the side of the back leg overhead and lean your torso away, pushing your hip out to the side, until you feel a stretch along the outer thigh and hip.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Push the hip out, lean away

safety: Hold a wall for balance
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Cross-body knee pull
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight. Bend one knee and use the opposite hand to pull it gently across your body towards the opposite shoulder.
Keep your shoulders on the floor, until you feel a stretch in the outer hip and glute.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not force it if your hips pinch
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Lateral leg swing
steps: Stand tall facing a wall or rail and hold it for support with both hands.
Swing one leg out to the side and across your body in a smooth pendulum, keeping your torso upright and gradually increasing the range.
Complete the reps on one leg, then switch.

safety: Hold a support
Do not swing wildly
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Wall calf stretch
steps: Stand facing a wall with your hands on it at shoulder height. Step one foot back, keeping your heel on the floor and your back leg straight.
Bend your front knee and lean forward gently, until you feel a stretch in the calf of your back leg.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Do not let the back foot turn out
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Heel-drop calf stretch
steps: Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of a step, holding a rail for balance.
Lower your heels below the level of the step slowly, until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then release.

safety: Hold a support for balance
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Knee-to-wall ankle mobilization
steps: Stand facing a wall with one foot about 4 inches (10 cm) from it. Place your hands on the wall for balance.
Keeping your heel flat on the floor, bend your knee forward to touch the wall.
Return and repeat. If it is easy, move your foot further back.
formCues: Knee tracks over the middle toes

safety: Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the ankle
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Ankle circles
steps: Sit or stand with one foot lifted off the floor.
Slowly draw large circles with your toes, moving only at the ankle, for 10 reps.
Reverse the direction, then switch feet.

safety: Stop if you feel pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Foam roll — calves
steps: Sit on the floor with the foam roller under your calves and your hands on the floor behind you.
Lift your hips off the floor and slowly roll from just above your ankle to just below your knee.
Pause on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, then continue rolling.

safety: Roll slowly, not fast
Avoid rolling directly over the knee joint
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Foam roll — quads
steps: Lie face down with the foam roller under your thighs and your forearms on the floor, in a plank-like position.
Slowly roll from just above your knee to just below your hip crease, using your arms to control the pressure.
Pause on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly.

safety: Avoid rolling directly over the knee or hip bones
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Foam roll — hamstrings
steps: Sit on the floor with the foam roller under your thighs and your hands on the floor behind you.
Lift your hips and slowly roll from just above your knee to just below your glutes.
Pause on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly.
formCues: Keep the weight in your hands to control pressure

safety: Avoid rolling directly over the back of the knee
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Foam roll — IT band and outer thigh
steps: Lie on your side with the foam roller under your outer thigh and your forearm on the floor. Cross the top leg over and place that foot on the floor in front of you.
Slowly roll from just above your knee to just below your hip.
Pause on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly.
formCues: Support with the forearm and top foot

safety: Avoid rolling directly over the hip bone or knee
Stop if you feel sharp pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce
metadata.reviewNote: The IT band itself does not stretch, and rolling it is uncomfortable; a gentler roll on the outer thigh is more common. Reviewer to decide.

exercises.name: Foam roll — glutes
steps: Sit on a foam roller with your hands on the floor behind you, and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Lean towards the side of the crossed leg and slowly roll over your glute.
Pause on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
formCues: Lean to the side being rolled

safety: Roll slowly
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Foam roll — adductors
steps: Lie face down with the foam roller placed parallel to your body and one leg bent out to the side, with your inner thigh over the roller.
Slowly roll along your inner thigh from your groin to just above your knee.
Pause on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.

safety: Avoid rolling directly over the groin or knee
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Foam roll — upper back
steps: Lie on your back with the foam roller under your upper back, just below your shoulder blades, knees bent and feet flat, with your hands behind your head to support your neck.
Lift your hips slightly and roll slowly up and down from your mid-back to your shoulder blades.
Pause on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly.

safety: Do not roll the lower back
Avoid arching the neck
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Thoracic extension over a foam roller
steps: Lie on your back with the foam roller under your upper back, knees bent and feet flat, hands behind your head to support your neck.
Keep your hips on the floor and gently extend your upper back over the roller, looking at the ceiling.
Return to neutral and move the roller up or down a little. Repeat for the planned reps.
formCues: Extend through the upper back only

safety: Do not extend through the lower back
Skip it if it causes neck pain
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Foam roll — lats
steps: Lie on your side with the foam roller under your armpit area and your bottom arm extended overhead.
Slowly roll down along the side of your back, towards the bottom of your ribs.
Pause on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

safety: Avoid rolling over the ribs hard
Stretch to a mild pull, never sharp pain
Do not bounce

exercises.name: Tadasana (mountain pose)
steps: Stand with your feet together or hip width apart, weight evenly spread across both feet, and your arms by your sides.
Lift your kneecaps gently, draw your tailbone down, lengthen your spine and lift your chest, with your shoulders relaxed down and back.
Keep your chin level and look straight ahead. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.
formCues: Spine long, crown of the head lifts

safety: Stand near a wall for balance if needed
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Tiryaka tadasana (swaying palm tree pose)
steps: Stand with your feet about hip width apart, interlace your fingers and stretch your arms overhead, palms facing up.
Inhale and lengthen your spine, then exhale and bend sideways from your waist, keeping your arms and chest facing forward.
Inhale to return to the centre and exhale to bend to the other side. Repeat smoothly.

safety: Do not bend further than is comfortable
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Kati chakrasana (standing spinal twist)
steps: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and your arms stretched out in front of you at shoulder height.
Inhale, then exhale and twist your torso and arms to the right, letting your left hand rest on your right shoulder and your right arm swing behind you.
Inhale back to the centre, then twist to the other side, in a smooth, rhythmic flow.

safety: Keep the movement gentle if your lower back is sensitive
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Utkatasana (chair pose)
steps: Stand with your feet together or hip width apart. Raise your arms overhead with your palms facing each other.
Bend your knees and sit your hips back as if sitting in a chair, with your weight in your heels and your chest lifted.
Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Stand up to release.

commonMistakes: Letting the knees go past the toes
safety: Reduce the depth if your knees hurt
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Vrksasana (tree pose)
steps: Stand in tadasana and shift your weight onto your left foot. Place the sole of your right foot on your left inner calf or thigh (not on the knee).
Press your foot and leg firmly into each other, and bring your palms together at your chest or overhead.
Fix your gaze on a point ahead. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.

commonMistakes: Placing the foot on the knee
safety: Stand near a wall for balance
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Trikonasana (triangle pose)
steps: Stand with your feet about 3–4 feet (1 m) apart, right foot turned out 90° and left foot turned in slightly, arms stretched out at shoulder height.
Reach your right hand forward, then hinge sideways from the hip and lower your right hand to your shin, ankle or a block, extending your left arm to the ceiling.
Keep both sides of your torso long and look up at your top hand, if comfortable. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Hinge from the hip, do not collapse
Both sides of the torso long

commonMistakes: Dropping the hand to the floor with a rounded back
safety: Use a block if you cannot reach the shin comfortably
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Virabhadrasana I (warrior I)
steps: Stand with your feet about 3–4 feet (1 m) apart. Turn your right foot out 90° and your back foot in about 45°, hips facing the front.
Bend your right knee to about 90° over your ankle and raise your arms overhead, palms facing each other.
Keep your back leg strong and your chest lifted. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Shorten the stance if your hips feel strained
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Virabhadrasana II (warrior II)
steps: Stand with your feet about 4 feet (1.2 m) apart. Turn your right foot out 90° and your back foot in slightly, arms stretched out at shoulder height.
Bend your right knee to about 90° over your ankle, keeping your torso upright over your hips.
Gaze over your right fingertips. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Front knee tracks over the second toe

safety: Shorten the stance if your hips feel strained
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Virabhadrasana III (warrior III)
steps: Stand in tadasana, step your left foot back and shift your weight onto your right foot, with your arms overhead.
Hinge forward from the hip, lifting your back leg until your torso and leg are parallel to the floor, with your hips level.
Keep your standing leg slightly bent or straight but not locked. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Torso and back leg form a straight line

safety: Place your hands on blocks or a wall if you lose balance
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Utthita parsvakonasana (extended side angle)
steps: Stand with your feet about 4 feet (1.2 m) apart. Turn your right foot out 90° and bend your right knee to about 90° over your ankle.
Lower your right forearm to your right thigh or your right hand to the floor inside your foot, and extend your left arm over your ear.
Press your front knee against your arm and rotate your chest open. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Long line from the back foot to the top hand

safety: Rest your forearm on your thigh or use a block
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Ardha chandrasana (half moon pose)
steps: From trikonasana on the right, bend your right knee and place your right hand on the floor or a block about a foot in front of your right foot.
Shift your weight onto your right foot and lift your left leg to hip height, straightening the standing leg.
Stack your hips and shoulders and extend your left arm to the ceiling. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Use a block under your hand
Practise near a wall
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Prasarita padottanasana (wide-legged forward fold)
steps: Stand with your feet about 4 feet (1.2 m) apart, toes pointing forward or slightly in, and your hands on your hips.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long spine, and place your hands on the floor under your shoulders.
Let your head hang, bend your elbows gently, and relax your neck. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Press into your feet to rise.
formCues: Weight on the balls of the feet

safety: Bend your knees or use blocks if your hamstrings are tight
Come up slowly to avoid dizziness
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Uttanasana (standing forward fold)
steps: Stand in tadasana with your feet hip width apart.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long spine and fold over your legs, letting your head and arms hang.
Bend your knees slightly if you need to, keeping your weight over the balls of your feet. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Roll up slowly.
formCues: Let the head and neck hang

commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach the floor
safety: Bend your knees if your hamstrings are tight
Roll up slowly
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Garudasana (eagle pose)
steps: Stand in tadasana, bend your knees and shift your weight onto your left foot. Cross your right thigh over your left thigh and hook your right foot behind your left calf if you can.
Cross your left arm over your right at the elbows, bring your palms together and lift your elbows to shoulder height.
Sit your hips back and lengthen your spine. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Keep your toes on the floor if you lose balance
Practise near a wall
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Natarajasana (dancer pose)
steps: Stand in tadasana and shift your weight onto your left foot. Bend your right knee and hold the inside of your right foot or ankle with your right hand.
Kick your foot back and up into your hand while extending your left arm forward and hinging your torso forward slightly.
Keep your hips square and your gaze steady. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.
formCues: Kick the foot into the hand

safety: Hold a wall or chair for balance
Use a strap around the foot if you cannot reach
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Parivrtta trikonasana (revolved triangle pose)
steps: Stand with your feet about 3 feet (1 m) apart, right foot forward, left foot turned in 45°, hips squared to the front.
Hinge forward from the hip with a long spine and place your left hand on the floor or a block outside your right foot, then twist and reach your right arm to the ceiling.
Rotate the chest open, keeping your hips square. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Use a block under your hand
Skip it with lower back pain
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Sukhasana (easy pose)
steps: Sit on a mat with your legs crossed comfortably in front of you, and your sit bones grounded.
Lengthen your spine, relax your shoulders and rest your hands on your knees or in your lap.
Keep your breathing slow and steady. Hold for the planned time.

commonMistakes: Knees much higher than the hips
safety: Sit on a folded blanket or cushion if your knees are higher than your hips
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Vajrasana (thunderbolt pose)
steps: Kneel on a mat with your knees together and your big toes touching, then sit back on your heels.
Keep your spine tall, shoulders relaxed and hands resting on your thighs.
Breathe slowly. Hold for the planned time.

safety: Place a cushion between your calves and thighs or under your ankles if your knees or ankles hurt
Avoid it with knee injuries
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain
metadata.reviewNote: Often used for sitting after meals in Indian practice.

exercises.name: Dandasana (staff pose)
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you and your feet flexed.
Press your hands into the floor beside your hips and lengthen your spine, drawing your shoulders back.
Engage your thighs and abs. Hold for the planned time.

safety: Sit on a cushion if your lower back rounds
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Janu sirsasana (head-to-knee pose)
steps: Sit with your right leg straight and your left knee bent, with the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and hinge forward over your right leg, holding your shin, foot or a strap.
Keep your spine long. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.

commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach the foot
safety: Use a strap and sit on a cushion if needed
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Navasana (boat pose)
steps: Sit with your knees bent and feet flat, and lean back slightly with a long spine.
Lift your feet off the floor so your shins are parallel to the floor, and reach your arms forward alongside your knees.
Straighten your legs if you can, keeping your chest lifted. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.

safety: Keep your knees bent or hold behind your thighs
Skip it with lower back pain
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Gomukhasana (cow face pose)
steps: Sit with your legs crossed so your knees stack on top of each other, as best you can, sitting tall.
Reach your right arm up and bend it behind your head, and your left arm behind your back, and try to clasp your hands or hold a strap.
Lift your chest and keep your head upright. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Use a strap between your hands
Skip the leg position if your knees hurt
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Supta baddha konasana (reclined bound angle pose)
steps: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and your knees dropping out to the sides.
Rest your arms by your sides with your palms up, or place your hands on your belly.
Relax and breathe slowly. Hold for the planned time.

safety: Support each knee with a cushion if the stretch is strong
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Ananda balasana (happy baby pose)
steps: Lie on your back and bring your knees towards your chest, then take hold of the outsides of your feet.
Open your knees wider than your torso and pull your knees towards your armpits, keeping your ankles above your knees.
Keep your tailbone and head on the floor. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.

safety: Hold behind your thighs if you cannot reach your feet
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Supta padangusthasana (reclined hand-to-big-toe pose)
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight. Bend your right knee and loop a strap around the ball of your right foot.
Straighten the right leg towards the ceiling, pressing through the heel, and keep your left leg active and flat on the floor.
Keep your shoulders on the floor. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.

safety: Bend the lifted knee if it is too intense
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Utthan pristhasana (lizard pose)
steps: From a low lunge with your right foot forward, place both hands on the floor inside your right foot, and walk your front foot towards the outside of the mat.
Lower your hips towards the floor and, if comfortable, come down onto your forearms, keeping your back leg strong.
Keep your chest open. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Repeat on the other side.

commonMistakes: Letting the front knee fall in
safety: Rest your back knee on the mat
Use blocks under your hands
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Salabhasana (locust pose)
steps: Lie face down with your arms alongside your body, palms up, and your forehead on the floor.
Inhale and lift your head, chest, arms and legs off the floor, squeezing your glutes and back.
Look slightly forward without straining your neck. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.
formCues: Lift from the back and glutes

safety: Lift only the chest or only the legs if it is too strong
Skip it with lower back pain
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Dhanurasana (bow pose)
steps: Lie face down, bend your knees and reach back to hold your ankles with your hands.
Inhale and lift your chest and thighs off the floor, kicking your feet back into your hands.
Look forward and breathe steadily. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.

commonMistakes: Pulling the head back too far
safety: Skip it with lower back pain, high blood pressure or an abdominal hernia
Avoid it in pregnancy
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Ustrasana (camel pose)
steps: Kneel with your knees hip width apart and your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down.
Lift your chest and arch back gently, pushing your hips forward, and reach for your heels one at a time if you can.
Keep your hips over your knees and your neck relaxed. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Return slowly.

safety: Keep your hands on your lower back if you cannot reach your heels
Skip it with neck or lower back pain
Come up slowly
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Urdhva dhanurasana (wheel pose)
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat near your hips, and your hands beside your ears, fingers pointing towards your shoulders.
Press into your hands and feet to lift your hips, then straighten your arms to lift your head off the floor.
Press your chest towards the wall behind you. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing. Lower slowly.
formCues: Press evenly through hands and feet

safety: Only attempt after building shoulder, spine and wrist mobility
Skip it with wrist, shoulder or lower back problems
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain
metadata.reviewNote: Advanced backbend; reviewer to decide whether general trainers need it.

exercises.name: Matsyasana (fish pose)
steps: Lie on your back with your legs together and your hands under your hips, palms down.
Press into your forearms and elbows to lift your chest, arching your upper back and letting the crown of your head rest lightly on the floor.
Keep most of your weight on your elbows, not your head. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.

commonMistakes: Putting weight on the head and neck
safety: Skip it with neck problems
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Urdhva mukha svanasana (upward-facing dog)
steps: Lie face down with your hands beside your lower ribs and the tops of your feet on the floor.
Press through your hands and the tops of your feet to straighten your arms and lift your chest and thighs off the floor.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears and look forward or slightly up. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.

safety: Use cobra instead if your lower back or wrists hurt
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Adho mukha svanasana (downward-facing dog)
steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands slightly ahead of your shoulders and your toes tucked under.
Lift your knees and push your hips up and back, forming an inverted V, with your arms and spine long.
Press your heels towards the floor (they do not need to touch), and relax your head between your arms. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.

commonMistakes: Walking the hands too close to the feet
safety: Bend your knees if your hamstrings are tight
Skip it with wrist pain
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Chaturanga dandasana (four-limbed staff pose)
steps: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Shift forward slightly and bend your elbows, keeping them hugged to your ribs, lowering your body until your elbows are at 90°.
Hold with your body in a straight line from head to heels. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.

commonMistakes: Dropping the shoulders below the elbows
safety: Lower your knees to the floor to make it easier
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Bakasana (crow pose)
steps: Squat down with your feet close together and your hands flat on the floor, shoulder width apart, fingers spread.
Place your knees high on the backs of your upper arms, and lean forward until your weight is over your hands.
Lift your feet off the floor one at a time and balance, gazing slightly forward. Hold for about 5 slow breaths (20–30 seconds) before releasing.

commonMistakes: Dumping the weight on the wrists
safety: Place a cushion under your head in case you fall
Skip it with wrist problems
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain
metadata.reviewNote: Advanced balance; reviewer to decide whether to keep it.

exercises.name: Pavanamuktasana (wind-relieving pose)
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight. Bend both knees and hug them towards your chest with both arms.
Lift your head and chest towards your knees, if comfortable, keeping your lower back on the floor.
Breathe steadily. Hold for the planned time, then release.

safety: Skip it in late pregnancy
Keep your head on the floor if your neck hurts
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain
metadata.reviewNote: Traditional wind-relieving pose; reviewer to confirm the benefits claim is not shown in the app.

exercises.name: Viparita karani (legs-up-the-wall pose)
steps: Sit sideways next to a wall, then swing your legs up the wall as you lie back, with your hips close to or against the wall.
Rest your arms by your sides with your palms up, and relax your neck and shoulders.
Breathe slowly. Hold for the planned time, then bend your knees and roll to the side to come out.

commonMistakes: Hips too far from the wall
safety: Skip it with glaucoma or uncontrolled high blood pressure
Come out slowly to avoid dizziness
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Shavasana (corpse pose)
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs slightly apart and your arms by your sides, palms facing up.
Close your eyes and relax every part of your body, from your toes up to your face.
Let your breath settle into its natural rhythm and stay still for the planned time.

commonMistakes: Falling asleep (fine, but not the aim)
safety: Come out slowly, rolling to one side before sitting up
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain
metadata.reviewNote: Relaxation rather than exercise. Filed under 'cardio' only because the muscle list has no 'relaxation'; reviewer to decide.

exercises.name: Anulom vilom (alternate nostril breathing)
steps: Sit comfortably with your spine tall and your left hand on your left knee. Fold the index and middle fingers of your right hand towards your palm.
Close your right nostril with your right thumb and inhale slowly through the left nostril. Close the left nostril with your ring finger, release the thumb, and exhale through the right.
Inhale through the right nostril, close it, and exhale through the left. That is one round.
Continue for the planned rounds, breathing slowly and evenly, without strain.

safety: Skip any breath holds if you have high blood pressure or a heart condition
Stop if you feel dizzy
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Kapalabhati (skull-shining breath)
steps: Sit comfortably with your spine tall and your hands on your knees. Take a deep breath in.
Exhale forcefully through your nose by pulling your lower belly in sharply, then let the inhale happen passively, without effort.
Continue in a steady rhythm for about 20–30 pumps per round, then breathe normally. Repeat for the planned rounds.
formCues: Belly pumps, shoulders and face relaxed

commonMistakes: Pumping from the chest or shoulders
safety: Skip it in pregnancy, with high blood pressure, heart disease, hernia, ulcers or recent abdominal surgery
Stop if you feel dizzy or lightheaded
Avoid it on a full stomach

exercises.name: Bhastrika (bellows breath)
steps: Sit comfortably with your spine tall and your hands on your knees.
Breathe in and out forcefully through your nose, expanding and contracting your belly and lower chest, at a steady rhythm, for about 10–20 breaths.
Finish with a deep inhale, hold briefly if comfortable, then exhale slowly. Rest and breathe normally before the next round.
formCues: Active in and out, belly leads

safety: Skip it in pregnancy, with high blood pressure, heart disease, hernia or epilepsy
Stop if you feel dizzy
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Bhramari (humming bee breath)
steps: Sit comfortably with your spine tall. Close your eyes and place your index fingers gently on the small flap of cartilage in front of each ear, or rest your hands on your knees.
Inhale slowly through your nose, then exhale slowly while making a steady humming sound like a bee, keeping your mouth closed.
Feel the vibration in your head. Repeat for the planned rounds.
formCues: Slow, steady exhale with a hum

commonMistakes: Pressing too hard on the ears
safety: Skip it with an ear infection
Stop if you feel dizzy
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Ujjayi (ocean breath)
steps: Sit comfortably with your spine tall. Take a slow breath in through your nose.
Gently constrict the back of your throat, as if fogging a mirror but with your mouth closed, so your breath makes a soft ocean-like sound.
Breathe in and out slowly through your nose with the same soft sound, keeping your breath smooth and even.

safety: Breathe gently, never strain
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic breathing (belly breathing)
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, or sit tall. Place one hand on your chest and one on your belly.
Breathe in slowly through your nose so that your belly rises while your chest stays still.
Breathe out slowly through your mouth or nose, letting your belly fall. Repeat for the planned reps.

safety: Stop if you feel dizzy
Breathe steadily and never force a pose into pain

exercises.name: EZ-bar curl
steps: Stand tall holding an EZ bar on the inner (or outer) angled grips with an underhand grip, arms hanging straight and elbows by your sides.
Keeping your elbows pinned, curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.

safety: Use a weight you can curl without swinging

exercises.name: EZ-bar preacher curl
steps: Adjust a preacher bench so your armpits rest on top of the pad. Sit down and hold the EZ bar with an underhand grip on the angled grips, arms nearly straight.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms on the pad.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.
formCues: Upper arms stay on the pad

commonMistakes: Dropping the bar fast and locking out
safety: Do not fully lock the elbows at the bottom
Use a light weight

exercises.name: EZ-bar reverse curl
steps: Stand tall holding an EZ bar with an overhand grip on the angled grips, arms hanging straight and elbows by your sides.
Keeping your elbows pinned, curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use lighter weight than your normal curl

exercises.name: EZ-bar lying triceps extension
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar with an overhand grip on the inner angled grips, arms straight above your chest.
Keeping your upper arms still, bend your elbows to lower the bar towards your forehead or just behind your head.
Extend your elbows to return the bar to the start, squeezing your triceps.

commonMistakes: Letting the upper arms drift back
safety: Use a spotter on heavy sets
Do not lower the bar onto your head

exercises.name: EZ-bar overhead triceps extension
steps: Sit on an upright bench with back support, holding an EZ bar overhead with an overhand grip on the inner angled grips, arms straight.
Keeping your elbows pointing forward, bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head.
Extend your elbows to press the bar back up to straight arms.

safety: Use a light weight

exercises.name: EZ-bar close-grip bench press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar, feet flat and shoulder blades pulled back. Grip the EZ bar on the inner angled grips.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Press back up to straight arms, keeping your elbows tucked.

safety: Use a spotter or rack safeties

exercises.name: EZ-bar wide-grip curl
steps: Stand tall holding an EZ bar on the outer angled grips with an underhand grip, arms hanging straight.
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use a weight you can control

exercises.name: EZ-bar upright row
steps: Stand tall holding an EZ bar with an overhand grip on the inner grips in front of your thighs.
Lift the bar up along your body, leading with your elbows, until your elbows are about shoulder height.
Lower under control to the start.

commonMistakes: Pulling the elbows above the shoulders
safety: Keep the bar below chest height
Skip it if you have shoulder pain

exercises.name: Trap bar deadlift
steps: Stand inside the trap bar with your feet hip width apart and the bar around you, and the handles at your sides.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the handles, keeping your chest up and your back flat.
Drive through your whole foot to stand tall, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Lower the bar under control by hinging your hips back first, then bending the knees.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

commonMistakes: Jerking the bar off the floor
safety: Do not lift with a rounded back
Use collars

exercises.name: Trap bar deadlift (high handles)
steps: Stand inside the trap bar with the high handles facing up and your feet hip width apart.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the handles, chest up and back flat.
Drive through your whole foot to stand tall, then lower under control.

safety: Do not lift with a rounded back
metadata.reviewNote: A shorter range, easier on mobility.

exercises.name: Trap bar Romanian deadlift
steps: Stand inside the trap bar holding the handles at your sides, knees slightly bent.
Brace your core and push your hips back, letting the bar slide down your legs with a flat back.
Lower until you feel a hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand tall.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Stop if your back rounds

exercises.name: Trap bar shrug
steps: Stand inside the trap bar holding the handles at your sides with straight arms.
Keeping your arms straight, lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Use straps for heavy loads

exercises.name: Trap bar farmer's carry
steps: Stand inside the trap bar and hinge down to pick it up by the handles, keeping your back flat.
Stand tall, brace your core and walk with short, controlled steps for the set distance or time.
Set the bar down under control.

safety: Pick up and set down with a flat back
metadata.reviewNote: Counted by distance or time.

exercises.name: Trap bar jump
steps: Stand inside a lightly loaded trap bar with the handles at your sides, knees slightly bent.
Dip into a quarter squat, then jump as high as you can, driving through the floor.
Land softly with bent knees and reset.

safety: Use a light load
Skip it with knee, ankle or lower back problems

exercises.name: Plate front raise
steps: Stand tall holding a weight plate with both hands at the sides (at 3 and 9 o'clock), arms straight in front of your thighs.
Raise the plate in front of you to about shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower slowly.

safety: Use a light plate
Grip the plate firmly

exercises.name: Plate squeeze press
steps: Hold a weight plate between your palms at your chest, pressing your palms together hard.
Press the plate straight out in front of you until your arms are straight, squeezing your palms the entire time.
Bring it back to your chest under control.

safety: Use a light plate
Grip it firmly

exercises.name: Plate halo
steps: Stand tall holding a weight plate with both hands at chest height, close to your chin.
Keeping the plate close to your head and your torso still, circle it around your head slowly, passing it behind your neck and back to the front.
Reverse the direction after the planned reps.

safety: Use a light plate
Hold it firmly

exercises.name: Plate goblet squat
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width, holding a weight plate against your chest with both hands.
Brace your core and sit down and back, lowering until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.

safety: Hold the plate firmly

exercises.name: Plate Russian twist
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels on or just off the floor, leaning back slightly with a straight back. Hold a weight plate at your chest.
Brace your core and rotate your torso to one side, moving the plate towards the floor beside you.
Rotate to the other side. Each side counts as one rep.

safety: Use a light plate
Start without lifting your feet

exercises.name: Plate wood chop
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, holding a weight plate with both hands near one hip.
Brace your core and rotate your torso as you lift the plate diagonally across your body to above the opposite shoulder, pivoting on your feet.
Return under control. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Turn from the torso and hips

commonMistakes: Using a plate that is too heavy
safety: Use a light plate

exercises.name: Plate pinch hold
steps: Take a weight plate (or two smooth plates together) and pinch it between your fingers and thumb, with your arm straight by your side.
Stand tall and hold for the planned time, keeping your shoulder relaxed.
Set the plate down and switch hands.
formCues: Pinch with the fingers and thumb

safety: Do not drop the plate on your foot

exercises.name: Plate overhead triceps extension
steps: Stand or sit tall holding a weight plate by its sides with both hands, and press it overhead to straight arms.
Keeping your elbows pointing forward, bend your elbows to lower the plate behind your head.
Extend your elbows to press the plate back up.

safety: Use a light plate
Hold it firmly

exercises.name: Resistance band chest press
steps: Wrap a band around your back, under your armpits, holding an end in each hand (or anchor it behind you at chest height).
Stand with a split stance and your hands at your chest, elbows bent.
Press your hands straight forward until your arms are straight, then return slowly.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band chest fly
steps: Anchor a band at chest height behind you, or wrap it around your back. Hold an end in each hand with your arms out to the sides and a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide arc, squeezing your chest.
Return slowly under control.

commonMistakes: Bending the elbows into a press
safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band lat pulldown
steps: Anchor a band to a high point (a pull-up bar or door anchor) and kneel or sit facing it, holding the band with straight arms above you.
Pull the band down towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your lats, then return slowly.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band straight-arm pulldown
steps: Anchor a band high and stand facing it, holding the band with straight arms in front of you at head height.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, pull the band down to your thighs, squeezing your lats.
Return slowly.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band seated row
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and a band looped around your feet, holding an end in each hand with straight arms.
Sit tall and pull the band to your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band face pull
steps: Anchor a band at face height and hold an end in each hand with straight arms, then step back until the band is taut.
Pull the band towards your face, splitting your hands apart, with your elbows high.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return slowly.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band pull-apart
steps: Hold a band in front of you at shoulder height with straight arms, hands about shoulder width apart.
Pull the band apart by moving your hands out to the sides until your arms are in line with your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly under control.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band overhead press
steps: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet hip width apart, holding an end in each hand at shoulder height.
Brace your core and press your hands straight overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower under control to shoulder height.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band lateral raise
steps: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet hip width apart, holding an end in each hand at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides, leading with your elbows, until they are about level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band biceps curl
steps: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet hip width apart, holding an end in each hand with an underhand grip, arms by your sides.
Keeping your elbows pinned, curl your hands up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band triceps pushdown
steps: Anchor a band high and stand facing it, holding the band with your elbows pinned to your sides and your forearms at about 90°.
Press your hands down until your arms are straight.
Return slowly until your forearms are just past parallel.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band overhead triceps extension
steps: Stand on one end of the band and hold the other end behind your head with both hands, elbows pointing up.
Extend your elbows to press the band overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly behind your head.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band squat
steps: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet shoulder width apart, holding the ends at your shoulders.
Brace your core and sit down and back until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band deadlift
steps: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet hip width apart, holding the ends in front of your thighs.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back, lowering your hands towards your shins.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band pull-through
steps: Anchor a band low behind you and stand facing away from the anchor, straddling the band, holding it between your legs with both hands.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back while keeping a flat back and your knees slightly bent.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band glute kickback
steps: Place a band around your feet or ankles and get on your hands and knees, with your hands under your shoulders.
Brace your core and kick one leg back against the band, squeezing your glute.
Return slowly. Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.
formCues: Do not arch the lower back

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band standing leg curl
steps: Anchor a band low and loop the other end around one ankle, then stand facing the anchor, holding a support.
Curl your heel up towards your glute, keeping your thigh still.
Return slowly. Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set
Hold a support for balance

exercises.name: Resistance band Pallof press
steps: Anchor a band at chest height to a sturdy point and stand side-on to it, holding the band at your chest with both hands.
Brace your core and press the band straight out in front of you, resisting the pull to rotate.
Hold, then bring it back to your chest. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band shrug
steps: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet hip width apart, holding the ends at your sides with straight arms.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can, keeping your arms straight.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set

exercises.name: Resistance band external rotation
steps: Anchor a band at elbow height and stand side-on to it, with your elbow bent 90° and tucked against your side (use a rolled towel), holding the band across your body.
Keeping your elbow pinned, rotate your forearm outwards, away from your body, as far as is comfortable.
Return slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Rotate the forearm, not the body

safety: Anchor the band securely and check it for tears before each set
Use a light band
metadata.reviewNote: A rotator-cuff drill for shoulder health.

exercises.name: Band-assisted pull-up
steps: Loop a thick resistance band over a pull-up bar and place one knee or foot in the loop. Grip the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Pull your chest towards the bar by driving your elbows down and back, until your chin is over the bar.
Lower under control to straight arms.

safety: Check the band for tears
Use a thinner band as you get stronger

exercises.name: Band shoulder dislocate
steps: Stand holding a long resistance band (or a stick) in front of you with a wide overhand grip and straight arms.
Keeping your arms straight, lift the band overhead and behind you in an arc until it reaches your lower back, if your shoulders allow.
Reverse the movement back to the front. Narrow your grip only as your mobility improves.

safety: Stop if you feel pinching
Use a wide grip

exercises.name: Mini band lateral walk
steps: Place a mini band around your legs just above your knees (or around your ankles), and stand with your feet hip width apart in a quarter squat.
Step sideways with one foot, keeping tension on the band, and follow with the other foot without letting your feet come together.
Continue for the planned steps, then walk back the other way.
formCues: Stay low in a quarter squat

safety: Check the band for tears

exercises.name: Mini band monster walk
steps: Place a mini band around your legs just above your knees (or around your ankles), and stand with your feet hip width apart in a quarter squat.
Step diagonally forward and out with one foot, then the other, keeping tension on the band and your toes pointing forward.
Continue for the planned steps, then walk back.

safety: Check the band for tears

exercises.name: Mini band clamshell
steps: Lie on your side with a mini band around your legs just above your knees, and your hips and knees bent at about 45°, feet together.
Keeping your feet together, open your top knee up against the band without rolling your hips back.
Lower slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the band for tears

exercises.name: Mini band glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, hip width apart, and a mini band around your legs just above your knees.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips, pressing your knees out against the band.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.

safety: Check the band for tears

exercises.name: Mini band squat
steps: Place a mini band around your legs just above your knees and stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Sit down and back into a squat, pushing your knees out against the band, until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand.

safety: Check the band for tears

exercises.name: Mini band fire hydrant
steps: Start on your hands and knees with a mini band around your legs just above your knees.
Keeping your knee bent at 90°, lift one knee out to the side against the band, without rotating your torso.
Lower slowly. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Check the band for tears

exercises.name: Mini band seated hip abduction
steps: Sit on a bench or chair with a mini band around your legs just above your knees, feet flat and hip width apart.
Push your knees apart against the band, keeping your back tall.
Return slowly.

safety: Check the band for tears

exercises.name: Mini band hip thrust
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a mini band around your legs just above your knees, feet flat.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips, pressing your knees out against the band.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.

safety: Use a stable bench
Check the band for tears

exercises.name: Suspension trainer row
steps: Hold the handles with your palms facing each other and walk your feet forward until your body leans back at an angle, arms straight, body in a straight line.
Pull your chest up towards your hands by driving your elbows back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to straight arms, keeping your body in a straight line.

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length
Walk your feet back to make it easier

exercises.name: Suspension trainer chest press
steps: Face away from the anchor, holding the handles at chest height, and lean forward with your body in a straight line and your feet back.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest between your hands, keeping your body straight.
Press back up to straight arms.

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length
Step your feet closer to make it easier

exercises.name: Suspension trainer chest fly
steps: Face away from the anchor, holding the handles with your arms out in front of your chest at shoulder height and lean forward with a straight body.
Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until your hands are in line with your chest.
Squeeze your chest to bring your hands back together.

commonMistakes: Bending the elbows into a press
safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length
Stand more upright to make it easier

exercises.name: Suspension trainer rear delt fly
steps: Face the anchor holding the handles with straight arms in front of you, and lean back with your body in a straight line.
Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until they are in line with your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly.

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length

exercises.name: Suspension trainer biceps curl
steps: Face the anchor, holding the handles with your palms facing up and your arms straight in front of you, leaning back with a straight body.
Keeping your upper arms level with your shoulders, bend your elbows to bring your hands towards your head.
Lower slowly.

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length

exercises.name: Suspension trainer triceps extension
steps: Face away from the anchor, holding the handles at head height and lean forward with your arms overhead and your body in a straight line.
Bend your elbows to lower your head between your hands, keeping your upper arms still.
Extend your elbows to return to the start.

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length
Stand more upright to make it easier

exercises.name: Suspension trainer squat
steps: Stand facing the anchor holding the handles with straight arms in front of you, feet shoulder width apart.
Sit down and back into a squat, leaning back on the straps for balance, until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Drive up through your heels, using the straps only as much as you need.

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length

exercises.name: Suspension trainer reverse lunge
steps: Stand facing the anchor, holding the handles with straight arms in front of you, feet hip width apart.
Step one foot back into a lunge, lowering your back knee towards the floor, using the straps for balance.
Drive through your front foot to stand. Alternate legs.

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length

exercises.name: Suspension trainer hamstring curl
steps: Lie on your back with your heels in the foot cradles and your legs straight, hips lifted off the floor in a bridge.
Curl your heels towards your glutes, bending your knees, keeping your hips lifted.
Extend your legs slowly.

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length

exercises.name: Suspension trainer pike
steps: Place your feet in the foot cradles and get into a high plank with your hands on the floor, body in a straight line.
Keeping your legs straight, lift your hips up towards the ceiling, bringing your feet towards your hands.
Lower slowly back to the plank.
formCues: Hips up and over the shoulders

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length
Master the plank and the pike push-up first

exercises.name: Suspension trainer body saw
steps: Place your feet in the foot cradles and get into a forearm plank with your body in a straight line.
Brace your core and rock your body forward and back by moving your shoulders, in small controlled movements.
Keep your body straight throughout.

safety: Check that the straps are anchored securely to a strong point and set to the right length

exercises.name: Stability ball crunch
steps: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward until your lower back is supported on the ball and your feet are flat, hip width apart.
Place your hands lightly behind your head and curl your torso up by contracting your abs.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly back over the ball.
formCues: Curl the ribs towards the pelvis
Do not pull on the neck

safety: Use a ball that is the right size and not overinflated

exercises.name: Stability ball pike
steps: Place your shins or feet on a stability ball and get into a high plank with your hands on the floor.
Keeping your legs straight, lift your hips up towards the ceiling, rolling the ball towards your hands.
Roll the ball back to the plank slowly.
formCues: Hips up and over the shoulders

safety: Use a ball that is the right size and not overinflated
Master the plank first

exercises.name: Stability ball hamstring curl
steps: Lie on your back with your heels on a stability ball and your legs straight, hips lifted in a bridge.
Curl your heels towards your glutes, rolling the ball in, keeping your hips lifted.
Extend your legs slowly.

safety: Use a ball that is the right size and not overinflated

exercises.name: Stability ball push-up
steps: Place your hands on the ball (hands-on) or your shins on the ball (feet-on) and get into a plank with your body in a straight line.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest, keeping your body straight and the ball steady.
Press back up to straight arms.

safety: Use a ball that is the right size and not overinflated
Start with hands on the ball for an easier version

exercises.name: Stability ball wall squat
steps: Place a stability ball between your lower back and a wall, with your feet shoulder width apart and a little in front of you.
Bend your knees and sit down, rolling the ball down the wall until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Press through your heels to stand.

commonMistakes: Feet too close to the wall
safety: Use a ball that is the right size and not overinflated

exercises.name: Stability ball back extension
steps: Lie face down over a stability ball with your hips on the ball and your toes on the floor, hands behind your head or across your chest.
Keeping your back neutral, lower your torso over the ball, then lift it until your body is in a straight line.
Do not arch past a straight line.

safety: Use a ball that is the right size and not overinflated

exercises.name: Stability ball plank
steps: Place your forearms on a stability ball and walk your feet back until your body is in a straight line from head to heels.

exercises.name: Stability ball rollout

exercises.name: Stability ball glute bridge

exercises.name: Medicine ball slam
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, holding a slam ball (a dead-bounce medicine ball) with both hands at chest height.
Raise the ball overhead, rising onto your toes, then slam it down hard into the floor in front of you, bending your knees and hinging your hips.

exercises.name: Medicine ball chest pass

exercises.name: Medicine ball overhead throw
steps: Stand facing a sturdy wall about 6 feet away, holding a medicine ball overhead with both hands.
Step forward and throw the ball forcefully at the wall in an arc, following through with your arms.
Catch the ball on the bounce, and repeat.

exercises.name: Medicine ball rotational throw
steps: Stand side-on to a sturdy wall about 3–4 feet away, with your feet shoulder width apart and holding a medicine ball at your hip.
Rotate your hips and torso towards the wall, throwing the ball explosively against it.
Catch the ball as it returns, and repeat. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

safety: Use a ball that is safe to throw and catch, and a clear wall or partner

exercises.name: Medicine ball Russian twist
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels on or just off the floor, leaning back slightly with a straight back. Hold a medicine ball at your chest.

exercises.name: Wall ball
steps: Stand facing a wall about 1–2 feet away, holding a medicine ball at your chest with both hands.
Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up.
Drive up explosively and throw the ball at a target on the wall above you.
Catch the ball as it comes back and go straight into the next squat.

safety: Use a ball that is safe to throw and catch, and a clear wall or partner

exercises.name: Medicine ball squat to press

exercises.name: Medicine ball sit-up and throw
steps: Sit on the floor facing a wall (or partner) about 3 feet away, with your knees bent, feet flat and a medicine ball held to your chest.

safety: Use a ball that is safe to throw and catch, and a clear wall or partner

exercises.name: Battle rope alternating waves
steps: Anchor a battle rope and hold one end in each hand, stepping back until there is slight slack. Stand in a quarter squat with your core braced.

exercises.name: Battle rope double waves

exercises.name: Battle rope slams

exercises.name: Battle rope side-to-side waves
steps: Stand in a quarter squat holding the ends of the rope with both hands in front of you.

exercises.name: Battle rope jumping jacks

exercises.name: Skipping — basic jump
steps: Hold the handles of a skipping rope at hip height with your elbows close to your sides. Stand tall with the rope behind your feet.

exercises.name: Skipping — high knees

exercises.name: Skipping — double under
steps: Hold the rope as for the basic jump and stand tall.

exercises.name: Skipping — side-to-side hop

exercises.name: Sled push
steps: Load the sled and stand behind it, holding the handles with your arms straight or slightly bent, body leaning forward at about 45°.

exercises.name: Sled drag (backward)

exercises.name: Sled drag (forward)

safety: Use a sled and surface suited to each other, and keep the lane clear

exercises.name: Sled row
steps: Attach a rope to the sled and place a clear lane in front of you. Stand facing the sled, holding the rope with both hands, feet hip width apart.
Walk backwards and row the rope towards your lower ribs, pulling the sled towards you, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Walk the sled in with a hand-over-hand pull, keeping your torso upright.

exercises.name: Ab wheel rollout (kneeling)
steps: Kneel on a mat holding the ab wheel with both hands under your shoulders.
